0. EXACT SCOPE AND ROOT THEOREM

Space: T^3 = R^3/Z^3, with normalized Lebesgue measure.
Equation: unforced incompressible three-dimensional Navier--Stokes.
Parameters: nu > 0 and hbar > 0.
Initial data: arbitrary a in C^\infty_sigma(T^3; R^3).
Mean: arbitrary, retained and conserved.
Regularity endpoint: C^\infty through t = 0, on every finite time interval.
Fourier cutoffs: all integer N >= 1; the constant Fourier modes are retained.

ROOT THEOREM.

For every nu > 0 and hbar > 0:

(R1) Every standard real Fourier--Galerkin NSE system has a completely
specified canonical Hamiltonian lift and a selfadjoint Schroedinger
generator H_N on L^2(R^{d_N}, dq).

(R2) Its unitary evolution U_N(t) induces exactly the Galerkin NSE flow on
the commutative algebra of fluid observables, with deterministic data
reconstructed by characters or localized normalized wave packets.

(R3) The five precisely quantified propositions
  FB(nu), G_3(nu), LIP(nu), QREG(nu,hbar), QLIP(nu,hbar)
are equivalent. QREG uses the localized H^3-energy observable; QLIP
uses the time-integrated localized gradient-supremum observable.
Every localization limit is taken at fixed N before the cutoff supremum.

(R4) The finite models satisfy the explicit identities and bounds of:
  Round 1 / Section2.A: arbitrary-mean Galilean conjugacy;
  Round 2 / Section3.A: constant divergence and exact Jacobian;
  Round 3 / Section7.A: orthogonal basis and parameter covariance;
  Round 4 / Section8.4: quantitative packet localization;
  Round 6 / Section6: explicit nonreal resolvents, direct selfadjoint
    closure, maximal derivative/adjoint domains and quantitative core;
  Round 7 / Section8.5: reference-trajectory gradient stability.
Round 5 / Section14.A establishes the LIP/QLIP equivalences.
FiniteCutoffStrengthening denotes precisely these conclusions.

(R5) For every prescribed admissible profile family
  eta_N in C_c^infinity(B(0,1);C), ||eta_N||_2=1,
and positive radius family rho_N with
  w_N=(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(3/2),
  D=sup_{N>=1} w_N*rho_N < infinity,
the finite-width predicates of Section14.B satisfy
  G_3(nu) <=> QREG_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar)
          <=> QLIP_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar).
Their definitions contain no state-localization limit. Consequently all
seven classical and quantum criteria are equivalent.

The explicit data-independent radius
  epsilon_N=1/[(N+1)*(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(3/2)]
has D=1/2. The real radial normalized profiles in Section14.B supply a
fully specified admissible family. Under G_3, these states have the
quantitative observable errors of Section14.C and recover the H3-energy
and integrated-gradient observables of the unique smooth continuum NSE
solution as N tends to infinity. This is a conditional observable limit.

In symbols:

  forall nu>0, forall hbar>0:
    [forall N>=1: CanonicalQuantumLift(N,nu,hbar)
                   /\ ExactFluidObservableConjugacy(N,nu,hbar)

1. NOTATION AND THE PERIODIC ENDPOINT

1.1 Fourier and Sobolev conventions.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI01]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP01, CP02, CP03, CP17; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML01--ML05; MT02, MT07, MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD01, AD02, AD04.
  APPLICATION: Fourier normalization, Parseval, retained mean, and weighted coefficient norms.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


For k in Z^3,

  \widehat v(k) = \int_{T^3} v(x) exp(-2 pi i k.x) dx,

  ||v||_{H^s}^2
    = \sum_{k in Z^3} (1 + 4 pi^2 |k|^2)^s |\widehat v(k)|^2.

The subscript sigma denotes divergence-free real vector fields.
The pointwise spatial gradient norm is the Frobenius matrix norm;
||nabla v||_infinity is its spatial supremum. This norm dominates the
operator norm, so |(z.nabla)v|<=|z||nabla v|. The constants C_emb and C_m
throughout use this fixed convention.

For an integer m >= 0,

  ||v||_{H^m}^2
    = \sum_{|alpha| <= m}
        m! / ((m-|alpha|)! alpha!)
        ||D^alpha v||_2^2.                                      (1.1)

This equality follows by the multinomial expansion of
(1 + xi_1^2 + xi_2^2 + xi_3^2)^m.

1.2 Leray projection.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI02]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP02, CP03, CP04; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: MT02, MT03.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD01--AD04.
  APPLICATION: Modewise coefficientLeray and finite RHS; real-field realization remains explicit.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


For k != 0,

  \widehat{P v}(k)
    = (I - k k^T / |k|^2) \widehat v(k),

and \widehat{P v}(0) = \widehat v(0).

Set

  A = -Delta,
  B(v,w) = P((v.nabla)w),
  F_nu(u) = partial_t u + nu A u + B(u,u).

The operators A, P, all spatial derivatives, and all Fourier cutoffs
commute. P is orthogonal and contractive in every H^s.

1.3 FB(nu).

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI03]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP00, CP01, CP22, CP26; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: MT01.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD01, AD03, AD14.
  APPLICATION: Fefferman_B_0_adjust quantifies over all positive nu and mean-zero data; fixed-nu FB requires predicate transport.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


  FB(nu) :<=>
    forall a in C^\infty_sigma(T^3;R^3),
    exists u,p in C^\infty([0,infinity) x T^3):
      partial_t u + (u.nabla)u - nu Delta u + nabla p = 0,
      div u = 0,
      u(0) = a,
      \int_{T^3} p(t,x) dx = 0.

The pressure normalization fixes the gauge p -> p + c(t). Omitting that
normalization gives the same velocity statement. The endpoint retains
arbitrary initial mean and smoothness through t = 0.

This is the periodic unforced smoothness endpoint used throughout this
record; see [F] for the Fefferman formulation.

2. EXPLICIT FOURIER--GALERKIN DATA

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI04]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP02, CP03, CP04; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML01--ML05; MT02--MT07, MT20.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD01--AD04.
  APPLICATION: Plain complex Pi state is not the real L2 coordinate model. Energy isometry and RHS conjugacy are required.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Let Pi_N be the Fourier cutoff |k| <= N, acting on divergence-free fields.
Let

  V_N = Pi_N L^2_sigma(T^3;R^3),
  d_N = dim_R V_N.

Choose a real L^2-orthonormal Fourier eigenbasis
(e_{N,j})_{j=1}^{d_N}, including the constant modes:

  -Delta e_{N,j} = lambda_{N,j} e_{N,j},
  lambda_{N,j} >= 0.

For fixed N, suppress N in the indices and write

  I_N(q) = \sum_{j=1}^{d_N} q_j e_j,
  q in R^{d_N}.

Then

  ||I_N(q)||_2^2 = |q|^2,
  ||I_N(q)||_{H^s}^2 = \sum_j (1+lambda_j)^s q_j^2.       (2.1)

For every real s define the quadratic function
  e_{s,N}(q) = ||I_N(q)||_{H^s}^2.
Let A_N=diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_{d_N}) in this eigenbasis.


Define the exact interaction coefficients

  C_{jkl}
    = \int_{T^3} e_j . ((e_k.nabla)e_l) dx,                (2.2)

and the polynomial drift

  b_{N,j}(q)
    = -nu lambda_j q_j - \sum_{k,l} C_{jkl} q_k q_l.       (2.3)

Define the finite bilinear map, with the advecting argument first:
  (B_N(x,y))_j = sum_{k,l} C_{jkl} x_k y_l.
Then b_N(q)=-nu A_N q-B_N(q,q). This B_N is the coordinate realization
of Pi_N B(I_N(x),I_N(y)).


These coefficients are finite trigonometric integrals determined by the
chosen basis. No continuum NSE solution is used in their definition.

Periodic integration by parts gives

  C_{jkl} = -C_{lkj},                                     (2.4)

because div e_k = 0. Consequently,

  \sum_{j,k,l} C_{jkl} q_j q_k q_l = 0,

  q.b_N(q) = -nu \sum_j lambda_j q_j^2.                    (2.5)

For a in C^\infty_sigma, define

  a_N = I_N^{-1}(Pi_N a).

The coefficient equation

  dot q_N = b_N(q_N),
  q_N(0) = a_N                                             (2.6)

is equivalent to

  partial_t u_N + nu A u_N + Pi_N B(u_N,u_N) = 0,
  u_N(0) = Pi_N a,
  u_N = I_N(q_N).                                          (2.7)

For every constant basis vector e_j, lambda_j = 0 and
C_{jkl} = 0 by integration by parts. Hence the constant coordinates,
and therefore the spatial mean, are conserved.

2.A ROUND 1: ARBITRARY-MEAN GALILEAN CONJUGACY

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI05]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP26, CP28; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: MT01, MT02, MT09--MT11.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD01--AD04.
  APPLICATION: cutoffModes excludes zero; sobolevCutoffModes inserts zero. The Galilean adapter is proved in this section.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Let T_y v(x)=v(x+y), y in T^3. Let
  m = \int_{T^3} a(x) dx,
  a^0 = a-m,
  Pi_N^0 = Pi_N - Pi_0,
where Pi_0 is projection onto constant vector fields.

Mean conservation follows from integrating NSE or its Galerkin
projection:
  d/dt \int u dx=0.
Both Delta u and (u.nabla)u have zero spatial integral; the pressure is
periodic. Thus \bar u(t)=m.

For a smooth NSE solution, define
  v(y,t)=u(y+mt,t)-m,
  pi(y,t)=p(y+mt,t).

Then
  v_t = (u_t+m.nabla u)(y+mt,t),
  (v.nabla)v = ((u-m).nabla u)(y+mt,t),
  Delta v = (Delta u)(y+mt,t).
The two m.nabla u terms cancel. Therefore
  v_t+(v.nabla)v-nu Delta v+nabla pi=0,
  div v=0,
  \bar v=0,
  v(0)=a^0.
The inverse is
  u(x,t)=m+v(x-mt,t),
  p(x,t)=pi(x-mt,t).
Smoothness through t=0 is preserved in both directions.

Fourier form:
  \widehat{T_y f}(k)=exp(2 pi i k.y)\hat f(k).
Consequently T_y commutes with Pi_N, Pi_N^0, the Leray projector P,
A, and every spatial derivative. It also obeys
  T_y B(v,w)=B(T_y v,T_y w).
Moreover B(v,w) has zero mean whenever div v=0.

It follows, by the same chain rule and cancellation, that
  v_N(y,t)=u_N(y+mt,t)-m
is exactly the zero-mode-excluded Galerkin solution
  partial_t v_N+nu A v_N+Pi_N^0 B(v_N,v_N)=0,
  v_N(0)=Pi_N^0 a^0.
Conversely a solution of this equation determines the full Galerkin
solution by the inverse formula. No change to the nonlinear equation
or viscosity is made.

For every real Sobolev exponent s,
  ||u_N(t)||_{H^s}^2
    = |m|^2+||v_N(t)||_{H^s}^2,
because the constant mode is orthogonal to all nonzero modes and
translations preserve the Fourier weights. Also
  ||nabla u_N(t)||_infinity
    =||nabla v_N(t)||_infinity.

Definitions:
  FB_0(nu): the restriction of FB(nu) to mean-zero data and velocity;
  G_{3,0}(nu): the criterion (11.1) for Pi_N^0 and mean-zero data.

Therefore:
  FB(nu) <=> FB_0(nu),
  G_3(nu) <=> G_{3,0}(nu),
and the arbitrary-mean quantitative bound is recovered from the
mean-zero bound as
  C_full(nu,a,T)=|m|^2+C_zero(nu,a-m,T).

The quantum H^3 identity in Section 8 then yields the corresponding
QREG equivalence after localization. No equality of all finite-width
quantum ensembles with a fixed-mean ensemble is needed or asserted.

Coordinate identity:
Choose the three standard constant vector fields first, and write
q=(m,z). Let R_N(y) be the
orthogonal matrix of T_y on V_N^0, and let Phi_{N,0}^t be the mean-zero
Galerkin flow. Then
  Phi_N^t(m,z)
    =(m,R_N(-mt)Phi_{N,0}^t(z)).
This follows directly from the inverse Galilean transformation.
This proves the mathematical mean-mode adapter. Its later Lean realization
must also establish the real-coordinate and periodic-lift identifications
AD01--AD04; source endpoint MT09 alone does not supply those identifications.

3. COMPLETE GALERKIN FLOW

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI06]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP04, CP05, CP06; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML06--ML10; MT03--MT06, MT08, MT09, MT20.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD02, AD05.
  APPLICATION: MT09 gives forward existence/uniqueness. A two-sided smooth group and determinant formula require additional formal endpoints.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


The polynomial b_N is C^\infty and locally Lipschitz. Finite-dimensional
ODE local existence, uniqueness, smooth dependence, and the bounded-orbit
continuation criterion apply.

For every local solution q(t),

  (1/2) d|q(t)|^2/dt
    = -nu \sum_j lambda_j q_j(t)^2.                         (3.1)

For t >= 0,

  |q(t)| <= |q(0)|.                                         (3.2)

For r(s) = q(-s),

  d|r(s)|^2/ds
    = 2 nu \sum_j lambda_j r_j(s)^2
    <= 2 nu lambda_max,N |r(s)|^2.

Thus

  |q(-s)|^2
    <= exp(2 nu lambda_max,N s) |q(0)|^2
       for every finite s >= 0.                            (3.3)

The ODE continuation criterion excludes escape in finite positive or
negative time. Therefore

  Phi_N^t : R^{d_N} -> R^{d_N},  t in R,                    (3.4)

is a globally defined C^\infty flow, with

  Phi_N^0 = id,
  Phi_N^{t+s} = Phi_N^t o Phi_N^s,
  (Phi_N^t)^{-1} = Phi_N^{-t}.                              (3.5)

In particular every Phi_N^t is a smooth diffeomorphism.

Let

  J_N^t(q) = det D_q Phi_N^t(q).

The determinant differential equation yields

  J_N^t(q)
    = exp(\int_0^t div_q b_N(Phi_N^s(q)) ds) > 0.            (3.6)

All statements in this section are finite-dimensional. Their constants
may depend on N. No assertion about global smooth continuum NSE has
been used.

3.A ROUND 2: EXACT PHASE-SPACE DIVERGENCE AND JACOBIAN

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI07]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP07; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML01--ML03; MT02, MT03, MT05.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD02, AD04, AD05.
  APPLICATION: Constant diagonal projection kernel and div b=-nu Tr(A_N) are new bridge endpoints, not conclusions of energy cancellation alone.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Let
  K_N(x)=sum_{j=1}^{d_N} e_j(x) tensor e_j(x).

For a canonical real transverse Fourier basis, the two normalized
sine/cosine functions for a polarization p perpendicular to k contribute
  2 p tensor p [cos^2(2 pi k.x)+sin^2(2 pi k.x)]
    =2 p tensor p.
Thus K_N(x) is independent of x:
  K_N=I_3+sum_{0<|k|<=N}(I_3-k k^T/|k|^2).
The sum over an orthonormal basis defining K_N is unchanged by an
orthogonal change of basis, so this identity applies to every real
orthonormal Fourier eigenbasis of the same V_N.

Differentiate the polynomial drift:
  div_q b_N(q)
    =-nu sum_j lambda_j
     -sum_{j,l} C_{jjl}q_l
     -sum_{j,k} C_{jkj}q_k.

The last sum vanishes termwise:
  C_{jkj}=-C_{jkj}=0.

For fixed l,
  sum_j C_{jjl}
    =sum_{alpha,beta} integral
         K_{N,alpha beta} partial_beta e_{l,alpha} dx
    =0,
because K_N is constant and the integral of every periodic derivative
vanishes. Therefore
  div_q b_N(q)=-kappa_N,
  kappa_N=nu Tr(A_N)>=0.

For the full solenoidal ball cutoff, each nonzero pair {k,-k}
contributes four real transverse modes. Hence
  Tr(A_N)=2 sum_{0<|k|<=N} 4 pi^2 |k|^2,
  kappa_N=8 pi^2 nu sum_{0<|k|<=N}|k|^2.

The Jacobian formula (3.6) reduces to the exact closed expression
  J_N^t(q)=exp(-kappa_N t),
  t in R.

Thus
  (U_N(t)psi)(q)
    =exp(kappa_N t/2)psi(Phi_N^{-t}(q)),
  H_{N,min}
    =-i hbar [b_N.nabla_q-kappa_N/2].

The growing scalar factor in U_N is exactly compensated by contraction
of the configuration-space volume. The formulas agree with (4.6) and (5.1).
No bound on kappa_N uniform in N is asserted.

Coordinate interpretation:
  div of the finite Euler drift =0,
  div of the viscous drift =-nu Tr(A_N).
Energy skew cancellation alone would not imply this trace identity
for an arbitrary abstract coefficient tensor; the constant diagonal
Fourier projection kernel is the additional structural input.

4. COTANGENT HAMILTONIAN AND SYMMETRIC QUANTIZATION

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI08]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP08; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML15, ML19--ML26.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD06--AD09.
  APPLICATION: Construct the dense differential-operator domain before using unbounded adjoint and closure APIs.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


4.1 Classical canonical lift.

On T^*R^{d_N}, with canonical coordinates (q,pi), define

  mathscr H_N(q,pi) = \sum_j pi_j b_{N,j}(q).                (4.1)

Hamilton's equations are

  dot q_j = partial_{pi_j} mathscr H_N = b_{N,j}(q),

  dot pi_j
    = -partial_{q_j} mathscr H_N
    = -\sum_k pi_k partial_{q_j} b_{N,k}(q).                 (4.2)

Thus the q-equation is exactly (2.6). The auxiliary pi-equation is a
linear ODE along every q-trajectory and is defined on every finite time
interval.

The action

  S_N[q,pi]
    = \int pi . (dot q - b_N(q)) dt                         (4.3)

gives the same canonical system under compactly supported variations in t.

4.2 Quantum kinematics.

Set

  mathcal H_N = L^2(R^{d_N},dq;C),
  mathcal D_N = C_c^\infty(R^{d_N};C).

The Hilbert inner product is linear in the second argument.

On mathcal D_N, let

  Q_j = M_{q_j},
  P_j = -i hbar partial_{q_j}.

Then

  [Q_j,P_k] = i hbar delta_{jk} I,
  [Q_j,Q_k] = [P_j,P_k] = 0.                                (4.4)

4.3 Minimal symmetric Hamiltonian.

Define

  H_{N,min}
    = (1/2) \sum_j [P_j b_{N,j}(Q) + b_{N,j}(Q) P_j]
      on mathcal D_N.                                      (4.5)

In coordinates,

  H_{N,min}
    = -i hbar [b_N(q).nabla_q + (1/2) div_q b_N(q)].          (4.6)

By Section 3.A, div_q b_N=-kappa_N; hence the bracket equals
b_N.nabla_q-kappa_N/2.


Equivalently,

  H_{N,min}
    = -(nu/2) \sum_j lambda_j (P_j Q_j + Q_j P_j)
      -(1/2) \sum_{j,k,l} C_{jkl}
          (P_j Q_k Q_l + Q_k Q_l P_j).                      (4.7)

Thus viscosity gives quadratic canonical terms and advection gives
cubic canonical terms. Formula (4.7) is completely specified by the
NSE coefficients (2.2).

The generalized Koopman--von Neumann construction and this symmetric
canonical lift are described in [J]. Selfadjointness for the present
operators is proved directly in Sections 5--6.

5. THE EXPLICIT UNITARY GROUP

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI09]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP09; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML11--ML18.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD05--AD07.
  APPLICATION: Use Jacobian-weighted pullback. ML17--ML18 require measure preservation and do not directly implement viscous transport.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Define, for t in R,

  (U_N(t) psi)(q)
    = J_N^{-t}(q)^{1/2} psi(Phi_N^{-t}(q)).                  (5.1)

The explicit Fourier trace formula in Section 3.A gives equivalently
  (U_N(t)psi)(q)=exp(kappa_N t/2)psi(Phi_N^{-t}(q)).


5.1 Group property.

The Jacobian chain rule and (3.5) imply

  U_N(t+s) = U_N(t) U_N(s),
  U_N(0) = I.                                              (5.2)

5.2 Unitarity.

With q = Phi_N^t(y),

  ||U_N(t)psi||_2^2
    = \int J_N^{-t}(q) |psi(Phi_N^{-t}(q))|^2 dq
    = \int J_N^{-t}(Phi_N^t(y))
           |psi(y)|^2 J_N^t(y) dy
    = ||psi||_2^2.                                         (5.3)

Therefore

  U_N(t)^* = U_N(-t).                                      (5.4)

5.3 Invariant domain and strong continuity.

For psi in mathcal D_N,

  supp U_N(t)psi = Phi_N^t(supp psi).

For t in a compact interval, these supports lie in the compact image
of that interval times supp psi. Smoothness of Phi_N and J_N gives

  U_N(t) mathcal D_N = mathcal D_N,

  ||U_N(t)psi - psi||_2 -> 0 as t -> 0.                     (5.5)

Density of mathcal D_N and (5.3) extend strong continuity to all of
mathcal H_N.

Thus U_N is a strongly continuous unitary group. Section6 constructs
H_N=closure(H_{N,min}), proves H_N selfadjoint directly, and identifies
its exact strong derivative domain. The resulting evolution is denoted
  U_N(t)=exp(-i*t*H_N/hbar).                               (5.6)
The generator relation is proved before this notation is used. Section6.7
also identifies an independently defined spectral exponential.

6. ROUND 6: CONSTRUCTIVE RESOLVENTS AND THE EXACT GENERATOR DOMAIN

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI10]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP10; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML15, ML19--ML25, ML37--ML45.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD07.
  APPLICATION: Vectorwise Laplace resolvents, closed-graph limits, and a direct adjoint/range proof
               supply selfadjointness and the maximal strong generator domain.
  DETAILS: Section18; adapter contracts: Section19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no matching bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.

6.0. Exact premises and conventions

Fix one actual Galerkin cutoff N, viscosity ν>0 and parameter ħ>0. Set

  H = L²(R^{d_N},dq;C),    D = C_c^∞(R^{d_N};C),
  Tφ = -iħ [ b_N·∇φ + (div b_N)φ/2 ],    Dom(T)=D.

The Hilbert inner product is linear in its second argument. Thus the adjoint
convention is

  <Bx,y> = <x,B*y>,    x∈Dom(B), y∈Dom(B*).

The already proved inputs and the derived core identity are:

  (i) D is dense in H;
  (ii) the actual smooth Galerkin flow Φ_t exists for every real t;
  (iii) U(t)φ(q)=J_{-t}(q)^{1/2}φ(Φ_{-t}(q)) defines a strongly continuous
        unitary group on H;
  (iv) U(t)D=D;
  (v) T is symmetric on D;
  (vi) for φ∈D,

       dU(t)φ/dt = -(i/ħ) T U(t)φ                       (R6.1)

       in H, for every real t.

Derivation of (vi): for the actual drift, U(t)phi(q)=exp(kappa_N*t/2)
phi(Phi_{-t}(q)). Differentiation at fixed q gives
  partial_t U(t)phi(q)
    =(kappa_N/2)U(t)phi(q)
      -exp(kappa_N*t/2) b_N(Phi_{-t}(q)).nabla phi(Phi_{-t}(q)).
The flow identity Phi_{-t}(Phi_s(q))=Phi_s(Phi_{-t}(q)), differentiated
at s=0, gives D Phi_{-t}(q)b_N(q)=b_N(Phi_{-t}(q)). The spatial chain
rule therefore identifies the displayed derivative with
  -[b_N.nabla-kappa_N/2]U(t)phi=-(i/hbar)T U(t)phi.
For t in a compact neighborhood, the functions and their time derivatives
have a common compact spatial support and vary smoothly there. The
pointwise difference quotients converge uniformly on that compact set,
and hence in L2. This proves the strong derivative (R6.1); it is not an
additional analytic premise.

Local notation: H in this section denotes the Hilbert space, T the
minimal operator, and A its graph closure. At the conclusion H_N=A;
A_N continues to denote the finite viscous Laplacian matrix.

For the actual drift, div b_N=-κ_N and J_t=e^{-κ_Nt}; the argument below also
applies to the previously derived variable-Jacobian half-density formula.
Every derivative and integral below is a strong Hilbert-space derivative or
vector-valued Bochner integral unless a pointwise formula is explicitly stated.

6.1. Closability and the nonreal lower bound

Let φ_n∈D, φ_n→0 and Tφ_n→g in H. For ψ∈D, symmetry implies

  <ψ,g> = lim_n <ψ,Tφ_n> = lim_n <Tψ,φ_n> = 0.

Density of D gives g=0. Therefore the closure of graph(T) is the graph of a
densely defined closed operator A=closure(T). Its domain contains D. If
x,y∈Dom(A), choose graph-approximating sequences in D and pass to the limit in
the symmetry identity; hence A is symmetric and A⊆A*.

Let z∈C with β_z=|Im z|>0. For x∈Dom(A), symmetry makes <x,Ax> real, so

  Im <x,(A-z)x> = -(Im z)||x||².

Cauchy–Schwarz consequently gives

  ||(A-z)x|| ≥ β_z ||x||.                               (R6.2)

In particular A-z is injective. No selfadjointness premise occurs in this step.

Source routing: ML14; ML19--ML24. Closability is proved above before
using the graph-closure API.

6.2. Vectorwise resolvents in both half planes

Define σ_z=1 if Im z>0, and σ_z=-1 if Im z<0. For t≥0 set

  F_z(t)f = exp(σ_z i z t/ħ) U(σ_z t)f.

Define, for f∈H and T_0≥0,

  R_z f = (σ_z i/ħ) ∫_0^∞ F_z(t)f dt,
  R_{z,T_0} f = (σ_z i/ħ) ∫_0^{T_0} F_z(t)f dt.          (R6.3)

Thus the two branches are exactly

  Im z>0: R_z f = (i/ħ)∫_0^∞ exp(izt/ħ)U(t)f dt;
  Im z<0: R_z f = -(i/ħ)∫_0^∞ exp(-izt/ħ)U(-t)f dt.

For every f∈H, t↦F_z(t)f is strongly continuous and

  ||F_z(t)f|| = exp(-β_z t/ħ)||f||.                     (R6.4)

The scalar majorant is integrable, with tail integral

  ∫_{T_0}^∞ exp(-β_z t/ħ)dt
    = (ħ/β_z)exp(-β_z T_0/ħ).

Hence every integral in (R6.3) exists. Linearity of the integral and (R6.4)
construct bounded complex-linear operators satisfying

  ||R_z|| ≤ 1/β_z,
  ||R_{z,T_0}|| ≤ (1-exp(-β_z T_0/ħ))/β_z,
  ||R_z-R_{z,T_0}|| ≤ exp(-β_z T_0/ħ)/β_z.              (R6.5)

The operator-norm estimates follow by first proving the vector estimates for
every f and then taking a supremum. The integrand is the vector U(t)f. Strong
continuity of U does not provide the operator-norm measurability required to
replace (R6.3) by an operator-valued Bochner integral of U(t).

Source routing: ML37, ML38,
ML39, ML40, ML41.
The real exponential rate is a=-β_z/ħ<0. Integrals over Ioi 0 and [0,∞)
agree because Lebesgue singletons are null. Finite interval integrals are oriented
Lean interval integrals; T_0≥0 fixes their positive orientation.

6.3. Finite-time graph identity and the actual smooth compact core

For φ∈D, differentiate U(s)U(t)φ=U(t)U(s)φ at s=0. Since U(t) is bounded and
U(t)φ∈D, (R6.1) gives

  T U(t)φ = U(t)Tφ.                                    (R6.6)

Therefore t↦F_z(t)φ and t↦T F_z(t)φ are continuous in H, and

  dF_z(t)φ/dt = -(σ_z i/ħ)(T-z)F_z(t)φ.                (R6.7)

The graph-valued function

  t ↦ (F_z(t)φ, T F_z(t)φ)

takes values in graph(T)⊆graph(A). The latter is a closed linear subspace of
H×H, hence complete. Its finite-interval Bochner integral is again in graph(A).
Composing with the continuous coordinate projections identifies the two
components of that integral. The vector-valued fundamental theorem of calculus
applied to (R6.7) consequently gives

  R_{z,T_0}φ ∈ Dom(A),
  (A-z)R_{z,T_0}φ = φ-F_z(T_0)φ.                       (R6.8)

This graph argument justifies the domain before the unbounded operator is
passed through the integral.

For the actual smooth flow one obtains the stronger statement

  R_{z,T_0}φ ∈ D,
  (T-z)R_{z,T_0}φ = φ-F_z(T_0)φ.                       (R6.9)

Proof of the strengthened domain statement: if K=supp φ, every spatial support
for 0≤t≤T_0 is contained in

  K_{z,T_0}={ Φ_{σ_z t}(q) : t∈[0,T_0], q∈K }.

This is the continuous image of a compact set. The explicit half-density
integrand is jointly smooth in (t,q). On each compact spatial neighborhood all
its spatial derivatives are uniformly bounded for t∈[0,T_0]. Differentiation
under this finite-time integral therefore gives a smooth spatial function.
Its support is contained in K_{z,T_0}, so it belongs to C_c^∞. The pointwise
integral represents the Bochner integral in H: pairing with any χ∈H and applying
Fubini is justified by

  ∫_0^{T_0}∫ |χ(q)| |F_z(t)φ(q)| dq dt
    ≤ ||χ|| ∫_0^{T_0}||F_z(t)φ||dt <∞.

Consequently (R6.8) restricts to (R6.9). This is a proof about the actual common
core D; no independently chosen invariant test space is substituted.

Source routing: ML42 and ML43; ML24 for the
closed graph. The compact-support/differentiation-under-the-integral wrapper
in (R6.9) is a project lemma to be formalized. The graph route proves (R6.8)
without making that wrapper a prerequisite for selfadjointness.

6.4. Right and left inverses on the full Hilbert space

First fix φ∈D. By (R6.5), R_{z,T_0}φ→R_zφ as T_0→∞. Equations (R6.4) and
(R6.8) imply

  A R_{z,T_0}φ = z R_{z,T_0}φ + φ-F_z(T_0)φ
     → zR_zφ+φ.

Closedness of A yields R_zφ∈Dom(A) and (A-z)R_zφ=φ.

For f∈H choose φ_n∈D with φ_n→f. Boundedness of R_z gives R_zφ_n→R_zf, while
A R_zφ_n=zR_zφ_n+φ_n→zR_zf+f. A second application of closedness gives

  R_z f ∈ Dom(A),    (A-z)R_z f=f,    f∈H.             (R6.10)

For x∈Dom(A), both x and R_z(A-z)x lie in Dom(A), and (A-z) applied to their
difference is zero. Injectivity from (R6.2) proves

  R_z(A-z)x=x,    x∈Dom(A).                             (R6.11)

Thus A-z is bijective Dom(A)→H and R_z=(A-z)^(-1), for every nonreal z,
before any use of selfadjointness. Applying the same dense-domain limiting
argument to the bounded finite-time operators extends (R6.8) to every f∈H:

  R_{z,T_0}f∈Dom(A),
  (A-z)R_{z,T_0}f=f-F_z(T_0)f.                         (R6.12)

Source routing: ML15, ML24 and the sources of R6.2–R6.3. Required project
lemmas are closed-graph limit membership and the two inverse identities.

6.5. Direct selfadjointness from the two ranges

Fix nonreal z and v∈Dom(A*). Let

  w=R_z(A*-z)v ∈ Dom(A),    η=v-w.

Since A⊆A*, equation (R6.10) implies (A*-z)η=0. For u∈Dom(A), the adjoint
identity and the convention linear in the second argument give

  <η,(A-conj(z))u>
    = <A*η,u>-conj(z)<η,u>
    = <zη,u>-conj(z)<η,u>
    = 0.

The conjugate shift A-conj(z) is surjective by (R6.10), using the opposite
half-plane formula. Therefore η is orthogonal to all of H and η=0. It follows
that v=w∈Dom(A). Combined with A⊆A*, this proves

  A*=A,    H_N:=A=closure(H_{N,min}).                   (R6.13)

The proof is a direct adjoint-pairing/range argument. No general deficiency
criterion and no generic Stone generator are premises. In particular, the
deficiency subspaces ker(A*∓iα) are zero for every α>0, as an immediate
consequence of (R6.2) and (R6.13).

If B is any selfadjoint extension of T, closedness of B gives A⊆B. Reversal
under adjoints gives B=B*⊆A*=A, hence B=A. Therefore T is essentially
selfadjoint, with this unique selfadjoint extension.

Source routing: ML19–ML24; the range/adjoint argument is a new project lemma.
Only dense-domain adjoints are used. A fallback branch of a totalized adjoint
definition cannot substitute for the proved density premise.

6.6. Invariant exact domain and the strong derivative characterization

For x∈Dom(A), choose φ_n∈D with φ_n→x and Tφ_n→Ax. By (R6.6),

  U(t)φ_n→U(t)x,    T U(t)φ_n=U(t)Tφ_n→U(t)Ax.

Closedness gives U(t)x∈Dom(A) and A U(t)x=U(t)Ax. Applying the same statement
at -t establishes equality of domains:

  U(t)Dom(A)=Dom(A),    A U(t)x=U(t)Ax.                 (R6.14)

On D, integrate (R6.1) to obtain

  U(t)φ-φ=-(i/ħ)∫_0^t U(s)Tφ ds.

Pass to a graph-approximating sequence for x∈Dom(A). Unitarity bounds the
difference of the integrals by |t| ||Tφ_n-Ax||, so

  U(t)x-x=-(i/ħ)∫_0^t U(s)Ax ds.                      (R6.15)

The integrand is continuous. The fundamental theorem of calculus implies

  dU(t)x/dt=-(i/ħ)U(t)Ax=-(i/ħ)A U(t)x.               (R6.16)

Conversely, let x∈H and suppose g=lim_{t→0}(U(t)x-x)/t exists strongly. For
φ∈D the unitary pairing identity is

  <U(-t)φ,x>=<φ,U(t)x>.

Its derivative at zero, with the conjugate scalar in the first argument, is

  -(i/ħ)<Tφ,x>=<φ,g>,
  <Tφ,x>=<φ,iħg>.

Extend the last identity from D to Dom(A) by graph approximation. This is the
maximal-adjoint-domain condition x∈Dom(A*) and A*x=iħg. Equation (R6.13) gives

  Dom(A) = { x∈H : lim_{t→0}(U(t)x-x)/t exists in H },
  Ax = iħ lim_{t→0}(U(t)x-x)/t.                        (R6.17)

Thus the exact strong generator is -(i/ħ)A. No hidden extension of the
Hamiltonian domain is introduced.

The maximal weak-domain characterization is exact as well. A vector x belongs
to Dom(T*) precisely when there exists y∈H such that

  <Tφ,x>=<φ,y>    for every φ∈D.

The identity extends by graph approximation to every φ∈Dom(A), so T*⊆A*.
The reverse inclusion follows from T⊆A. Consequently T*=A*=A. In particular, (R6.2) gives
  forall z in C with Im z!=0: ker(T*-z Id)={0}.
Moreover,

  Dom(A)={x∈H : ∃y∈H, ∀φ∈D, <Tφ,x>=<φ,y>},
  Ax=y for the unique such y.                           (R6.17a)

This maximal weak domain, the graph-closure domain and the strong-derivative
domain in (R6.17) coincide. No additional pointwise differentiability of x is
assumed.

Source routing: ML24, ML43, ML44, ML19–ML21. New project
lemmas: graphwise domain invariance, the integral identity, and the maximal
strong-derivative-domain equivalence.

6.7. Uniqueness of Schrödinger evolution and spectral notation

For x∈Dom(A), t↦U(t)x is a strong solution of

  iħ ψ'(t)=Aψ(t),    ψ(0)=x.

For any two strong solutions on the same interval with identical initial
value, their difference w satisfies w'=-(i/ħ)Aw. Since <w,Aw> is real,

  d||w||²/dt=2 Re <w,-(i/ħ)Aw>=0.

The initial value gives w=0. Hence (R6.16) is the unique strong Schrödinger
evolution on Dom(A).

If exp(-itA/ħ) is independently defined by the selfadjoint spectral calculus,
its identification with U(t) is a subsequent characterization, not a premise
for (R6.13). Indeed, with spectral measure E_A and
μ_x(B)=<x,E_A(B)x>, the domain condition is ∫λ² dμ_x(λ)<∞. For x∈Dom(A),

  |(exp(-itλ/ħ)-1)/t| ≤ |λ|/ħ

and dominated convergence in the spectral norm prove that this spectral
unitary evolution preserves Dom(A) and has derivative -(i/ħ)A at zero.
The group law yields the derivative at all t. Strong uniqueness gives

  U(t)x=exp(-itA/ħ)x    for x∈Dom(A),

and density plus boundedness extends the equality to every x∈H. Thus the
standard spectral interpretation is mathematically valid. A future Lean
root using an independently defined spectral exponential must prove or cite
this specific characterization. The resolvent construction alone does not
certify availability of the spectral-calculus API.

6.8. Resolvent adjoint, identity and norm differentiability

For f,g∈H set u=R_zf and v=R_conj(z)g. Equations (R6.10)–(R6.13) give

  <R_zf,g>
    = <u,(A-conj(z))v>
    = <(A-z)u,v>
    = <f,R_conj(z)g>.

Therefore

  R_z*=R_conj(z).                                      (R6.18)

For arbitrary nonreal z,w, equation (R6.11) applied to R_wf yields

  R_wf = R_z(A-z)R_wf
        = R_zf+(w-z)R_zR_wf.

Consequently

  R_z-R_w=(z-w)R_zR_w,
  R_zR_w=R_wR_z,
  ||R_z-R_w|| ≤ |z-w|/(β_zβ_w).                        (R6.19)

Commutativity follows by interchanging z,w when z≠w, and is tautological when
z=w. The estimate proves norm continuity locally on C\R. Dividing the identity
by a nonzero complex increment δ and taking δ→0 gives

  dR_z/dz=R_z²                                        (R6.20)

in bounded-operator norm on each half-plane. No finite-dimensional matrix
resolvent is substituted for this unbounded Hamiltonian resolvent.

6.9. Quantitative graph approximation by the actual core

Define ||x||_A=||x||+||Ax|| on Dom(A), and

  C_z=1+(1+|z|)/β_z.

Equation (R6.10) gives

  ||R_zf||_A ≤ C_z ||f||.

From (R6.10) and (R6.12),

  A(R_z-R_{z,T_0})f
    =z(R_z-R_{z,T_0})f+F_z(T_0)f.

Together with (R6.4)–(R6.5), this proves

  ||R_zf-R_{z,T_0}f||_A
    ≤ C_z exp(-β_z T_0/ħ)||f||.                        (R6.21)

For x∈Dom(A), set f=(A-z)x. Choose f_n∈D with f_n→f, and choose T_n≥0 with
T_n→∞. The actual test functions

  x_n=R_{z,T_n}f_n ∈ D

obey, using R_zf=x,

  ||x_n-x||_A
    ≤ C_z [ ||f_n-f||+exp(-β_z T_n/ħ)||f_n|| ] →0.      (R6.22)

The sequence f_n is bounded because it converges. Equation (R6.22) therefore
constructs explicit graph-core approximants with a quantified time-truncation
error. Independently, A=closure(T) already gives the abstract core conclusion

  Dom(T)=D is a core of A.                             (R6.23)

Source routing: ML45, ML15 and R6.2–R6.4 sources. The cached
declaration LinearPMap.closureHasCore provides the exact abstract core wrapper;
(R6.22) supplies additional model-specific quantitative information.

7. EXACT HEISENBERG NSE AND OBSERVABLE DOMAINS

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI11]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP11; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML11--ML14, ML19--ML26.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD07, AD08.
  APPLICATION: Multiplier selfadjointness, maximal domains, and equality under conjugation require domain-aware bridge theorems.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


For a measurable real function f on R^{d_N}, M_f denotes the
selfadjoint multiplication operator on its maximal domain

  D(M_f) = {psi in mathcal H_N: f psi in mathcal H_N}.

A direct substitution into (5.1) gives

  U_N(t)^* M_f U_N(t)
    = M_{f o Phi_N^t}.                                     (7.1)

This is equality of operators with equality of domains:

  {psi: U_N(t)psi in D(M_f)}
    = D(M_{f o Phi_N^t}).                                  (7.2)

For smooth f, multiplication preserves mathcal D_N and

  [H_{N,min},M_f]
    = -i hbar M_{b_N.nabla_q f}

on mathcal D_N. Therefore

  (i/hbar)[H_{N,min},M_f]
    = M_{b_N.nabla_q f}.                                   (7.3)

In particular,

  (i/hbar)[H_{N,min},Q_j] = b_{N,j}(Q).                      (7.4)

Set

  Q_j(t)
    = U_N(t)^* Q_j U_N(t)
    = M_{Phi_{N,j}^t(q)}.

Differentiation on mathcal D_N yields

  dQ_j(t)/dt
    = -nu lambda_j Q_j(t)
      -\sum_{k,l} C_{jkl} Q_k(t)Q_l(t).                    (7.5)

Every product and differential identity in (7.3)--(7.5) is asserted
on the common invariant domain mathcal D_N.

For

  widehat u_N(x,t) = \sum_j e_j(x) Q_j(t),

equation (7.5) is exactly

  partial_t widehat u_N - nu Delta widehat u_N
    + Pi_N P((widehat u_N.nabla)widehat u_N) = 0,

  div widehat u_N = 0.                                     (7.6)

All Q_j(t) are multiplication operators. Their spectral projections
commute, including at different times:

  [Q_j(t),Q_k(s)] = 0
  on mathcal D_N, for all j,k,t,s.                          (7.7)

Thus the fluid-observable sector is commutative. The auxiliary canonical
pairs (Q_j,P_j) supply the noncommutative quantum structure.

7.A ROUND 3: BASIS COVARIANCE AND PARAMETER NORMALIZATION

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI12]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP14, CP28; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML11--ML16, ML24--ML26; MT02, MT03.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD02, AD09.
  APPLICATION: Orthogonal realification, unitary dilation, and closure transport are separate from source Fourier existence.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


7.A.1 Orthogonal basis covariance.

Let q=O r with O^T O=I, and define the new coordinate realization
  I'_N(r)=I_N(O r).
Then
  b'_N(r)=O^T b_N(O r),
  A'_N=O^T A_N O,
  Phi_N'^t(r)=O^T Phi_N^t(O r).

Define
  (W_O psi)(r)=psi(O r).
Since |det O|=1, W_O is unitary. The chain rule gives, on C_c^\infty,
  H'_{N,min}=W_O H_{N,min} W_O^{-1}.
Unitary conjugation commutes with operator closure, so
  H'_N=W_O H_N W_O^{-1},
  U'_N(t)=W_O U_N(t) W_O^{-1}.
For every multiplication observable,
  W_O M_f W_O^{-1}=M_{f o O}.

The H^s energy is
  e_{s,N}(q)=q^T(I+A_N)^s q.
Its transformed value is
  e'_{s,N}(r)=e_{s,N}(O r).
For eigenbases, the same identity follows directly from the scalar
Fourier weights; no matrix fractional-power formalization is required.

Characters transform by a'_N=O^T a_N. Packet profiles can be chosen
as eta'_N(r)=eta_N(O r), in which case the packet transform is exact.
The localized limits are profile-independent in any case.

Therefore the canonical model and QREG are invariant under real
orthonormal changes of Galerkin coordinates. This permits a convenient
mode-by-mode basis for proofs and later transport to another Lean
basis representation.

7.A.2 Viscosity normalization.

Write b_{nu,N}(q)=-nu A_N q-B_N(q,q). Bilinearity gives
  b_{nu,N}(nu r)=nu^2 b_{1,N}(r).

Consequently
  Phi_{nu,N}^t(q)
    =nu Phi_{1,N}^{nu t}(q/nu).                         (V1)
Indeed the right side has derivative b_{nu,N} and initial value q;
finite-dimensional uniqueness applies.

Let
  (D_nu psi)(r)=nu^{d_N/2}psi(nu r).
This is unitary from the q-coordinate L^2 space to the r-coordinate
L^2 space. On C_c^\infty, substitution and the chain rule give
  D_nu H_{nu,N}^{hbar} D_nu^{-1}
    =nu H_{1,N}^{hbar}.
After closure,
  D_nu U_{nu,N}(t)D_nu^{-1}
    =U_{1,N}(nu t).                                    (V2)

For every s,
  D_nu M_{e_{s,N}}D_nu^{-1}
    =nu^2 M_{e_{s,N}}.                                 (V3)

With the same packet profile eta_N,
  D_nu Psi_{N,a,epsilon}
    =Psi_{N,a/nu,epsilon/nu}.                           (V4)

Notation for the packets defined in Section 8.2:
  Q^{(s)}_{nu,N,a,epsilon}(t)
    = <U_{nu,N}(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon},
         M_{e_{s,N}}U_{nu,N}(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon}>.
Here a denotes physical initial data and its center is
I_N^{-1}(Pi_N a); replacing a by a/nu divides that center by nu.
The same notation is valid for every real s at fixed N.

Therefore the exact quantum expectation identity is
  Q^{(s)}_{nu,N,a,epsilon}(t)
    =nu^2 Q^{(s)}_{1,N,a/nu,epsilon/nu}(nu t).           (V5)

In particular
  QREG(nu,hbar)<=>QREG(1,hbar).
The equivalence uses the bijection (a,T)<->(a/nu,nu T);
it does not require a bound uniform in nu.

Together with the hbar cancellation proved in Section 15.1,
  H_{nu,N}^{hbar}=hbar H_{nu,N}^1,
  U_{nu,N}^{hbar}(t)=U_{nu,N}^1(t),
all positive nu and hbar are recovered from the normalized finite
models nu=hbar=1 by explicit transformations.

The continuum scaling is
  u_nu(x,t)=nu u_1(x,nu t),
  p_nu(x,t)=nu^2 p_1(x,nu t),
  a_nu=nu a_1.
Thus FB(nu)<=>FB(1), with arbitrary conserved means preserved by the
same scaling.

Consequences:
  QREG(nu,hbar) <=> QREG(1,1),
  QLIP(nu,hbar) <=> QLIP(1,1),
  FB(nu) <=> FB(1).
For QLIP, ell_N(nu q)=nu ell_N(q) and the substitution tau=nu t
give equality of the corresponding integrated deterministic observables.
The packet relation (V4), followed by localization, yields its quantum
counterpart. The bound is permitted to depend on viscosity.

8. DETERMINISTIC RECONSTRUCTION AND LOCALIZED STATES

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI13]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP12, CP13; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML10--ML15, ML31--ML36.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD08, AD10.
  APPLICATION: Character identification, normalized packets, compact-support domain membership, and fixed-cutoff limit order.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


8.1 Characters.

Let

  mathfrak A_N = C_0(R^{d_N})

with its faithful multiplication representation on mathcal H_N.

Since Phi_N^t is a homeomorphism, pullback defines a C^*-automorphism

  alpha_N^t(f) = f o Phi_N^t.

Every q in R^{d_N} defines a character

  chi_q(f) = f(q).

Then

  chi_q o alpha_N^t = chi_{Phi_N^t(q)}.                     (8.1)

Characters of C_0(R^{d_N}) are precisely point evaluations. Therefore
(8.1) gives a bijection between Galerkin coefficient trajectories and
the induced character trajectories.

Point evaluation is not an ordinary normalized position eigenvector
in L^2(R^{d_N}). No identification of all quantum states with deterministic
fluid data is asserted.

8.2 Normalized wave packets.

For every N, fix any

  eta_N in C_c^\infty(B(0,1);C),
  ||eta_N||_2 = 1.

For epsilon > 0 and a_N = I_N^{-1}(Pi_N a), set

  Psi_{N,a,epsilon}(q)
    = epsilon^{-d_N/2}
      eta_N((q-a_N)/epsilon).                              (8.2)

Then

  Psi_{N,a,epsilon} in mathcal D_N,
  ||Psi_{N,a,epsilon}||_2 = 1,
  supp Psi_{N,a,epsilon} subset B(a_N,epsilon).

For continuous real f,

  <U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon},
     M_f U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon}>
    = \int f(Phi_N^t(q)) |Psi_{N,a,epsilon}(q)|^2 dq.        (8.3)

For each fixed N and finite T, all relevant supports for
|t| <= T and 0 < epsilon <= 1 lie in a compact set. Uniform continuity
therefore gives

  sup_{|t|<=T}
  |<U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon},
       M_f U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon}>
       - f(Phi_N^t(a_N))|
    -> 0 as epsilon -> 0.                                  (8.4)

For such packets, every smooth multiplication observable is defined on
the evolved state because its support remains compact.

8.3 Exact H^3 observable.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI14]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP16, CP27; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML03, ML05; MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD02, AD04, AD08, AD10.
  APPLICATION: Match the exact (1+4*pi^2*|k|^2)^3 weight and then the maximal multiplication operator.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Define

  e_{3,N}(q)
    = ||I_N(q)||_{H^3}^2
    = \sum_j (1+lambda_j)^3 q_j^2,

  mathcal E_{3,N} = M_{e_{3,N}} >= 0.                       (8.5)

Equations (8.3)--(8.4) give

  lim_{epsilon->0}
  <U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon},
     mathcal E_{3,N} U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon}>
    = ||u_N^a(t)||_{H^3}^2.                                (8.6)

This limit is independent of the chosen family eta_N. Its convergence
is uniform on compact time intervals for each fixed N. No uniformity
in N is claimed.

8.4 ROUND 4: EXPLICIT FINITE-CUTOFF STABILITY AND PACKET ERROR

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI15]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP13; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML09--ML14; MT05, MT06.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD02, AD08, AD10.
  APPLICATION: Scalar energy Gronwall supplies the finite-N estimate; no cutoff-independent beta_N or Gamma_N is inferred.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Let
  beta_N=(sum_{j,k,l}|C_{jkl}|^2)^{1/2}.
Then Cauchy--Schwarz gives
  |B_N(x,y)|<=beta_N |x||y|.

Let q(t)=Phi_N^t(q_0), r(t)=Phi_N^t(r_0), z=q-r.
The exact difference equation is
  dot z=-nu A_Nz-B_N(z,q)-B_N(r,z).

Skew cancellation gives
  <z,B_N(r,z)>=0.
Therefore
  (1/2)d|z|^2/dt+nu<A_Nz,z>
    =-<z,B_N(z,q)>
    <=beta_N |q| |z|^2.

If |q_0|,|r_0|<=R, forward energy gives |q(t)|,|r(t)|<=R,
and Gronwall yields
  |Phi_N^t(q_0)-Phi_N^t(r_0)|
    <=exp(beta_N R t)|q_0-r_0|,
  t>=0.                                                  (P1)

The viscous term has been kept with its favorable sign; no additive
nu lambda_max term is needed in (P1).

For s>=0, write
  Lambda_{s,N}=(1+lambda_max,N)^s,
  e_{s,N}(q)=sum_j(1+lambda_j)^s q_j^2.

On the radius-R ball,
  |e_{s,N}(q)-e_{s,N}(r)|
    <=Lambda_{s,N}(|q|+|r|)|q-r|
    <=2R Lambda_{s,N}|q-r|.                              (P2)

Let a_N be fixed, set R=|a_N|+1, and take 0<epsilon<=1.
Every normalized packet supported in B(a_N,epsilon) satisfies, for
every finite T>=0,
  sup_{0<=t<=T}
  |<U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon},
      M_{e_{s,N}}U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon}>
     -e_{s,N}(Phi_N^t(a_N))|
    <=2R Lambda_{s,N} exp(beta_N R T) epsilon.            (P3)

Proof: combine (P1)--(P2) pointwise for initial q in packet support
and r_0=a_N, then integrate against the unit-mass density |Psi|^2.

For the gradient observable
  ell_N(q)=||nabla I_N(q)||_infinity,
define
  Gamma_N=(sum_j ||nabla e_j||_infinity^2)^{1/2}.
The triangle inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
  |ell_N(q)-ell_N(r)|<=Gamma_N |q-r|.

Consequently
  sup_{0<=t<=T}
  |<U_N(t)Psi,M_{ell_N}U_N(t)Psi>
      -ell_N(Phi_N^t(a_N))|
    <=Gamma_N exp(beta_N R T)epsilon,                    (P4)
and the corresponding integrated error is at most
  T Gamma_N exp(beta_N R T)epsilon.                      (P5)

In (P3)--(P5), the quantum inner products use maximal multiplication
domains. The evolved packet has compact support; e_{s,N} and ell_N are
continuous, so each displayed expectation is finite and well-defined.

All constants are explicitly determined by finite coefficients and
the basis. They may grow with N. This is a quantitative localization
result, not cutoff-uniform regularity.

8.5 ROUND 7: REFERENCE-TRAJECTORY GRADIENT STABILITY

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI33]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP32; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML05, ML09; MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD04, AD10, AD15.
  APPLICATION: Full bilinear skew cancellation, a continuous-coefficient integrating factor, and the
               exact finite spectral weight.
  DETAILS: Section18; adapter contracts: Section19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no matching bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.

For this section, E_N=R^{d_N} is the real coefficient space,
w_N=(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(3/2), and ell_N(q)=||nabla I_N(q)||_infinity.
The Frobenius spatial-gradient convention of Section1 is fixed.

THEOREM [P6: REFERENCE_GRADIENT_STABILITY].
For every q_0,r_0 in E_N and t >= 0,

  |Phi_N^t(q_0)-Phi_N^t(r_0)|
    <= |q_0-r_0| exp(integral_0^t ell_N(Phi_N^s(r_0)) ds).

The exponent depends only on the reference trajectory r. In particular,
there is no beta_N coefficient and no additional viscosity term.

DERIVATION.
Let q(t)=Phi_N^t(q_0), r(t)=Phi_N^t(r_0), z(t)=q(t)-r(t).
Bilinearity gives the exact identity

  B_N(q,q)-B_N(r,r) = B_N(z,r)+B_N(q,z).

Thus

  dot z = -nu A_N z-B_N(z,r)-B_N(q,z).

The full fixed-advecting skew identity of CP04 gives

  <z,B_N(q,z)> = 0.

The physical/Fourier isometry and orthogonality of the Galerkin/Leray
projections give

  <z,B_N(z,r)>
    = integral_T^3 I_N(z).((I_N(z).nabla)I_N(r)) dx.

Consequently,

  |<z,B_N(z,r)>|
    <= ell_N(r) integral_T^3 |I_N(z)|^2 dx
    = ell_N(r) |z|^2,

and

  (1/2) d|z|^2/dt + nu <A_N z,z>
    <= ell_N(r(t)) |z|^2.                                  (P6a)

Set I_r(t)=integral_0^t ell_N(r(s))ds. Continuity of ell_N and the
finite smooth flow imply I_r is continuously differentiable, with
I_r'(t)=ell_N(r(t)). Since A_N is nonnegative,

  d[exp(-2 I_r(t)) |z(t)|^2]/dt <= 0.

Evaluation at 0, followed by the nonnegative square root, proves P6.
The argument includes the case z(0)=0 without division by |z|.
It also applies when q_0 and r_0 have different spatial means.

THEOREM [P7: SPECTRAL_UPGRADE_OF_REFERENCE_STABILITY].
For all v in E_N,

  ||I_N(v)||_{H^3}^2
    = sum_j (1+lambda_j)^3 v_j^2
    <= (1+4*pi^2*N^2)^3 |v|^2.

Therefore,

  ||I_N(Phi_N^t(q_0)-Phi_N^t(r_0))||_{H^3}
    <= w_N |q_0-r_0| exp(I_r(t)).                           (P7)

This is a finite-cutoff inequality with an explicit spectral factor.
No cutoff-independent L2-to-H3 embedding is asserted.


9. ENERGY AND AN EXACT SQUEEZING SECTOR

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI16]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP15; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML06, ML08, ML09, ML14; MT05--MT08.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD02, AD07--AD09.
  APPLICATION: Source energy equals ||u||_2^2; Section 9 uses E_0=||u||_2^2/2. Preserve the factor two.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


9.1 Energy commutator.

Let E_0(q) = |q|^2/2. By (2.5) and (7.3),

  (i/hbar)[H_{N,min},M_{E_0}]
    = -nu M_{\sum_j lambda_j q_j^2} <= 0                   (9.1)

as a quadratic-form identity on mathcal D_N.

For psi_0 in mathcal D_N and psi(t)=U_N(t)psi_0,

  d<psi(t),M_{E_0}psi(t)>/dt
    = -nu <psi(t),M_{\sum_j lambda_j q_j^2}psi(t)>.          (9.2)

The conserved Hamiltonian expectation and the dissipating fluid energy
are distinct observables.

9.2 Single shear mode.

Fix k in Z\{0} and

  e(x) = sqrt(2) e_1 sin(2 pi k x_2).

Then ||e||_2=1, div e=0, and (e.nabla)e=0.

For u(x,t)=q(t)e(x),

  dot q = -gamma q,
  gamma = 4 pi^2 nu k^2.

The derived quantum Hamiltonian is

  H_gamma = -(gamma/2)(Q P + P Q),                          (9.3)

with evolution

  (U_gamma(t)psi)(q)
    = exp(gamma t/2) psi(exp(gamma t)q).

Consequently,

  Q(t) = exp(-gamma t) Q,
  P(t) = exp(gamma t) P,

  [Q(t),P(t)] = i hbar I.                                  (9.4)

Thus viscous contraction of this fluid amplitude is exactly represented
by canonical squeezing of the enlarged pair (Q,P).

10. ANALYTIC LEMMAS FOR THE CONTINUUM EQUIVALENCE

All constants below may depend on the displayed Sobolev index and the
fixed torus. They are independent of N.

10.1 Fourier projection properties.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI17]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP17; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML01--ML05; MT10, MT11.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD01, AD04, AD11.
  APPLICATION: MT11 gives an adjacent-order integer Sobolev tail and compact inclusion; (10.2) has a sharper displayed weight and arbitrary nonnegative gap.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


For r >= 0,

  ||Pi_N v||_{H^r} <= ||v||_{H^r}.                          (10.1)

For s >= 0,

  ||(I-Pi_N)v||_{H^r}
    <= (1+4 pi^2 N^2)^{-s/2} ||v||_{H^{r+s}}.              (10.2)

Equation (10.2) follows term by term from |k|>N in the Fourier sum.

10.2 Sobolev product and embedding estimates.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI18]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP18; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML29, ML30; MT10, MT11.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11.
  APPLICATION: ML29 is Euclidean compact-support Sobolev; ML30 is Euclidean distributional Sobolev. Neither is the exact periodic product/embedding theorem.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


For each integer m >= 2,

  ||v w||_{H^m}
    <= C_m ||v||_{H^m} ||w||_{H^m},

  ||B(v,w)||_{H^m}
    <= C_m ||v||_{H^m} ||w||_{H^{m+1}}.                    (10.3)

Also,

  ||nabla v||_infinity <= C_emb ||v||_{H^3}.                (10.4)

These are the standard periodic Sobolev algebra and embedding inequalities:
m>3/2 for the algebra, and 3>1+3/2 for (10.4). Multiplication estimates
follow from the Leibniz rule, Holder, and Sobolev embeddings; P is
contractive in H^m.

10.3 Tame energy inequality: derivation.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI19]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP18, CP19; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML29; MT05.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11.
  APPLICATION: Higher-order periodic Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation and tame commutators require exact new endpoints.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


For every integer m >= 1 and every smooth divergence-free v,

  |<v,B(v,v)>_{H^m}|
    <= C_m ||nabla v||_infinity ||v||_{H^m}^2.              (10.5)

Proof.

For a multi-index alpha,

  D^alpha((v.nabla)v)
    = v.nabla D^alpha v
      + \sum_{0<beta<=alpha} binom(alpha,beta)
          (D^beta v).nabla D^{alpha-beta}v.

The transport contribution vanishes:

  \int D^alpha v . (v.nabla D^alpha v) dx
    = (1/2)\int v.nabla|D^alpha v|^2 dx = 0.

Write ell=|alpha|, w=nabla v,
j=|beta|-1, and l=ell-|beta|. Then j+l=ell-1.

For ell>=2, periodic Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation gives, for
0<=j<=ell-1,

  ||D^j w||_{L^{2(ell-1)/j}}
    <= C_ell ||w||_infinity^{1-j/(ell-1)}
               ||w||_{H^{ell-1}}^{j/(ell-1)},              (10.6)

where j=0 means L^infinity. The analogous bound holds for l.
Their reciprocal exponents sum to 1/2. Holder therefore yields

  ||(D^j w)(D^l w)||_2
    <= C_ell ||w||_infinity ||w||_{H^{ell-1}}
    <= C_ell ||nabla v||_infinity ||v||_{H^ell}.

For ell=1 the estimate is directly L^infinity times L^2; for ell=0
the transport term vanishes completely.

Pair with D^alpha v and sum using the positive weights in (1.1).
This proves (10.5). The projection P disappears in these pairings
because D^alpha v is divergence-free and P commutes with derivatives.

This integer-order derivation is the tame commutator mechanism; [KP]
provides general background.

10.4 Consequence for Galerkin solutions.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI20]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP19, CP20; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML09; MT06, MT12, MT13.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11, AD14.
  APPLICATION: The direct estimate (10.7) does not require AX6; MT13 is a separate conditional high-order route.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Orthogonality of Pi_N and derivative commutation give

  (1/2) d||u_N||_{H^m}^2/dt
    + nu ||nabla u_N||_{H^m}^2
    <= C_m ||nabla u_N||_infinity ||u_N||_{H^m}^2.           (10.7)

No continuum solution or global smoothness hypothesis is used in (10.7).

11. GALERKIN H^3 CRITERION

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI21]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP17, CP25; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: MT10--MT12.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11--AD14.
  APPLICATION: G_3 and AX6 are distinct propositions. No definition or namespace import proves either bound.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Define

  G_3(nu) :<=>
    forall a in C^\infty_sigma(T^3),
    forall T in (0,infinity),
      sup_{N>=1} sup_{0<=t<=T} ||u_N^a(t)||_{H^3}^2
        < infinity.                                        (11.1)

THEOREM.

  forall nu>0: FB(nu) <=> G_3(nu).                          (11.2)

Sections 12 and 13 prove the two directions. The proof does not assume
an unknown continuation or regularity theorem.

12. G_3(nu) IMPLIES FB(nu)

Fix smooth a and finite T>0. Assume

  M = sup_N sup_{0<=t<=T} ||u_N^a(t)||_{H^3} < infinity.

12.1 All spatial Sobolev norms.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI22]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP20; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML09; MT10, MT13, MT14.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11, AD12, AD14.
  APPLICATION: This proof uses G_3. Source AX6 endpoints require their explicit hAX6 premise.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


By (10.4),

  sup_N sup_{[0,T]} ||nabla u_N||_infinity <= C_emb M.

For each integer m>=3, (10.7) and Gronwall give

  sup_N sup_{[0,T]} ||u_N(t)||_{H^m}^2
    <= ||a||_{H^m}^2 exp(2 C_m C_emb M T).                  (12.1)

Lower Sobolev orders are bounded by the H^3 bound. Hence every spatial
Sobolev norm is bounded uniformly in N on [0,T].

12.2 All time derivatives.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI23]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP20; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: MT15--MT17.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11, AD12, AD14.
  APPLICATION: MT17 synthesizes an already supplied positive-time flow; it neither constructs that witness nor supplies t=0 trace.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


The Galerkin trajectories are smooth. Repeated differentiation of (2.7)
gives, for r>=0,

  partial_t^{r+1} u_N
    = -nu A partial_t^r u_N
      -Pi_N \sum_{j=0}^r binom(r,j)
          B(partial_t^j u_N, partial_t^{r-j}u_N).            (12.2)

Induction in r, using (12.1), (10.3), and contractivity of Pi_N, proves

  forall r,m>=0:
    sup_N sup_{[0,T]} ||partial_t^r u_N(t)||_{H^m}
      < infinity.                                          (12.3)

For m<2, use the established bounds at larger spatial Sobolev orders.
Every bound in this induction may depend on a,nu,T,r,m, but not on N.

12.3 Smooth compactness through the initial time.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI24]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP21; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML04, ML27, ML28; MT11, MT14, MT16.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11, AD12, AD14.
  APPLICATION: Spatial compact inclusion is available; countable mixed-derivative compactness on the closed time cylinder is an additional endpoint.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Arbitrarily high Sobolev embedding in x turns (12.3) into uniform
bounds for every mixed space-time derivative on [0,T]xT^3. One additional
space or time derivative supplies equicontinuity.

Diagonal Arzela--Ascoli gives a subsequence N_j -> infinity with

  u_{N_j} -> u
    in C^\infty([0,T]xT^3).                                (12.4)

Here C^\infty on the closed half-cylinder means that all mixed
derivatives extend continuously to t=0 and t=T.

Since Pi_N a -> a in every Sobolev norm,

  u(0)=a,
  div u=0.

12.4 Passing the equation to the limit.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI25]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP21; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML04; MT15--MT17.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11, AD12, AD14.
  APPLICATION: Convection identity and compatible Sobolev trajectories require explicit convergence and witness transport.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Product continuity gives

  B(u_{N_j},u_{N_j}) -> B(u,u)

in every spatial Sobolev norm, uniformly in time. Moreover, for each
integer m and s>0,

  ||(I-Pi_N)B(u_N,u_N)||_{H^m}
    <= (1+4 pi^2 N^2)^{-s/2}
       ||B(u_N,u_N)||_{H^{m+s}} -> 0,

using (12.1) and (10.3). Therefore (2.7) converges to

  partial_t u + nu A u + B(u,u)=0.                          (12.5)

12.5 Pressure reconstruction.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI26]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP22; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: MT01, MT18.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD01, AD03, AD12, AD14.
  APPLICATION: MT18 takes a GlobalGalerkinStrongLimit witness and yields the normalized quadratic Fourier pressure.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Define the mean-zero periodic p by

  -Delta p = \sum_{i,j} partial_i partial_j (u_i u_j),
  \int_{T^3}p dx = 0.                                      (12.6)

For k!=0,

  \widehat p(k)
    = -\sum_{i,j} (k_i k_j/|k|^2)
                    \widehat{u_i u_j}(k),
  \widehat p(0)=0.                                         (12.7)

The source in (12.6) has zero mean. Fourier multiplier bounds and
(12.4) give p in C^\infty([0,T]xT^3). Equation (12.5) is consequently
equivalent to

  partial_t u + (u.nabla)u - nu Delta u + nabla p=0.

12.6 Compatibility of finite time intervals.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI27]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP22; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML08, ML09; MT01, MT14, MT16.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD01, AD03, AD12, AD14.
  APPLICATION: Initial trace, smooth uniqueness, and interval gluing retain t=0 and arbitrary-mean scope.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


If u,v are two smooth solutions with the same datum, w=u-v satisfies

  (1/2) d||w||_2^2/dt + nu ||nabla w||_2^2
    <= ||nabla v||_infinity ||w||_2^2.

Gronwall and w(0)=0 imply w=0. The mean-zero pressure is then unique.

Apply the finite-interval construction for T=1,2,3,... . Smooth
uniqueness makes the solutions agree on overlaps. They define a global
smooth periodic solution with initial datum a and conserved mean
\overline a.

Thus FB(nu) follows from G_3(nu).

13. FB(nu) IMPLIES G_3(nu)

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI28]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP23, CP24; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML04, ML05, ML09, ML10; MT10, MT11.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11, AD12.
  APPLICATION: Residual convergence and nonlinear bootstrap are explicit converse adapters; the forward conditional root MT19 does not provide them.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Assume FB(nu). Fix smooth a and finite T>0, and choose its smooth solution
u on [0,T]. Let

  M_m = sup_{0<=t<=T} ||u(t)||_{H^m} < infinity,

  v_N = Pi_N u,
  r_N = (I-Pi_N)u,
  e_N = u_N - v_N.

Then e_N(0)=0. Subtracting the projected exact equation from the Galerkin
equation gives

  partial_t e_N + nu A e_N
    + Pi_N[B(v_N,e_N)+B(e_N,v_N)+B(e_N,e_N)]
      = F_N,                                               (13.1)

where

  F_N
    = Pi_N[B(u,u)-B(v_N,v_N)]
    = Pi_N[B(v_N,r_N)+B(r_N,v_N)+B(r_N,r_N)].                (13.2)

13.1 Residual bound.

By the H^3 algebra estimate,

  ||B(v,w)||_{H^3} <= C ||v||_{H^3} ||w||_{H^4}.

Contractivity and (10.2) imply

  delta_N := sup_{[0,T]}||F_N||_{H^3}
    <= C M_4 sup_{[0,T]}||r_N||_{H^4}
    <= C M_4 M_5 (1+4 pi^2 N^2)^{-1/2}
    -> 0.                                                   (13.3)

13.2 Error energy inequalities.

The three required pairings satisfy

  |<e,B(v,e)>_{H^3}|
    <= C ||v||_{H^4} ||e||_{H^3}^2,                         (13.4)

  |<e,B(e,v)>_{H^3}|
    <= C ||v||_{H^4} ||e||_{H^3}^2,                         (13.5)

  |<e,B(e,e)>_{H^3}|
    <= C ||e||_{H^3}^3.                                    (13.6)

For (13.4), expand derivatives up to order three and cancel
v.nabla D^alpha e. The remaining factors are bounded by

  ||nabla v||_infinity + ||D^2 v||_infinity + ||D^3 v||_2
    <= C ||v||_{H^4},

  ||nabla e||_infinity <= C ||e||_{H^3}.

All lower-order terms are controlled by the same norms.
Equation (13.5) follows from the H^3 algebra estimate.
Equation (13.6) follows from (10.5) and (10.4).

Let E_N=||e_N||_{H^3}^2. Pair (13.1) with e_N in H^3, use
orthogonality of Pi_N, discard the nonnegative viscous term, and apply
Young's inequality to the residual. The result is

  E_N'
    <= C(1+M_4)E_N + C E_N^{3/2} + C delta_N^2,
  E_N(0)=0.                                                 (13.7)

All constants are independent of N.

13.3 Bootstrap and spectral stability.

While E_N<=1, set K=C(2+M_4)>0, enlarged if necessary. Then

  E_N' <= K E_N + C delta_N^2,

  E_N(t) <= C T delta_N^2 exp(KT)
       for 0<=t<=T.                                        (13.8)

By (13.3), choose N_0 such that

  C T delta_N^2 exp(KT) < 1/4
       for all N>=N_0.

If E_N first reached 1 before T, (13.8) would give E_N<1/4 at that
time, a contradiction. Hence (13.8) holds throughout [0,T].

It follows that

  sup_{[0,T]}||e_N||_{H^3}
    <= sqrt(C T) delta_N exp(KT/2) -> 0.

Since r_N -> 0 uniformly in H^3,

  u_N -> u in C([0,T];H^3).                                (13.9)

Thus all sufficiently large cutoffs satisfy a common H^3 bound.

For the finitely many N<N_0, finite-dimensional norm comparison and
the Galerkin energy estimate give

  sup_{[0,T]}||u_N(t)||_{H^3}^2
    <= (1+4 pi^2 N^2)^3 ||a||_2^2.

Taking the finite maximum and combining with (13.9) proves G_3(nu).

Together with Section 12, this proves (11.2).

14. THE QUANTUM-OBSERVABLE REGULARITY EQUIVALENCE

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI29]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP27, CP29, CP30; exact contracts in Section 21.
  OPTIONAL_ROUTE: CP30 retains AX6; it is not a CP29 prerequisite.
  REFERENCES: MT12, MT19; ML11--ML14.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD08, AD10, AD12--AD14.
  APPLICATION: Logical composition uses the exact localized observables. AX6=>Fefferman_B_0_adjust does not supply this quantum biconditional.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Define

  Q_{N,a,epsilon}(t)
    = <U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon},
         mathcal E_{3,N}U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon}>.

Define the proposition

  QREG(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall a in C^\infty_sigma(T^3),
    forall T in (0,infinity),
      sup_{N>=1} sup_{0<=t<=T}
        [lim_{epsilon downarrow 0} Q_{N,a,epsilon}(t)]
          < infinity.                                      (14.1)

Every limit in (14.1) exists by (8.6), and

  lim_{epsilon downarrow 0} Q_{N,a,epsilon}(t)
    = ||u_N^a(t)||_{H^3}^2.

Therefore

  QREG(nu,hbar) <=> G_3(nu).                                (14.2)

Combining (11.2) and (14.2),

  forall nu>0, forall hbar>0:
    FB(nu) <=> QREG(nu,hbar).                               (14.3)

The admissible bound has the quantifier form

  forall a, forall finite T>0,
    exists C=C(nu,a,T)<infinity,
      forall N>=1, forall t in [0,T]:
        lim_{epsilon downarrow 0}Q_{N,a,epsilon}(t) <= C.

No uniformity in all initial data and no bound uniform in T=infinity
is asserted. No interchange of the localization limit with the
cutoff supremum is used.

The mathematical equivalence (14.3) is proved. Neither side is
established by the equivalence alone.

14.A ROUND 5: TIME-INTEGRATED GRADIENT OBSERVABLE CRITERION

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI30]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP25, CP27; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML09, ML11--ML14; MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD08, AD10--AD13.
  APPLICATION: Variable-coefficient integrating-factor estimate; time-integrated packet convergence; localization precedes cutoff supremum.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


Define the classical proposition
  LIP(nu) :<=>
    forall a in C^\infty_sigma, forall finite T>0,
      sup_N integral_0^T ||nabla u_N^a(t)||_infinity dt
        <infinity.

Then
  FB(nu)<=>G_3(nu)<=>LIP(nu).                             (L1)

Proof of G_3=>LIP:
The existing Sobolev embedding gives
  integral_0^T ||nabla u_N||_infinity dt
    <=C_emb T sup_{0<=t<=T}||u_N(t)||H3,
so the right side is uniform in N.

Proof of LIP=>G_3:
Let
  L=sup_N integral_0^T ||nabla u_N||_infinity dt.
The existing tame estimate (10.7) at m=3 gives
  d||u_N||H3^2/dt
    <=2 C_3 ||nabla u_N||_infinity ||u_N||H3^2.
Thus
  sup_N sup_{0<=t<=T}||u_N(t)||H3^2
    <=||a||H3^2 exp(2 C_3 L)<infinity.
The previously proved G_3<=>FB completes (L1).

Quantum form:
  mathcal L_N=M_{ell_N},
  ell_N(q)=||nabla I_N(q)||_infinity>=0.
This is a continuous nonnegative multiplier; smoothness of ell_N is
not required, because its observable conjugacy is multiplication-based.

For fixed N and T, (P4)--(P5), or compact uniform continuity, gives
  lim_{epsilon downarrow 0} integral_0^T
    <U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon},
      mathcal L_N U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon}>dt
      =integral_0^T ||nabla u_N^a(t)||_infinity dt.

Define
  QLIP(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall a in C^\infty_sigma, forall finite T>0,
      sup_N [
        lim_{epsilon downarrow 0} integral_0^T
          <U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon},
             mathcal L_N U_N(t)Psi_{N,a,epsilon}>dt
      ]<infinity.

Then
  FB(nu)<=>G_3(nu)<=>QREG(nu,hbar)<=>QLIP(nu,hbar).         (L2)

Quantifiers:
  localization first at fixed N;
  integration over a finite time interval;
  supremum over N afterwards;
  bound may depend on (nu,a,T).

The criterion is equivalent to the original regularity endpoint.
No universal QLIP bound is established.

Trajectorywise operator inequality:
For every q and 0<=t<=T,
  e_{3,N}(Phi_N^t(q))
    <=e_{3,N}(q)
       exp(2 C_3 integral_0^t ell_N(Phi_N^s(q))ds).
Thus, as an inequality of nonnegative multiplication quadratic forms,
  U_N(t)^* mathcal E_{3,N} U_N(t)
    <= M_{ e_{3,N}(q)
            exp(2 C_3 integral_0^t ell_N(Phi_N^s(q))ds) }.
Domain convention: if R_t(q) denotes the right-hand multiplier, then
  D(M_{R_t}^{1/2}) subset D(M_{e_{3,N} o Phi_N^t}^{1/2}),
and the inequality holds on D(M_{R_t}^{1/2}); it is not an assertion
that the two unbounded operators have the same domain.

A bound on a general ensemble average of ell_N alone does not control
the expectation of this exponential. Equivalence (L2) uses the localized
deterministic limits. The additional finite-width equivalence in
Section14.B instead uses a bounded spectral support radius, a derived
reference trajectory, and reference stability; it makes no inference
from a first moment to an exponential moment.

14.B ROUND 8: PRESCRIBED NORMALIZED STATES AND EXACT CRITERIA

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI34]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP33, CP34; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML13, ML14, ML46--ML49, ML51; MT10, MT11.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD08, AD10, AD11, AD13, AD15.
  APPLICATION: Construct the Born probability measure, verify maximal multiplier domains, apply
               fixed-cutoff Fubini and exact subaverage selection, and prove the finite-width
               criterion cycle.
  DETAILS: Section18; adapter contracts: Section19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no matching bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.

Notation: E_N=R^{d_N}; w_N=(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(3/2).
Every occurrence of support denotes closed support (Lean: tsupport).
The family is prescribed before a and T are quantified.

DEFINITION [ADMISSIBLE_PRESCRIBED_PACKET_FAMILY].
Choose once, before the datum and time interval are quantified,

  rho_N > 0,
  eta_N in C_c^infinity(B(0,1);C),
  integral_E_N |eta_N(x)|^2 dx = 1.

The family may depend on N. It is fixed while (a,T) vary. Define

  theta_N = w_N rho_N,
  D = sup_{N>=1} theta_N,

and impose the explicit support-radius condition D < infinity.
For each datum a define

  Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a}(q)
    = rho_N^(-d_N/2) eta_N((q-a_N)/rho_N).

The affine change of variables q=a_N+rho_N x proves

  Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a} in C_c^infinity(E_N),
  ||Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a}||_2 = 1,
  K_{N,a}:=supp(Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a})
    is a nonempty compact subset of B(a_N,rho_N).

For every q in the closed ball of radius rho_N around a_N,

  ||I_N(q)-Pi_N a||_{H^3} <= theta_N,
  ||I_N(q)||_{H^3} <= ||a||_{H^3}+theta_N.                  (P8)

The second inequality uses the full-cutoff H3 contraction; it does not
apply a source zero-mode-excluded Galerkin projection to nonzero-mean
data without the established adapter.

An explicit admissible profile is available. Put

  chi_prof_N(x) = exp(-1/(1-4|x|^2))     if |x| < 1/2,
           0                      if |x| >= 1/2,
  Z_N = integral_E_N |chi_prof_N(x)|^2 dx,
  eta_N = Z_N^(-1/2) chi_prof_N.

For |x|<1/2, every spatial derivative is a finite sum of a polynomial
in x and (1-4|x|^2)^(-1), multiplied by exp(-1/(1-4|x|^2)).
For every integer m>=0, r^(-m)*exp(-1/r) tends to zero as r decreases
to zero. Induction on derivative order therefore extends every derivative
continuously by zero across |x|=1/2. Hence chi_prof_N is smooth and supported
in the closed radius-1/2 ball, which is a compact subset of B(0,1).
Its strict positivity near 0 and compact support give 0<Z_N<infinity.
Thus the normalization is defined and has unit L2 norm.

DEFINITION [FINITE_WIDTH_EXPECTATIONS].
For the prescribed packet, put

  Q^E_{N,a}(t)
    = <U_N(t)Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a},
        mathcal E_{3,N} U_N(t)Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a}>,

  Q^L_{N,a}(t)
    = <U_N(t)Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a},
        mathcal L_N U_N(t)Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a}>.

Both expressions are real and nonnegative. On every finite interval,
the evolved packets have compact support and belong to the maximal
domains of both continuous multiplication operators. Consequently,
these are genuine finite expectations, not merely formal quadratic
expressions or total-integral conventions.

The exact multiplier conjugacy gives

  Q^E_{N,a}(t)
    = integral e_{3,N}(Phi_N^t(q)) |Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a}(q)|^2 dq,

  Q^L_{N,a}(t)
    = integral ell_N(Phi_N^t(q)) |Psi^{rho,eta}_{N,a}(q)|^2 dq.   (P9)

Let mu_{N,a} be the probability measure with density |Psi|^2. Define

  I_{N,T}(q) = integral_0^T ell_N(Phi_N^t(q))dt.

The function (t,q) -> ell_N(Phi_N^t(q)) is continuous on the compact
set [0,T] x K_{N,a}. It is bounded there. Thus Fubini applies to the
finite weighted integral, and

  integral_0^T Q^L_{N,a}(t)dt
    = integral I_{N,T}(q) dmu_{N,a}(q).                    (P10)

THEOREM [P11: REFERENCE_SELECTION_FROM_A_PACKET_AVERAGE].
If integral_0^T Q^L_{N,a}(t)dt <= L, then there exists r_N in K_{N,a}
such that

  I_{N,T}(r_N) <= L.                                      (P11)

DERIVATION.
Continuity of I_{N,T} follows from uniform continuity on the preceding
compact product. The continuous function I_{N,T} attains a minimum on
the nonempty compact set K_{N,a}. For a minimizer r_N,

  I_{N,T}(r_N)
    = I_{N,T}(r_N) mu_{N,a}(K_{N,a})
    <= integral I_{N,T}(q) dmu_{N,a}(q)
    <= L.

Equivalently, the source endpoint
ML46 / MeasureTheory.exists_notMem_null_le_integral can be applied to mu_{N,a}
and the null complement of K_{N,a}; its exact source entry is supplied
in Section18.5. The derivation does not require
measurable dependence of r_N on N, a or T.

DEFINITION [QREG_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar)].
For every smooth divergence-free a and every finite T>0, there exists
K=K(nu,a,T,rho,eta)>=0 such that

  forall N>=1, forall t in [0,T], Q^E_{N,a}(t) <= K.

DEFINITION [QLIP_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar)].
For every smooth divergence-free a and every finite T>0, there exists
L=L(nu,a,T,rho,eta)>=0 such that

  forall N>=1, integral_0^T Q^L_{N,a}(t)dt <= L.

Neither predicate contains a rho->0, epsilon->0, or state-localization
limit. The prescribed family is part of the definition. These new
predicates do not redefine QREG or QLIP from Sections 14 and 14.A.

THEOREM [P12: FINITE_WIDTH_CRITERION_EQUIVALENCE].
For every admissible prescribed packet family with D<infinity,

  G_3(nu)
    <=> QREG_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar)
    <=> QLIP_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar).                       (P12)

DERIVATION OF G_3 => QREG_pkt.
Fix a,T and let

  A_a = ||a||_{H^3},
  M = sup_N sup_{0<=t<=T} ||u_N^a(t)||_{H^3} < infinity,
  Lambda = C_emb M T.

The Sobolev embedding gives

  integral_0^t ell_N(Phi_N^s(a_N))ds <= Lambda
  for all N and 0<=t<=T.

For q in K_{N,a}, P7 with the center trajectory as reference gives

  ||I_N(Phi_N^t(q))-u_N^a(t)||_{H^3}
    <= theta_N exp(Lambda) <= D exp(Lambda).              (P13)

Therefore every such trajectory satisfies

  ||I_N(Phi_N^t(q))||_{H^3} <= M+D exp(Lambda).

Integrating its squared norm against the unit-mass density gives

  Q^E_{N,a}(t) <= [M+D exp(Lambda)]^2.                    (P14)

The right side is finite and independent of N,t and of the profile
shape. This proves QREG_pkt.

DERIVATION OF QREG_pkt => QLIP_pkt.
Pointwise, ell_N <= C_emb sqrt(e_{3,N}). Cauchy--Schwarz with the
probability density in P9 gives

  Q^L_{N,a}(t)
    <= C_emb integral sqrt(e_{3,N}(Phi_N^t(q))) dmu_{N,a}(q)
    <= C_emb sqrt(Q^E_{N,a}(t)).

If Q^E_{N,a}(t)<=K uniformly in N,t, then

  integral_0^T Q^L_{N,a}(t)dt <= C_emb T sqrt(K).          (P15)

This proves QLIP_pkt. Every integral is finite by compact support.

DERIVATION OF QLIP_pkt => G_3.
Fix a,T, set A_a=||a||H3, and take a common L>=0 from QLIP_pkt. For each N, P11 supplies
r_N in K_{N,a} with I_{N,T}(r_N)<=L. The initial H3 bound is

  ||I_N(r_N)||_{H^3} <= A_a+theta_N <= A_a+D.

The cutoff-independent tame inequality, applied to this one finite
trajectory, gives

  (1/2) d||I_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))||_{H^3}^2/dt
    <= C_3 ell_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))
         ||I_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))||_{H^3}^2.

Multiplication by exp(-2 C_3 integral_0^t ell_N(Phi_N^s(r_N))ds)
and taking square roots give

  sup_{0<=t<=T} ||I_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))||_{H^3}
    <= (A_a+theta_N) exp(C_3 L).                            (P16)

This step applies the already proved finite-trajectory energy inequality.
It does not apply G_3 to the N-dependent datum I_N(r_N).

Use r_N as reference in P7, with q_0=a_N. Since |a_N-r_N|<=rho_N,

  sup_{0<=t<=T} ||u_N^a(t)-I_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))||_{H^3}
    <= theta_N exp(L).

Hence

  sup_{N>=1} sup_{0<=t<=T} ||u_N^a(t)||_{H^3}
    <= (A_a+D) exp(C_3 L)+D exp(L) < infinity.              (P17)

The datum a and interval T were arbitrary. Thus G_3 holds, completing
the cycle and the proof of P12.

COROLLARY [P18: ONE AVERAGE CONTROLS THE FULL SUPPORT BALL].
Under the same one-packet integrated bound <=L, every q_0 satisfying
|q_0-a_N|<=rho_N obeys

  sup_{0<=t<=T} ||I_N(Phi_N^t(q_0))||_{H^3}
    <= (A_a+theta_N) exp(C_3 L)+2 theta_N exp(L).             (P18)

Indeed, |q_0-r_N|<=2rho_N, so P7 and P16 apply. This includes points
outside the support of the particular packet. Consequently, if the same bound integral_0^T Q^L_{N,a}(t)dt<=L
holds for every N>=1, then

  sup_{N>=1,0<=t<=T} Q^E_{N,a}(t)
    <= [(A_a+D) exp(C_3 L)+2D exp(L)]^2.                   (P19)

No estimate of the expectation of exp(C_3 I_{N,T}) from the expectation
of I_{N,T} has been used. The additional hypothesis is the bounded
spectral support radius D. An unrestricted ensemble average does not
provide that hypothesis.

COROLLARY [P20: SEVEN CRITERIA].
Composition with the previously derived implications yields

  FB(nu)
    <=> G_3(nu)
    <=> LIP(nu)
    <=> QREG(nu,hbar)
    <=> QLIP(nu,hbar)
    <=> QREG_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar)
    <=> QLIP_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar).                       (P20)

This is an equivalence theorem. None of these universal predicates is
asserted without its equivalent hypothesis. No continuum Hamiltonian
or positive coercive Hamiltonian energy is inferred.

CANONICAL EXPLICIT WIDTH.
Choose

  rho_N = epsilon_N
    = 1 / [(N+1)(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(3/2)].

Then theta_N=1/(N+1), D=1/2 for N>=1, and theta_N->0. This choice is
independent of a, nu, hbar and T, and is of order N^(-4). With any fixed
admissible profiles eta_N, P12 and P20 apply to actual normalized
wavefunctions at these positive widths. The width is prescribed before
any unknown regularity bound is evaluated.

14.C ROUND 9: CONDITIONAL QUANTITATIVE OBSERVABLE LIMITS

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI35]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP35; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML05, ML14; MT10, MT11.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD11--AD13, AD15.
  APPLICATION: Reference stability gives explicit packet errors; the already proved smooth-reference
               Galerkin convergence gives the conditional continuum-observable limit.
  DETAILS: Section18; adapter contracts: Section19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no matching bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.

THEOREM [P21: QUANTITATIVE PRESCRIBED-PACKET ERRORS].
Assume G_3(nu). Fix a,T and M,Lambda as in P13. For every N,

  sup_{q in K_{N,a}} sup_{0<=t<=T}
    ||I_N(Phi_N^t(q))-u_N^a(t)||_{H^3}
      <= theta_N exp(Lambda).                            (P21a)
