The H3-energy expectation obeys

  sup_{0<=t<=T}
    |Q^E_{N,a}(t)-||u_N^a(t)||_{H^3}^2|
      <= [2M+theta_N exp(Lambda)] theta_N exp(Lambda).     (P21b)

The gradient expectation obeys

  sup_{0<=t<=T}
    |Q^L_{N,a}(t)-||nabla u_N^a(t)||_infinity|
      <= C_emb theta_N exp(Lambda),                      (P21c)

and therefore

  |integral_0^T Q^L_{N,a}(t)dt
     -integral_0^T ||nabla u_N^a(t)||_infinity dt|
      <= C_emb T theta_N exp(Lambda).                    (P21d)

DERIVATION.
Equation P21a is P13. For v=I_N(Phi_N^t(q)), u=u_N^a(t), put
e=theta_N exp(Lambda). Then ||u||H3<=M and ||v-u||H3<=e. Thus

  | ||v||H3^2-||u||H3^2 |
    <= (||v||H3+||u||H3) ||v-u||H3
    <= (2M+e)e.

Integration against the probability density proves P21b. The reverse
triangle inequality and the Sobolev embedding give

  | ||nabla v||_infinity-||nabla u||_infinity |
    <= ||nabla(v-u)||_infinity <= C_emb ||v-u||H3.

Integration proves P21c, and time integration proves P21d.

If theta_N->0, all errors in P21 tend to zero on the fixed interval.
For the canonical widths, the explicit bounds are

  [2M+exp(Lambda)/(N+1)] exp(Lambda)/(N+1)

for the energy expectation and

  C_emb T exp(Lambda)/(N+1)

for the integrated-gradient expectation. Thus one prescribed family of
normalized states has an O((N+1)^(-1)) conditional observable error.
The constants depend on the G3 bound for a,T; the state construction
does not. No estimate is claimed without the stated G3 hypothesis.

The criterion equivalence P12 requires only bounded theta_N. The
additional condition theta_N->0 is used only for the error limit.
In particular, ρ_N proportional to w_N^(-1), of order N^(-3), already
gives the criterion equivalence; the additional (N+1)^(-1) factor gives
the displayed convergence rate. No optimality claim is made for either
choice of width.

COROLLARY [P22: CONDITIONAL CONTINUUM OBSERVABLE ACCESS].
Assume G_3(nu), fix smooth a and finite T>0, and let u be the unique
smooth NSE solution supplied by Section12. Section13 applied to this u
gives
  zeta_N=sup_{0<=t<=T}||u_N^a(t)-u(t)||H3 ->0.
Set M_u=sup_{0<=t<=T}||u(t)||H3 and e_N^pkt=theta_N*exp(Lambda),
with M and Lambda as in P13. Triangle inequalities and P21 give
  sup_{0<=t<=T} |Q^E_{N,a}(t)-||u(t)||H3^2|
    <=(2*M+e_N^pkt)*e_N^pkt+(M+M_u)*zeta_N,                (P22a)
  sup_{0<=t<=T} |Q^L_{N,a}(t)-||nabla u(t)||_infinity|
    <=C_emb*(e_N^pkt+zeta_N),                             (P22b)
  |integral_0^T Q^L_{N,a}(t)dt
      -integral_0^T ||nabla u(t)||_infinity dt|
    <=C_emb*T*(e_N^pkt+zeta_N).                           (P22c)
For the energy term use
  | ||u_N||H3^2-||u||H3^2 |<=(M+M_u)||u_N-u||H3;
for the gradient term use the reverse triangle inequality and embedding.

For N sufficiently large, the actual residual delta_N from (13.3) and
the bootstrap (13.8) give the explicit additional bound
  zeta_N<=sqrt(C*T)*exp(K*T/2)*delta_N
             +M_4*(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(-1/2),
  delta_N<=C*M_4*M_5*(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(-1/2).
Thus zeta_N=O(N^(-1)) on this fixed interval. The canonical widths give
e_N^pkt=exp(Lambda)/(N+1), so (P22a)--(P22c) are O(N^(-1)) as well.
Every rate constant depends on the stated smooth-solution/regularity
bounds. The packet family itself is fixed independently of those bounds.

The conclusions are limits of scalar observables from the finite quantum
models. No identification of all Hilbert spaces mathcal H_N with a common field
Hilbert space, or existence of a continuum quantum generator, is used.


14.D ROUND 11: FINITE-MOMENT NORMALIZED STATES AND EXACT CRITERIA

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI37]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP37, CP38; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML13, ML14, ML46--ML49; MT10, MT11.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD15, AD17.
  APPLICATION: Actual fourth-moment integrability supplies maximal observable domains; noncompact
               Fubini and joint-score first-moment selection replace compact support.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

Notation: omega_N=w_N*sqrt(m_{2,N}); D_2=sup_N omega_N.
D_N remains the dense compact smooth test subspace. Gamma_N is the
already established finite gradient coefficient from Section8.4.

14.D.1. Prescribed profile and probability-measure contract.

For every N choose a measurable representative chi_N:E_N->C such that

  integral |chi_N(z)|^2 dz = 1,
  m_{4,N}:=integral |z|^4 |chi_N(z)|^2 dz < infinity.

Integrability convention for later Lean statements:
  chi_N is measurable and represents an actual L2 state of norm one;
  Integrable (fun z => |z|^4*|chi_N(z)|^2) volume.
The displayed fourth moment is an ordinary integral after this explicit
integrability premise is established. A totalized real integral merely
having a finite value is not the intended hypothesis.

The profile family is fixed before a and T are quantified. No compact
support, differentiability, phase restriction or centered first moment
is imposed. Define

  m_{2,N}=integral |z|^2 |chi_N(z)|^2 dz,
  omega_N=w_N sqrt(m_{2,N}),
  D_2=sup_{N>=1} omega_N,

and assume D_2<infinity. The fourth moments need not be uniform in N.

For every a set

  Psi^chi_{N,a}(q)=chi_N(q-a_N),
  dmu_{N,a}(q)=|Psi^chi_{N,a}(q)|^2 dq.                    (M1)

Translation invariance gives ||Psi^chi_{N,a}||_2=1, so mu_{N,a} is a
probability measure. The measure is constructed from the nonnegative
integrable density before an IsProbabilityMeasure instance is used.
Changing chi_N on a Lebesgue-null set changes neither the L2 state nor
the probability measure, since translations preserve null sets.

Probability Cauchy--Schwarz gives

  m_{2,N} <= sqrt(m_{4,N}),
  integral |z| |chi_N(z)|^2 dz <= sqrt(m_{2,N}).           (M2)

In particular the lower moments are finite. The translated density has
finite fourth moment because

  |a_N+z|^4 <= 8(|a_N|^4+|z|^4).

This proves all finite-moment claims required below independently of
any continuum regularity assertion.

14.D.2. Genuine maximal-operator expectations without compact support.

For every t>=0 the established finite Galerkin energy identity gives

  |Phi_N^t(q)|<=|q|.

The exact half-density change of variables therefore implies, for
r=2 and r=4,

  integral |q|^r |U_N(t)Psi(q)|^2 dq
    = integral |Phi_N^t(q)|^r |Psi(q)|^2 dq
    <= integral |q|^r |Psi(q)|^2 dq < infinity.            (M3)

Since e_{3,N}(q)^2<=w_N^4|q|^4 and
ell_N(q)^2<=Gamma_N^2|q|^2, equation (M3) proves

  U_N(t)Psi^chi_{N,a} in Dom(mathcal E_{3,N}),
  U_N(t)Psi^chi_{N,a} in Dom(mathcal L_N).                 (M4)

Thus the definitions

  Q^{E,chi}_{N,a}(t)
    = <U_N(t)Psi^chi_{N,a},mathcal E_{3,N}U_N(t)Psi^chi_{N,a}>,
  Q^{L,chi}_{N,a}(t)
    = <U_N(t)Psi^chi_{N,a},mathcal L_N U_N(t)Psi^chi_{N,a}>

are finite ordinary maximal-operator expectations. Neither is merely
a totalized integral or an unspecified quadratic form.
The general measurable profile need not belong to Dom(H_N); its unitary
Hilbert-space evolution is already defined. Gaussian membership in all
Hamiltonian powers is proved separately in (G4).

Exact multiplier conjugacy gives

  Q^{E,chi}_{N,a}(t)=integral e_{3,N}(Phi_N^t(q)) dmu_{N,a}(q),
  Q^{L,chi}_{N,a}(t)=integral ell_N(Phi_N^t(q)) dmu_{N,a}(q).  (M5)

On every finite interval [0,T], the first integrand is bounded by
w_N^2|q|^2 and the second by Gamma_N|q|. Both majorants are integrable
with respect to mu_{N,a}. Continuity of Phi_N and ell_N, followed by
dominated convergence, shows that both expectations are continuous in t.

Set

  I_{N,T}(q)=integral_0^T ell_N(Phi_N^t(q))dt.

Then

  0<=I_{N,T}(q)<=Gamma_N T |q|.                            (M6)

Joint continuity of the integrand gives product measurability, and the
right side of (M6) gives product integrability on [0,T] x E_N. Hence

  integral_0^T Q^{L,chi}_{N,a}(t)dt
    = integral I_{N,T}(q) dmu_{N,a}(q).                    (M7)

No compact-support argument or cutoff-uniform dominating function is
used in this fixed-N/T Fubini step.

14.D.3. Reference selection with a simultaneous moment constraint.

Assume, for fixed a,T, a common L>=0 satisfies

  forall N>=1:
    integral_0^T Q^{L,chi}_{N,a}(t)dt <= L.

For any lambda>0 define

  F_{N,lambda}(q)=I_{N,T}(q)+lambda*w_N^2|q-a_N|^2,
  S_lambda=L+lambda*D_2^2,
  R_lambda=sqrt(D_2^2+L/lambda).

The function F_{N,lambda} is nonnegative and mu_{N,a}-integrable.
Equations (M1), (M7) and the definition of D_2 give

  integral F_{N,lambda} dmu_{N,a}
    <= L+lambda*omega_N^2 <= S_lambda.

The exact probability first-moment theorem, applied with the empty null
set, supplies r_N in E_N such that

  F_{N,lambda}(r_N)<=S_lambda.

Both terms are nonnegative. Therefore

  I_{N,T}(r_N)<=S_lambda,
  w_N|r_N-a_N|<=R_lambda.                                (M8)

The point r_N may depend on N,a,T,lambda. No measurable choice in these
parameters is required. In particular, r_N is a derived existential;
it is not an unresolved input witness.

14.D.4. Exact moment-family regularity predicates.

Define QREG_mom^chi(nu,hbar) by

  forall a in C-infinity_sigma, forall finite T>0,
  exists K=K(nu,hbar,a,T,chi)>=0,
  forall N>=1, forall t in [0,T]: Q^{E,chi}_{N,a}(t)<=K.

Define QLIP_mom^chi(nu,hbar) by

  forall a in C-infinity_sigma, forall finite T>0,
  exists L=L(nu,hbar,a,T,chi)>=0,
  forall N>=1: integral_0^T Q^{L,chi}_{N,a}(t)dt<=L.

THEOREM [M9: MOMENT_FAMILY_CRITERION_EQUIVALENCE].
For every prescribed measurable normalized L2 profile family with
Integrable (fun z => |z|^4*|chi_N(z)|^2) volume for every N and D_2<infinity,

  G_3(nu) <=> QREG_mom^chi(nu,hbar)
          <=> QLIP_mom^chi(nu,hbar).                     (M9)

DERIVATION OF G_3 => QREG_mom.
Fix a,T. Let

  A_a=||a||H3,
  M=sup_{N>=1,0<=t<=T}||u_N^a(t)||H3<infinity,
  Lambda=C_emb*M*T.

For every q in E_N, the reference-trajectory estimate with reference a_N
gives

  ||I_N(Phi_N^t(q))-u_N^a(t)||H3
    <= exp(Lambda)*w_N|q-a_N|,
    0<=t<=T.                                             (M10)

Consequently

  Q^{E,chi}_{N,a}(t)
    <= integral [M+exp(Lambda)*w_N|q-a_N|]^2 dmu_{N,a}
    <= M^2+2M exp(Lambda)*omega_N+exp(2Lambda)*omega_N^2
    <= [M+D_2 exp(Lambda)]^2.                            (M11)

The middle inequality uses probability Cauchy--Schwarz. Its right side
is independent of N and t, so QREG_mom follows.

DERIVATION OF QREG_mom => QLIP_mom.
The pointwise embedding and probability Cauchy--Schwarz imply

  Q^{L,chi}_{N,a}(t)
    <= C_emb integral sqrt(e_{3,N}(Phi_N^t(q))) dmu_{N,a}
    <= C_emb sqrt(Q^{E,chi}_{N,a}(t)).

Thus a common energy bound K gives

  integral_0^T Q^{L,chi}_{N,a}(t)dt<=C_emb*T*sqrt(K),      (M12)

uniformly in N.

DERIVATION OF QLIP_mom => G_3.
Fix a,T, set A_a=||a||H3, and take a common L>=0 from QLIP_mom. Fix
lambda>0. The point r_N derived in (M8) obeys

  ||I_N(r_N)||H3
    <=||Pi_N a||H3+w_N|r_N-a_N|<=A_a+R_lambda.

Apply the already proved finite-trajectory tame inequality to r_N:

  d||I_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))||H3^2/dt
    <=2*C_3*ell_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))*||I_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))||H3^2.

The integrating factor and (M8) give

  sup_{0<=t<=T}||I_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))||H3
    <=(A_a+R_lambda)*exp(C_3*S_lambda).

Using r_N as reference in the exact stability estimate gives

  sup_{0<=t<=T}||u_N^a(t)-I_N(Phi_N^t(r_N))||H3
    <=R_lambda*exp(S_lambda).

Therefore

  sup_{N>=1,0<=t<=T}||u_N^a(t)||H3
    <=(A_a+R_lambda)*exp(C_3*S_lambda)
       +R_lambda*exp(S_lambda)<infinity.                 (M13)

The choice lambda=1 is valid for every L,D_2>=0, including zero values.
Thus (M13) has no exceptional denominator case and proves G_3.
If L>0 and D_2>0, the optional choice lambda=L/D_2^2 gives the sharper
explicit pair S_lambda=2L and R_lambda=sqrt(2)*D_2.

The converse applies a finite-trajectory inequality to r_N. It never
applies G_3 to the N-dependent datum I_N(r_N), never assumes a global
smooth continuum solution, and never bounds an exponential moment by
the first moment.

14.D.5. Conditional expectation errors and the compact-family specialization.

Under G_3, define M,Lambda as in (M10). For every N,

  sup_{0<=t<=T}
    |Q^{E,chi}_{N,a}(t)-||u_N^a(t)||H3^2|
      <=2M exp(Lambda)*omega_N+exp(2Lambda)*omega_N^2,     (M14a)

  sup_{0<=t<=T}
    |Q^{L,chi}_{N,a}(t)-||nabla u_N^a(t)||_infinity|
      <=C_emb exp(Lambda)*omega_N,                       (M14b)

  |integral_0^T Q^{L,chi}_{N,a}(t)dt
      -integral_0^T ||nabla u_N^a(t)||_infinity dt|
      <=C_emb*T*exp(Lambda)*omega_N.                      (M14c)

Proof: with x(q)=w_N|q-a_N| and e(q)=exp(Lambda)x(q), (M10) gives

  | ||I_N(Phi_N^t(q))||H3^2-||u_N^a(t)||H3^2 |
    <=2M e(q)+e(q)^2.

Integrate, using integral x<=omega_N and integral x^2=omega_N^2.
For the gradient apply the reverse norm triangle inequality and the
periodic embedding to (M10), then integrate. Time integration gives
(M14c). All required functions are integrable by the preceding bounds.

If omega_N->0, the errors vanish uniformly on each fixed finite interval.
Combining with the existing Section13 continuum Galerkin error zeta_N
gives (P22a)--(P22c) with e_N^pkt replaced by exp(Lambda)*omega_N.
The premise G_3 remains explicit in every such continuum-observable limit.

For the earlier compact packet family, set

  chi_N(z)=rho_N^(-d_N/2)*eta_N(z/rho_N).

Then m_{2,N}<=rho_N^2 and m_{4,N}<=rho_N^4, so
omega_N<=w_N*rho_N. The actual states agree exactly with Section14.B.
The new theorem therefore applies to every earlier admissible compact
family, without changing the original predicates or their definitions.

14.E ROUND 12: GAUSSIAN STATES, WEYL KINEMATICS AND HARMONIC DRIFT

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI38]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP39; supporting G13 belongs to CP36; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML13, ML14, ML20--ML25, ML37--ML45, ML50, ML52--ML57; MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD07, AD17, AD18.
  APPLICATION: Normalize product Gaussians in actual Euclidean volume, prove all polynomial moments
               and weighted graph domains, then derive selfadjoint momenta and Weyl relations from
               explicit translations.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.E.1. Exact normalized Gaussian family.

Fix d=d_N, sigma>0 and p in R^d. Put z=q-a_N and define

  Psi_{N,a;sigma,p}(q)
    =(2*pi*sigma^2)^(-d/4)
      exp(-|z|^2/(4*sigma^2))*exp(i*p.z/hbar).             (G1)

The profile at a_N=0 is prescribed before the datum and T. Its Born
density is

  g_{sigma,d}(z)
    =(2*pi*sigma^2)^(-d/2)*exp(-|z|^2/(2*sigma^2))
    =product_{j=1}^d g_{sigma,1}(z_j).

The one-dimensional Gaussian integral gives integral g_{sigma,1}=1;
finite-product integration therefore gives integral g_{sigma,d}=1.
Hence ||Psi_{N,a;sigma,p}||_2=1. The phase has modulus one.

For the one-dimensional normalized density g=g_{sigma,1},

  g'(x)=-(x/sigma^2)g(x).

Oddness gives integral x*g(x)dx=0. Gaussian decay makes all polynomial
products and their derivatives integrable and their boundary terms zero.
Integration by parts gives

  integral x^2*g(x)dx
    =-sigma^2 integral x*g'(x)dx=sigma^2,
  integral x^4*g(x)dx
    =-sigma^2 integral x^3*g'(x)dx=3*sigma^4.

Finite-product factorization yields

  integral z_j*g_{sigma,d}(z)dz=0,
  integral z_j*z_k*g_{sigma,d}(z)dz=sigma^2*delta_{jk},
  integral |z|^2*g_{sigma,d}(z)dz=d*sigma^2,
  integral |z|^4*g_{sigma,d}(z)dz=d*(d+2)*sigma^4.        (G2)

The last equality is
  sum_j 3*sigma^4+2*sum_{j<k}sigma^4=d*(d+2)*sigma^4.

14.E.2. Actual closed Hamiltonian and momentum domains.

Every spatial derivative of the state (G1) is a polynomial in q,
with coefficients depending on a_N,sigma,p,hbar, times the same
Gaussian and phase. Gaussian decay dominates every polynomial.
Consequently

  Psi_{N,a;sigma,p} in Schwartz(E_N;C).                   (G3)

Write T_pol for the explicit polynomial differential expression

  T_pol psi=-i*hbar*[b_N.nabla psi+(div b_N)psi/2].

Because b_N is polynomial of degree at most two and div b_N is constant,

  T_pol:Schwartz(E_N;C)->Schwartz(E_N;C).

For every Schwartz psi and phi in the actual compact test domain,
compact-test integration by parts gives

  <H_{N,min}phi,psi>=<phi,T_pol psi>.

The right-hand vector T_pol psi belongs to L2. The maximal weak-domain
characterization (R6.17a) therefore proves

  psi in Dom(H_N),
  H_N psi=T_pol psi.

Induction, using preservation of Schwartz functions, gives

  Schwartz(E_N;C) subset intersection_{k>=0} Dom(H_N^k),
  H_N^k psi=T_pol^k psi in Schwartz(E_N;C).               (G4)

No Hamiltonian domain is inferred from smoothness alone; the L2 image
and exact adjoint test-pairing identity supply domain membership.

For momentum, retain the original minimal operator
  P_{j,min}=-i*hbar*partial_j on C_c^infinity(E_N;C).
It is densely defined and symmetric. The same density/symmetry
argument used for H_{N,min} proves P_{j,min} closable.
Let P_j denote its graph closure in the following Gaussian formulas.

If cut_R(q)=cut(q/R), where cut is real smooth compactly supported,
equal to one on B(0,1), and zero outside B(0,2), then for Schwartz psi,

  cut_R psi -> psi in L2,
  P_{j,min}(cut_R psi)
    =cut_R*(-i*hbar*partial_j psi)
       -i*hbar*(partial_j cut_R)*psi
    ->-i*hbar*partial_j psi in L2.

The derivative-cutoff term is supported where |q|>=R and bounded by
C/R times |psi|. Thus

  Schwartz(E_N;C) subset Dom(P_j),
  P_j psi=-i*hbar*partial_j psi.                          (G5)

The maximal coordinate multiplier Q_j also acts on Schwartz functions
and preserves that class. Every mean and variance below consequently
has a proved operator domain. Selfadjointness of the individual P_j
is not needed for these identities and is not introduced as a premise.

14.E.3. Exact Gaussian canonical moments.

On the state (G1), direct differentiation gives

  P_j Psi
    =[p_j+i*hbar*z_j/(2*sigma^2)]Psi.

Using (G2),

  <Psi,Q_j Psi>=a_{N,j},
  <Psi,P_j Psi>=p_j,
  Var_Psi(Q_j)=||[Q_j-a_{N,j}]Psi||_2^2=sigma^2,
  Var_Psi(P_j)=||[P_j-p_j]Psi||_2^2=hbar^2/(4*sigma^2).   (G6)

Therefore

  sqrt(Var_Psi(Q_j))*sqrt(Var_Psi(P_j))=hbar/2,
  [sum_j Var_Psi(Q_j)]*[sum_j Var_Psi(P_j)]
    =hbar^2*d^2/4,                                       (G7)

and

  sum_j ||P_j Psi||_2^2
    =|p|^2+hbar^2*d/(4*sigma^2).                          (G8)

These equalities concern the prescribed Gaussian and the proved closed
momentum action. They do not require a position eigenstate or a
distributional wavefunction.

For the real amplitude g=(2*pi*sigma^2)^(-d/4)
exp(-|q-a_N|^2/(4*sigma^2)), the weighted graph approximation below
extends the real-test identity <phi,H_N phi>=0 to g. Thus

  <g,H_N g>=0.

The explicit phase product rule gives

  H_N(exp(i*p.(q-a_N)/hbar)*g)
    =exp(i*p.(q-a_N)/hbar)*[H_N g+(p.b_N)g],

and hence

  <Psi_{N,a;sigma,p},H_N Psi_{N,a;sigma,p}>
    =p.integral b_N(q)*g_{sigma,d}(q-a_N)dq.               (G9)

All terms are integrable because b_N is quadratic and the state has
Gaussian moments. The finite Fourier trace identity, separately
derived at CP40, evaluates the remaining drift expectation.

14.E.4. Canonical Gaussian regularity criteria.

Choose once for every N

  sigma_N=1/[(N+1)*w_N*sqrt(d_N)],
  p_N in R^{d_N},

where the momentum sequence is fixed while a and T vary. Formula (G1)
defines the corresponding translated profile family. By (G2),

  omega_N=w_N*sqrt(d_N*sigma_N^2)=1/(N+1),
  D_2=1/2,
  w_N^4*m_{4,N}=(1+2/d_N)/(N+1)^4.                     (G10)

Thus the moment-family hypotheses are explicit and independent of any
unknown regularity bound. Let QREG_Gauss and QLIP_Gauss denote the
predicates in (M9) for this prescribed family. Then

  G_3(nu) <=> QREG_Gauss(nu,hbar)
          <=> QLIP_Gauss(nu,hbar).                        (G11)

Composition with the previously proved FB/G3 equivalence gives the
same NSE endpoint for these actual full-support normalized Gaussian
states. The canonical Gaussian family has conditional O((N+1)^(-1))
observable errors by (M14), and the conditional continuum errors follow
by the same zeta_N composition used in P22.

The phase sequence changes momentum means but not the initial density
or any transported fluid-multiplier expectation. Hence the truth values
of (G11) and all bounds from (M9)--(M14) are independent of p_N.

Equation (G8) becomes the exact identity

  sum_j ||P_j Psi_{N,a;sigma_N,p_N}||_2^2
    =|p_N|^2+hbar^2*d_N^2*w_N^2*(N+1)^2/4.              (G12)

SUPPORTING COROLLARY, assigned to CP36 rather than the CP39 core contract.
For N>=2, the existing dimension estimate (R10.4), combined with the
exact Gaussian variance formula (G12), gives

  sum_j Var_Psi(P_j)
    >=(64*pi^6/27)*hbar^2*N^14.                           (G13)

The state has unbounded support. Equations (G10)--(G13) use its exact
second moment, not a compact support radius. The coefficient-space
momentum quadratic norm remains separate from the transport Hamiltonian
expectation and from any computational complexity assertion.

14.E.5. Weighted actual-core approximation for all Schwartz states.

For m>=0 define

  ||f||_{(m)}^2=integral (1+|q|^2)^m |f(q)|^2 dq.

Fix a Schwartz state psi, an integer k>=0, and cut_R as in (G5), with
0<=cut<=1. Put psi_R=cut_R*psi, R>=1. Then psi_R is an actual
C_c^infinity test function, and

  for every j<=k:
    ||H_N^j psi_R-H_N^j psi||_{(m)} ->0.                 (G14)

DERIVATION.
Induction on j shows that the differential expression T_pol^j has the
finite representation

  T_pol^j=sum_{|alpha|<=j} p_{j,alpha}(q)*partial^alpha,
  degree(p_{j,alpha})<=2j.

The induction follows from the product rule: composition by b_N.nabla
either differentiates the coefficient or adds one derivative to the
input; multiplying by b_N raises polynomial degree by at most two.
The zeroth-order coefficient div b_N/2 is constant.

Since H_N agrees with T_pol on Schwartz and on the actual test domain,

  H_N^j(cut_R psi)-H_N^j psi
    =(cut_R-1)H_N^j psi
      +sum_{|alpha|<=j} sum_{0<beta<=alpha}
         binomial(alpha,beta)*p_{j,alpha}
         *(partial^beta cut_R)*(partial^{alpha-beta}psi). (G15)

The first term tends to zero in ||.||_{(m)} by dominated convergence,
because H_N^j psi is Schwartz. Every remaining term is supported where
R<=|q|<=2R, and

  |partial^beta cut_R(q)|<=C_beta*R^(-|beta|)<=C_beta.

After squaring and applying the weight, each term is dominated by an
integrable polynomial weight times a squared Schwartz derivative, with
an additional indicator of {|q|>=R}. Dominated convergence therefore
annihilates every term. The sum is finite, proving (G14).

Quantitatively, for every K>0 there exists a finite constant C such that

  max_{0<=j<=k}||H_N^j psi_R-H_N^j psi||_{(m)}
    <=C*R^(-K),    R>=1.                                 (G16)

To verify this, choose a Schwartz decay order
L>2k+m+d_N/2+K. Bound each relevant derivative by
C_L*(1+|q|)^(-L); the polynomial coefficients have degree at most 2k.
The tail radial integral then has norm decay
O(R^(2k+m+d_N/2-L)), which is O(R^(-K)). The cutoff-derivative
factors only improve this bound. The constant may depend on the fixed
cutoff N, coefficients, nu,hbar,psi,m,k,K. No N-uniform rate is asserted.

In particular, m=1 and k=3 prove simultaneous weighted convergence
of psi_R and H_N^3 psi_R for every Gaussian state (G1). Any weighted
unitary/resolvent error estimate proved on the actual test domain and
continuous under these two norms therefore extends to these Gaussian
states, after the corresponding bounded-operator continuity is proved.

14.E.6. Selfadjoint momenta and exact Weyl kinematics.

Here eps_j denotes the j-th standard vector in coefficient space,
distinct from the physical Fourier field e_j=I_N(eps_j).
For y,p in E_N define on the whole Hilbert space

  (T_y psi)(q)=psi(q-y),
  (M_p psi)(q)=exp(i*p.q/hbar)*psi(q).

Translation invariance and the modulus-one phase give

  ||T_y psi||_2=||psi||_2,
  ||M_p psi||_2=||psi||_2,
  T_y^*=T_{-y},
  M_p^*=M_{-p}.

Both maps preserve the actual compact test domain. For a fixed coordinate
j, t->T_{t eps_j} is a strongly continuous unitary group: prove continuity
first for compact smooth functions by compact uniform continuity, then
extend using density and the isometry estimate. On that domain,

  d(T_{t eps_j}phi)/dt=-partial_j(T_{t eps_j}phi)
                   =-(i/hbar)P_{j,min}T_{t eps_j}phi.

Every premise of the direct Section6 resolvent proof is therefore
verified with the explicit complete flow q->q+t eps_j and Jacobian one.
The two resolvent integrals, graph identities and adjoint/range argument
give

  closure(P_{j,min})^*=closure(P_{j,min})=P_j,

  Dom(P_j)
    ={psi:lim_{t->0}(T_{t eps_j}psi-psi)/t exists in L2},
  P_j psi=i*hbar*lim_{t->0}(T_{t eps_j}psi-psi)/t.          (G17)

Thus the original minimal momentum has a uniquely specified selfadjoint
closure. This is a constant-drift specialization of the abstract proof
under its explicitly verified premises; it is not a positive-viscosity
NSE specialization and is not a claim that a ready Lean theorem supplies
the complete momentum construction.

Pointwise evaluation gives the whole-space bounded-operator identities

  T_y T_z=T_{y+z},
  M_p M_r=M_{p+r},
  T_y M_p=exp(-i*p.y/hbar)*M_p T_y.                       (G18)

The last identity is the exact Weyl commutation relation with the
document's sign convention. It is an identity of bounded unitaries,
so no unbounded product-domain convention is needed for (G18).

With g_sigma(q)=(2*pi*sigma^2)^(-d/4)*exp(-|q|^2/(4*sigma^2)),

  Psi_{N,a;sigma,p}=T_{a_N}M_p g_sigma
                 =exp(-i*p.a_N/hbar)*M_p T_{a_N}g_sigma. (G19)

Equations (G17)--(G19) give ordinary finite-dimensional canonical quantum
kinematics for the explicit states. They do not assert any additional
covariance or expectation-value closure of the nonlinear NSE drift.

14.E.T Fourier traces and exact initial Gaussian consistency.

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI39]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP40; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML02, ML05, ML14, ML49, ML50, ML52--ML57; MT02, MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD02, AD04, AD18.
  APPLICATION: Constant Fourier projection kernels supply the nonlinear trace, coefficient-space
               harmonicity and the pointwise derivative-kernel trace; Gaussian covariance supplies
               the exact initial moments.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

Notation.
  eps_j is the j-th standard coordinate vector of R^{d_N}.
  e_j=I_N(eps_j) is the corresponding real solenoidal Fourier field.
  A_N is the finite nonnegative Laplacian matrix; b_N(q)=-nu*A_N*q-B_N(q,q).
  Lap_q denotes the ordinary componentwise Laplacian in coefficient space.
  Lap_x denotes the physical periodic Laplacian. These operators are distinct.

THEOREM [R12T-A: NONLINEAR COORDINATE TRACE].
  sum_j B_N(eps_j,eps_j)=0,
  forall component l: sum_j C_{l j j}=0.                 (R12T.1)

Proof.
The actual full-cutoff diagonal projection kernel from Section3.A is
  K_N(x)=sum_j e_j(x) tensor e_j(x),
and K_N is independent of x. In physical component alpha,
  sum_beta partial_beta K_{N,alpha beta}
    =sum_j [((e_j.nabla)e_j)_alpha+e_{j,alpha} div e_j]
    =sum_j ((e_j.nabla)e_j)_alpha,
because every e_j is solenoidal. The left side is zero. Applying the
linear Galerkin/Leray projection and the coordinate isometry proves
R12T.1. This is a full quadratic trace identity; diagonal energy
cancellation alone would not imply it for an arbitrary bilinear map.

Since each component of b_N is a linear polynomial plus a homogeneous
quadratic polynomial,
  Lap_q b_{N,l}(q)=-2*sum_j C_{l j j}=0.                 (R12T.2)
Thus the coefficient-space drift is componentwise harmonic. This is an
identity for the specified finite Fourier drift, not an additional
equation imposed on a continuum velocity field.

THEOREM [R12T-B: POINTWISE GRADIENT-KERNEL TRACE].
  forall x in T^3: sum_j |nabla e_j(x)|_F^2=Tr(A_N).
Consequently, with g_N=sqrt(Tr(A_N)),
  ell_N(q)<=g_N*|q|,
  |ell_N(q)-ell_N(r)|<=g_N*|q-r|.                       (R12T.3)

Proof.
For a frequency pair {k,-k} and a unit real polarization p perpendicular
to k, the normalized fields are sqrt(2)*p*cos(2*pi*k.x) and
sqrt(2)*p*sin(2*pi*k.x). Their squared Frobenius-gradient norms sum to
  2*(4*pi^2*|k|^2)*(sin^2+cos^2)=2*(4*pi^2*|k|^2).
This equals the sum of their two Laplacian eigenvalues. Sum over both
transverse polarizations and all frequency pairs; constant fields have
zero gradient and zero eigenvalue. The pointwise sum is unchanged by
an orthogonal change of the real basis. Therefore it equals Tr(A_N)
for the same full finite Fourier space in every permitted coordinate
basis.

At each x, finite-dimensional Cauchy--Schwarz gives
  |sum_j q_j*nabla e_j(x)|_F
    <=|q|*(sum_j |nabla e_j(x)|_F^2)^(1/2)=g_N*|q|.
Take the spatial supremum. Apply the same estimate to q-r and use the
reverse norm triangle inequality to obtain the Lipschitz inequality.

The constant is explicitly
  g_N^2=Tr(A_N)=8*pi^2*sum_{0<|k|<=N}|k|^2,
  g_N=sqrt(kappa_N/nu).                                  (R12T.4)
It improves the earlier valid bound Gamma_N because
  g_N^2=sum_j ||nabla e_j||_2^2
       <=sum_j ||nabla e_j||_infinity^2=Gamma_N^2.
For the unrotated normalized sine/cosine polarization basis,
  Gamma_N^2=2*Tr(A_N), hence g_N=Gamma_N/sqrt(2).
This last ratio is basis-specific; g_N<=Gamma_N is basis-independent.
No claim of optimality of g_N is required.

THEOREM [R12T-C: EXACT ISOTROPIC GAUSSIAN DRIFT AVERAGE].
Let mu be the normal distribution on coefficient space with mean c and
covariance sigma^2*Id, sigma>0. Its moments satisfy
  integral q dmu=c,
  integral (q-c)_j*(q-c)_k dmu=sigma^2*delta_{jk}.
Then
  integral B_N(q,q)dmu=B_N(c,c),
  integral b_N(q)dmu=b_N(c).                              (R12T.5)

Proof.
Write q=c+z and expand
  B_N(q,q)=B_N(c,c)+B_N(c,z)+B_N(z,c)+B_N(z,z).
The two linear terms have zero average. The quadratic average is
  integral B_N(z,z)dmu
    =sigma^2*sum_j B_N(eps_j,eps_j)=0
by R12T.1. The linear viscous term averages to -nu*A_N*c.
Every polynomial integral here is absolutely integrable for the
explicit Gaussian density. The calculation holds for every sigma>0.

THEOREM [R12T-D: INITIAL CENTROID DERIVATIVE].
For the Gaussian initial density centered at a_N, define
  m_N(t)=integral Phi_N^t(q) dmu_{N,a}(q).
Then
  m_N(0)=a_N,
  m_N'(0)=b_N(a_N).                                      (R12T.6)

Proof.
For t in any fixed compact neighborhood of zero, the two-sided energy
bounds give |Phi_N^t(q)|<=exp(nu*lambda_max*|t|)|q|.
The finite polynomial drift obeys
  |b_N(v)|<=nu*||A_N||*|v|+beta_N*|v|^2.
Thus the time derivative b_N(Phi_N^t(q)) is dominated on that
neighborhood by C_N*(|q|+|q|^2), which is integrable against the
Gaussian probability measure. Differentiation under the integral is
therefore justified, giving m_N'(0)=integral b_N(q)dmu=b_N(a_N).
The same argument gives m_N'(t)=integral b_N(Phi_N^t(q))dmu at every
finite t, without identifying that expectation with b_N(m_N(t)).

THEOREM [R12T-E: GAUSSIAN CANONICAL HAMILTONIAN EXPECTATION].
Let
  Psi(q)=(2*pi*sigma^2)^(-d_N/4)
          *exp(-|q-a_N|^2/(4*sigma^2))
          *exp(i*p.(q-a_N)/hbar),
with real p in R^{d_N}. The Gaussian is in the actual domain of H_N.
Then
  <Psi,H_N Psi>=p.b_N(a_N).                              (R12T.7)

Proof.
Write Psi=exp(i*p.(q-a_N)/hbar)*g(q) with g real. The product rule gives
  H_N Psi=exp(i*p.(q-a_N)/hbar)
            [ (p.b_N(q))*g(q)
              -i*hbar*(b_N.nabla g+(div b_N)*g/2) ].
The imaginary expectation term is
  -i*hbar/2 * integral div(b_N*g^2)dq=0.
This integration by parts is legitimate because b_N is polynomial and
g is Schwartz. Equivalently, approximate by compact smooth cutoffs and
use the weighted polynomial tails proved in the Gaussian-domain step.
The remaining term is p.integral b_N(q)dmu=p.b_N(a_N), by R12T.5.
For p=0 the expectation is zero.

ADDITIONAL EXACT INITIAL OBSERVABLES.
Let W_{3,N}=(Id+A_N)^3, represented by diag((1+lambda_j)^3) in the
chosen eigenbasis. The same covariance gives
  <Psi,E_{3,N}Psi>
    =e_{3,N}(a_N)+sigma^2*Tr(W_{3,N}).                   (R12T.8)
For E0(q)=|q|^2/2,
  <Psi,M_E0 Psi>=|a_N|^2/2+d_N*sigma^2/2,
  d/dt|_{t=0}<U_N(t)Psi,M_E0 U_N(t)Psi>
    =-nu*[a_N.A_N*a_N+sigma^2*Tr(A_N)].                  (R12T.9)
The last identity uses the exact finite energy law and differentiation
under the Gaussian integral, dominated by a constant times |q|^2.

SCOPE.
  R12T.6 is an exact initial centroid derivative.
  No later-time Gaussian invariance or nonlinear centroid closure is asserted.
  R12T.2 concerns Lap_q of the coefficient drift; it does not replace
    the physical NSE equation or resolve any universal regularity bound.

14.F ROUND 13: WEIGHTED UNITARY RESOLVENT STEPS AND EXACT ERROR BOUNDS

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI40]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP41, CP42, CP43; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML11--ML16, ML20--ML24, ML37--ML44, ML50, ML51, ML58; MT06.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD07, AD18, AD19.
  APPLICATION: Actual resolvent domains and weighted finite-core graph limits prove Cayley
               contraction; two Banach-valued integrations by parts yield the exact cubic local
               defect and quadratic global error.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

NOTATION

Fix N>=1, nu>0 and hbar>0. Let
  E_N=R^{d_N},
  Hilbert_N=L2(E_N,dq;C),
  D_N=C_c^infinity(E_N;C),
  H=H_N=closure(H_{N,min}),
  G=-(i/hbar)H,
  U(t)=U_N(t).
H is the actual selfadjoint operator of Section6. On D_N,
  G phi=-b_N.nabla phi-(div b_N)phi/2.
The inner product is linear in its second argument.
The finite matrix A_N is the viscous Laplacian matrix; it is not H.

For every integer m>=0, set
  weight_m(q)=(1+|q|^2)^m,
  Hilbert_N^[m]=L2(E_N,weight_m(q)dq;C),
  ||psi||_[m]^2=integral weight_m(q)|psi(q)|^2 dq.
Thus ||psi||_[0] is the ordinary Hilbert norm. These weighted state norms
are not spatial Sobolev norms of the fluid field.

The inclusion Hilbert_N^[m] -> Hilbert_N is continuous, with norm<=1.
Multiplication J_m psi=weight_m^(1/2) psi is an onto isometry from
Hilbert_N^[m] to Hilbert_N, with inverse weight_m^(-1/2) multiplication.
Both weights are smooth and strictly positive. They map D_N onto D_N.
Consequently Hilbert_N^[m] is complete and D_N is dense in it, by the
ordinary L2 density already proved at CP08.

14.F.1. Exact affine resolvent and Cayley transform.

For h in R\{0}, define
  S_h=(I+i*h*H/(2*hbar))^(-1),
  C_h=2*S_h-I.
Set S_0=C_0=I.
The inverse in this definition is the actual bounded inverse supplied by
Section6, not a formal inverse of an unspecified operator.

Indeed, with z_h=2*i*hbar/h,
  I+i*h*H/(2*hbar)=(i*h/(2*hbar))*(H-z_h),
  S_h=(-2*i*hbar/h)*R_{z_h}.                              (C1)
For h!=0, S_h maps Hilbert_N into D(H), and
  (I+i*h*H/(2*hbar))S_h=I,
  S_h(I+i*h*H/(2*hbar))=I on D(H).

For h>0, the upper-half-plane resolvent formula becomes
  S_h psi=(2/h) integral_0^infinity exp(-2*s/h)U(s)psi ds. (C2)
The integral is vectorwise. Its scalar kernel is positive and has mass one.
For h<0 the corresponding formula has U(-s) and |h| in place of U(s)
and h. The ordinary Hilbert norm satisfies ||S_h||<=1 for all real h.

For y=S_h x, the equation x=y+i*h*H*y/(2*hbar) gives
  C_h x=y-i*h*H*y/(2*hbar).
Since <y,H*y> is real,
  ||y+i*h*H*y/(2*hbar)||_[0]^2
    =||y-i*h*H*y/(2*hbar)||_[0]^2.
Therefore ||C_h x||_[0]=||x||_[0].

For any x, put v=S_{-h}x. Then
  x=(I-i*h*H/(2*hbar))v,
  C_{-h}x=(I+i*h*H/(2*hbar))v,
so S_h C_{-h}x=v and C_h C_{-h}x=x. Reversing h gives the opposite
inverse identity. Hence
  C_h^*=C_{-h},
  C_h^*C_h=C_hC_h^*=I.                                   (C3)
In particular every finite power C_h^n is unitary in the ordinary Hilbert
space. The notation
  C_h=(I-i*h*H/(2*hbar))(I+i*h*H/(2*hbar))^(-1)
is well defined because S_h has range in D(H).

SOURCES: CP10; ML20--ML24, ML37--ML42. ML16 can package the proved
surjective isometry. No bounded-operator replacement of H is made.

14.F.2. Exact weighted forward dynamics.

The Jacobian change of variables and the finite NSE energy identity give
  ||U(t)psi||_[m]^2
    =integral weight_m(Phi_N^t(q))|psi(q)|^2 dq
    <=||psi||_[m]^2,    t>=0.                              (C4)
This initially follows for test representatives and then for every state
in Hilbert_N^[m] by the same nonnegative change-of-variables formula.

For a compact time interval, U(t)phi and all its time derivatives, with
phi in D_N, have a common compact spatial support. The explicit smooth
pullback therefore gives continuity and strong differentiation in every
weighted norm, not merely the ordinary norm.
Weighted density and (C4) extend strong right continuity at zero to all
psi in Hilbert_N^[m], and the semigroup law extends it to all t>=0.

For phi in D_N, compact-support integration by parts yields
  2*Re<phi,G phi>_[m]
    =integral b_N(q).nabla weight_m(q)|phi(q)|^2 dq
    =-2*m*nu integral (1+|q|^2)^(m-1)
          (q.A_N q)|phi(q)|^2 dq.
Thus
  Re<phi,G phi>_[m]<=0.                                    (C5)
At m=0 the integrand coefficient is zero and the identity agrees with
ordinary skew symmetry. Every displayed product is integrable by smooth
compact support.

The full calculation before cancellation is
  2*Re<phi,G phi>_[m]
    =-integral weight_m*b_N.nabla|phi|^2
       -integral weight_m*(div b_N)|phi|^2.
Using div(weight_m*b_N)=b_N.nabla weight_m+weight_m*div b_N
leaves exactly (C5), with no missing Jacobian/divergence term.

SOURCES: CP04, CP09; ML11--ML15, ML50, ML51; MT06 through the exact
coordinate/energy adapter. The weighted Hilbert-space realization is a
new explicit adapter; no weighted Cayley theorem is asserted available.

14.F.3. Weighted resolvents and weighted Cayley contraction.

For h>0 and psi in Hilbert_N^[m], the right side of (C2) is also a
Bochner integral in the complete weighted space. Equation (C4) and the
mass-one kernel give
  ||S_h psi||_[m]<=||psi||_[m].                             (C6)
The continuous inclusion into Hilbert_N commutes with the integral, so
this weighted integral is the same state as the actual S_h of (C1).

The estimate ||S_h||<=1 alone would not imply contraction of 2*S_h-I.
The following domain argument supplies the missing conclusion.

For phi in D_N and R>=0, define the finite-time core integral
  y_R=(2/h) integral_0^R exp(-2*s/h)U(s)phi ds.
The Section6 compact smooth support argument gives y_R in D_N. Its
finite-time identity is
  (I-h*G/2)y_R=phi-exp(-2*R/h)U(R)phi.                     (C7)
In every weighted norm,
  y_R -> y=S_h phi,
  G y_R -> (2/h)(y-phi),
because (C4) controls the exponentially decaying terminal term.

For every R, (C5) gives
  ||y_R+h*G y_R/2||_[m]^2
    -||y_R-h*G y_R/2||_[m]^2
      =2*h*Re<y_R,G y_R>_[m]<=0.
Taking the two weighted limits yields
  ||2*S_h phi-phi||_[m]<=||phi||_[m].
Consequently
  ||C_h psi||_[m]<=||psi||_[m],
  h>0, psi in Hilbert_N^[m].                               (C8)
The extension from D_N uses weighted density. It agrees with the original
unweighted bounded operator because the weighted inclusion is continuous.
No assertion that G is a bounded operator on Hilbert_N^[m] is used.

For later time integrals, the dependence on h is explicit. On compact
subintervals of h>0, dominated convergence in (C2) gives strong weighted
continuity of h |-> S_h. At h=0,
  S_h psi-psi
    =(2/h)integral_0^infinity exp(-2*s/h)(U(s)psi-psi)ds.
Given epsilon>0, choose delta>0 with ||U(s)psi-psi||_[m]<epsilon for
0<=s<=delta. Splitting the integral at delta gives
  ||S_h psi-psi||_[m]
    <=epsilon+2||psi||_[m]exp(-2*delta/h) ->epsilon.
Thus S_h psi->psi and C_h psi->psi as h decreases to zero. For fixed
integer n>=1,
  t |-> C_{t/n}^n psi
is strongly continuous in Hilbert_N^[m] on [0,infinity). The proof uses
the finite product and the contraction bound (C8).

SOURCES: ML37--ML44, ML50, ML51. Bounded inclusion commutation is ML42.
The domain step uses the actual finite-time C_c^infinity integrals; it
cannot be replaced by a merely formal dissipativity calculation.

14.F.4. Exact trapezoid defect and the local cubic bound.

The polynomial differential operator Hmin sends D_N into D_N. Hence
D_N is contained in every D(H^k), and U(s) commutes with H^k there.
For phi in D_N the orbit is three times strongly differentiable in
every weighted norm, with
  d^3 U(s)phi/ds^3=G^3 U(s)phi=U(s)G^3 phi.

For h>0, define the actual defect
  Delta_h(phi)
    =(I-h*G/2)(U(h)-C_h)phi.
Both states in the parenthesis belong to D(H): U(h)phi is a test state,
and C_h phi=2*S_h phi-phi lies in D(H). Thus the displayed operator is
defined. The affine inverse identity gives
  Delta_h(phi)
    =U(h)phi-phi-(h/2)(G U(h)phi+G phi)
    =integral_0^h U'(s)phi ds
       -(h/2)(U'(0)phi+U'(h)phi).

Two integrations by parts with the scalar polynomial s(h-s) give
  Delta_h(phi)
    =-(1/2)integral_0^h s(h-s)U'''(s)phi ds.              (C9)
Explicitly, for any C2 Banach-valued f,
  integral_0^h s(h-s)f''(s)ds
    =h[f(h)+f(0)]-2 integral_0^h f(s)ds;
apply this identity to f(s)=U'(s)phi. Boundary terms at s=0,h
vanish in the first integration. All derivatives and finite integrals
exist in the weighted Hilbert space.

By (C4),
  ||Delta_h(phi)||_[m]
    <=(1/2)integral_0^h s(h-s)||G^3 phi||_[m]ds
    =(h^3/12)||G^3 phi||_[m].
Since S_h=(I-h*G/2)^(-1), equation (C6) yields
  ||(U(h)-C_h)phi||_[m]
    <=h^3/(12*hbar^3)*||H^3 phi||_[m].                   (C10)
At h=0 the difference is zero.

SOURCES: ML42--ML44 and ML58 /
intervalIntegral.integral_smul_deriv_eq_deriv_smul_of_hasDerivAt.
The latter is applied twice with the displayed scalar polynomial weights.
Equation (C9) is a new project theorem; the exact source header and all
inherited Banach/scalar hypotheses are recorded in Section18.6.

14.F.5. Global finite-product error and strong convergence.

For t>=0 and n>=1, put h=t/n and
  V_n(t)=C_{t/n}^n.
The finite telescoping identity gives
  V_n(t)-U(t)
    =sum_{k=0}^{n-1} C_h^(n-1-k)(C_h-U(h))U(kh).
For phi in D_N, apply (C8) to the left factors and (C10) to the test
vectors U(kh)phi. Commutation and (C4) give
  ||H^3 U(kh)phi||_[m]
    =||U(kh)H^3 phi||_[m]<=||H^3 phi||_[m].
Therefore
  ||V_n(t)phi-U(t)phi||_[m]
    <=t^3/(12*hbar^3*n^2)*||H^3 phi||_[m].               (C11)
The bound is uniform for 0<=t<=T after replacing t^3 by T^3.

For arbitrary psi in Hilbert_N^[m], choose phi in D_N. Contractions give
  sup_{0<=t<=T}||V_n(t)psi-U(t)psi||_[m]
    <=2||psi-phi||_[m]
       +T^3/(12*hbar^3*n^2)||H^3 phi||_[m].
First choose phi close to psi, then let n tend to infinity. This proves
  sup_{0<=t<=T}||V_n(t)psi-U(t)psi||_[m] ->0.              (C12)
No rate is asserted for a general state without a third graph bound.

More generally, (C11) holds whenever psi in D(H^3) admits phi_j in D_N
with
  ||phi_j-psi||_[m]+||H^3 phi_j-H^3 psi||_[m] ->0.         (C13)
Indeed, pass to the limit in (C11), using (C8) and (C4). This is the
exact weighted third-graph approximation premise. The Gaussian/Schwartz
adapter CP39 derives (C13), so Gaussian instances require no additional
unresolved domain witness. The core theorem (C11) is independent of CP39.

V_n(t) is a unitary finite operator product for each t. A group law in
t for V_n is not claimed. Equation (C12) identifies its limit with the
already constructed exact unitary group U.

14.G.1. Observable domains and the weighted comparison lemma.

Retain
  e3_N(q)=||I_N(q)||H3^2,
  w_N=(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(3/2),
  ell_N(q)=||nabla I_N(q)||_infinity.
Choose an explicit g_N>=0 satisfying ell_N(q)<=g_N|q| for every q.
The CP40 derivative-kernel identity supplies the preferred exact value
  g_N=sqrt(Tr(A_N))
     =sqrt(8*pi^2*sum_{0<|k|<=N}|k|^2).                  (C14)
The earlier Gamma_N from Section8.4 also supplies a valid value;
C_emb*w_N is another valid, less purely finite-cutoff choice.

Pointwise,
  0<=e3_N(q)<=w_N^2|q|^2<=w_N^2*weight_1(q),
  0<=ell_N(q)<=g_N|q|<=(g_N/2)*weight_1(q).               (C15)
For any psi in Hilbert_N^[2],
  integral e3_N(q)^2 |psi(q)|^2 dq
    <=w_N^4||psi||_[2]^2<infinity.
Thus psi lies in the maximal domain of E3_N=M_e3_N. Similarly, a state
in Hilbert_N^[1] lies in the maximal domain of L_N=M_ell_N.
Both U(t) and V_n(t) preserve these spaces for t>=0 by (C4),(C8).

Let f be real measurable with |f(q)|<=c*weight_1(q), c>=0. For phi,psi
in Hilbert_N^[1], the finite quadratic integrals satisfy
  |integral f(q)(|phi(q)|^2-|psi(q)|^2)dq|
    <=c*(||phi||_[1]+||psi||_[1])*||phi-psi||_[1].        (C16)
The proof uses
  ||phi|^2-|psi|^2|<=|phi-psi|(|phi|+|psi|)
and weighted L2 Cauchy--Schwarz. If the vectors are in the maximal
multiplier domains, these integrals are their actual Hilbert expectations.

14.G.2. Explicit unbounded-observable error coefficients.

Let psi be a normalized test state, or a normalized Gaussian state with
the CP39 weighted graph approximation. In particular,
  psi in Hilbert_N^[2],
  ||H^3 psi||_[1]<infinity,
and (C11) is valid in the m=1 norm. Define
  Xi_N(psi)=||psi||_[1]*||H^3 psi||_[1].

Let
  Q^E_N(t;psi)=<U(t)psi,E3_N U(t)psi>,
  Q^L_N(t;psi)=<U(t)psi,L_N U(t)psi>,
  Q^{E,n}_N(t;psi)=<V_n(t)psi,E3_N V_n(t)psi>,
  Q^{L,n}_N(t;psi)=<V_n(t)psi,L_N V_n(t)psi>.
Every vector is normalized in the ordinary Hilbert norm. The preceding
domain proof applies before any expectation formula is used.

Equations (C4),(C8),(C11),(C15),(C16) imply
  |Q^{E,n}_N(t;psi)-Q^E_N(t;psi)|
    <=w_N^2*t^3/(6*hbar^3*n^2)*Xi_N(psi),               (C17)
  |Q^{L,n}_N(t;psi)-Q^L_N(t;psi)|
    <=g_N*t^3/(12*hbar^3*n^2)*Xi_N(psi).                (C18)
The factor in (C17) is 2*w_N^2 times the state error; the factor in
(C18) is g_N times that error. There is no missing square or norm factor.

The strong weighted continuity from Section14.F.3 and the quadratic
comparison lemma make both approximate observable functions continuous
on [0,T]. Thus time integration is legitimate, and
  |integral_0^T Q^{L,n}_N(t;psi)dt
       -integral_0^T Q^L_N(t;psi)dt|
    <=g_N*T^4/(48*hbar^3*n^2)*Xi_N(psi).                (C19)
The integral of t^3 is T^4/4. Using an arbitrary fixed n for the whole
curve is part of this assertion.

14.G.3. Prescribed finite step count without a regularity bound.

Choose one of the explicit profile families already constructed:
  F=compact canonical packets of Section14.B; or
  F=canonical Gaussian packets of CP39.
For either family, write its actual state as Psi^F_{N,a}. The family is
fixed before a and T are quantified. Define the finite nonnegative data
  K^E_{N,a,T}
    =w_N^2*T^3/(6*hbar^3)*Xi_N(Psi^F_{N,a}),
  K^L_{N,a,T}
    =g_N*T^4/(48*hbar^3)*Xi_N(Psi^F_{N,a}),
  K^rat_{N,a,T}=max(K^E_{N,a,T},K^L_{N,a,T}),
  delta_N=1/(N+1),
  n_{N,a,T}
    =max(1, ceil_N(sqrt((N+1)*K^rat_{N,a,T}))).           (C20)
Here ceil_N denotes the natural-number ceiling of a nonnegative real.
The finite derivatives of the specified state and the finite polynomial
coefficients determine Xi_N. No G3, FB, unknown continuum solution, or
cutoff-uniform estimate is an input to (C20).

Since n_{N,a,T}>=1 and
  n_{N,a,T}^2>=(N+1)*K^rat_{N,a,T},
equations (C17)--(C19) give
  sup_{0<=t<=T}|Q^{E,n_{N,a,T}}_N(t;Psi^F)-Q^E_N(t;Psi^F)|
    <=delta_N,
  |integral_0^T Q^{L,n_{N,a,T}}_N(t;Psi^F)dt
        -integral_0^T Q^L_N(t;Psi^F)dt|
    <=delta_N.                                            (C21)
If K^rat=0, the errors are zero and the max with 1 remains well defined.

For the real canonical profiles, H_N/hbar and the profiles are independent
of hbar. Hence Xi_N/hbar^3, and therefore (C20), are independent of hbar.
This statement does not apply without qualification to a profile whose
phase itself depends on hbar.

14.G.4. Exact finite-product regularity predicates.

For the chosen family F, define
  Q^E_{rat,N,a,T}(t)
    =Q^{E,n_{N,a,T}}_N(t;Psi^F_{N,a}),
  Q^L_{rat,N,a,T}(t)
    =Q^{L,n_{N,a,T}}_N(t;Psi^F_{N,a}).
The parameter T remains in the notation: different horizons may prescribe
different step counts and hence different finite-product curves.

  QREG_rat^F(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall smooth divergence-free a, forall finite T>0,
      exists finite K>=0,
        forall N>=1, forall t in [0,T], Q^E_{rat,N,a,T}(t)<=K.

  QLIP_rat^F(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall smooth divergence-free a, forall finite T>0,
      exists finite L>=0,
        forall N>=1, integral_0^T Q^L_{rat,N,a,T}(t)dt<=L.

Let QREG_F and QLIP_F denote the corresponding exact-U predicates for
the same chosen profile family. Since delta_N<=1/2 for N>=1, (C21) gives
  QREG_rat^F <=> QREG_F,
  QLIP_rat^F <=> QLIP_F.                                  (C22)
Proof in each direction: add 1/2 to the asserted finite common bound.
No interchange of a limit, supremum or existential witness is required.

The already derived family-specific equivalences now yield
  G3(nu) <=> QREG_rat^F(nu,hbar)
         <=> QLIP_rat^F(nu,hbar).                         (C23)
For F=compact use CP34; for F=Gaussian use CP38 and the explicit CP39
moment conditions. Compose with CP27 to retain the original FB, LIP,
QREG and QLIP conclusions.

These criteria involve finitely many bounded resolvent compositions for
each fixed (N,a,T,t). They do not constitute a finite witness for the
universal bound. No numerical inverse solver, finite evaluation oracle,
complexity bound or independently checked inverse certificate is supplied.
The underlying exact quantum dynamics remains the actual U_N(t).

14.G.5. Conditional continuum observables for the finite products.

Assume G3(nu). For the canonical compact family, Section14.C supplies
the continuum comparison errors E^E_N and E^L_N with order O(N^(-1)).
For the canonical Gaussian family, the moment theorem and the same

  sup_{0<=t<=T}|Q^E_{rat,N,a,T}(t)-||u(t)||H3^2|

Thus both errors are O(N^(-1)) on each fixed finite interval under the
explicit regularity hypothesis. The prescribed step count remains
independent of the unknown cutoff-uniform regularity constants.

14.H.1 ACTUAL HAMILTONIAN POWERS AS POLYNOMIALS

Define the derivation on coefficient polynomials

  (D P)(z)=b(a+z).nabla_z P(z),

and initially write the multiplication factor as

  V(z)=c/2-b(a+z).z/(2*tau).

Put

  P_0=1,
  P_{r+1}=D P_r+V P_r.                                (R15.2)

THEOREM [R15-A: EXACT POLYNOMIAL ACTION].
For every integer r>=0,

  H^r psi(q)=(-i*hbar)^r P_r(q-a)*psi(q).               (R15.3)

Proof.
The derivative of psi is
  partial_j psi(q)=-(q_j-a_j)/(2*tau)*psi(q).
For any polynomial P, the ordinary product rule gives
  H(P(q-a)psi(q))
    =-i*hbar*[D P(q-a)+V(q-a)P(q-a)]psi(q).
Both sides are the actual H action by the CP39 Schwartz-domain theorem.
Induct from P_0=1. Every intermediate polynomial-Gaussian state is
Schwartz, so the iteration is an equality of actual operator powers.

The first three polynomials have the finite closed expressions

  P_1=V,
  P_2=D V+V^2,
  P_3=D^2 V+3*V*(D V)+V^3.                            (R15.4)

Indeed, D is a derivation, so D(V^2)=2V(DV).
The expression D^2 V is entirely finite:

  D^2 V=sum_{i,j} b_i(a+z)*(partial_i b_j)(a+z)
                         *(partial_j V)(z)
         +sum_{i,j} b_i(a+z)*b_j(a+z)
                         *(partial_i partial_j V)(z).

Thus evaluating P_3 requires only finite polynomial addition,
multiplication and ordinary first/second polynomial derivatives.


14.H.2 DEGREE REDUCTION FROM THE ACTUAL NSE ENERGY IDENTITY

For a general quadratic drift with constant divergence, V has degree
at most three. Induction in (R15.2) gives

  degree P_r <=3r.                                    (R15.5)

This remains a valid conservative bound for the present NSE drift.
The actual finite energy identity yields a stronger statement. Since
q=a+z,

  b(a+z).z=b(q).q-b(q).a
            =-nu*q.A*q-a.b(q).

Consequently V has the explicit quadratic representative

  V(z)=c/2+[nu*(a+z).A*(a+z)+a.b(a+z)]/(2*tau).       (R15.6)

The right side has degree <=2. It can be used as the polynomial
definition of V; its pointwise equality to the Gaussian derivative
factor follows from the exact energy identity. This avoids treating
the cancellation of cubic coefficients as an additional assumption.

Use (R15.6) as the polynomial definition of V. The displayed equality
is then an equality of evaluated functions justified by the energy
identity; no additional polynomial-function extensionality endpoint
is required by this selected formal route.

THEOREM [R15-B: ACTUAL NSE DEGREE BOUND].
For every integer r>=0,

  degree P_r<=2r.                                     (R15.7)

Proof.
If degree P<=K, each partial derivative has degree <=K-1 whenever
nonzero. Multiplication by a quadratic b_i raises this to at most K+1.
Multiplication by V raises degree to at most K+2. Induction from the
constant P_0 gives (R15.7). The zero polynomial satisfies every upper
bound, so no degree(-infinity) convention is needed in the contract:
equivalently, every nonzero coefficient of P_r has total exponent <=2r.

This strengthening uses only the pointwise finite energy identity.
No bound on a, no G3 hypothesis, and no continuum solution enter it.


14.H.3 EXPLICIT FINITE COEFFICIENT RECURRENCE

For alpha=(alpha_1,...,alpha_d) in N^d write
  |alpha|=sum_i alpha_i,
  z^alpha=product_i z_i^(alpha_i),
  eps_i=(0,...,1,...,0).
Let A_K={alpha in {0,...,K}^d:|alpha|<=K}; this is a finite set.

Write the actual shifted drift and quadratic multiplier as

  b_i(a+z)=sum_{beta in A_2} b_{i,beta} z^beta,
  V(z)=sum_{delta in A_2} v_delta z^delta,
  P_r(z)=sum_{alpha in A_{2r}} c_{r,alpha} z^alpha.

Declare c_{r,alpha}=0 outside A_{2r}. Then c_{0,0}=1 and all
other c_{0,alpha}=0. For gamma in A_{2r+2},

  c_{r+1,gamma}
    =sum_i sum_{beta in A_2, alpha in A_{2r}, beta+alpha=gamma}
         b_{i,beta}*(alpha_i+1)*c_{r,alpha+eps_i}
      +sum_{delta in A_2, alpha in A_{2r}, delta+alpha=gamma}
         v_delta*c_{r,alpha}.                          (R15.8)

This is a finite recurrence in actual finite real coefficients. The
first term is the coefficient formula for a polynomial partial
derivative followed by finite convolution; the second is ordinary
finite convolution. The apparent boundary alpha+eps_i outside A_{2r}
contributes zero by the stated convention.

If the original coordinate drift is
  b_i(q)=-nu*sum_j A_ij q_j-sum_{j,k} C_ijk q_j q_k,
its shifted coefficients are obtained by expanding q_j=a_j+z_j.
In particular:
  constant coefficient: b_i(a);
  z_j coefficient: -nu*A_ij-sum_k(C_ijk+C_ikj)*a_k;
  z_j^2 coefficient: -C_ijj;
  z_j*z_k coefficient, j<k: -(C_ijk+C_ikj).
No symmetry of C in its last two indices is assumed.

Substitution into (R15.6) gives the coefficients v_delta by finite
addition/multiplication. No flow evaluation, inverse, differential
operator norm or unknown analytic witness is an input to (R15.8).


14.H.4 ALL REQUIRED GAUSSIAN MONOMIAL MOMENTS

Define the nonnegative integer odd product

  O(0)=1,
  O(k)=product_{j=1}^k (2j-1),       k>=1.

This convention replaces the notation (-1)!! by an empty product.
For gamma in N^d define the exact scalar moment table

  m_gamma(tau)=0,
    if at least one gamma_i is odd;

  m_gamma(tau)=tau^(|gamma|/2)*product_i O(gamma_i/2),
    if every gamma_i is even.                          (R15.9)

All exponents in the second line are natural numbers.

THEOREM [R15-C: FINITE MOMENT TABLE].
  E[Z^gamma]=m_gamma(tau),   Z~N(0,tau*Id).

Proof.
The normalized one-dimensional Gaussian density rho_tau satisfies
  rho_tau'(x)=-(x/tau)rho_tau(x).
Every polynomial times rho_tau is absolutely integrable, and every
polynomial times rho_tau tends to zero at both ends. Odd moments vanish
by reflection. Integration by parts gives, for every n>=0,
  integral x^(n+2)rho_tau(x)dx
    =tau*(n+1)*integral x^n rho_tau(x)dx.
Starting from the normalized zeroth moment, this yields
  E[X^(2k)]=tau^k O(k).
Finite product integration gives (R15.9) for the actual Euclidean
Gaussian. Integrability is supplied before product factorization by
ML53 and ML55; ML52 supplies normalization, ML50 the IBP identity,
ML56 the finite product integral, and ML57 the Euclidean volume adapter.

Define the finite weighted moment table

  M_gamma(a,tau)
    =(1+|a|^2)m_gamma
      +2*sum_i a_i*m_{gamma+eps_i}
      +sum_i m_{gamma+2eps_i}.                         (R15.10)

Expanding 1+|a+Z|^2 gives
  M_gamma=E[(1+|a+Z|^2)Z^gamma].
Some off-diagonal weighted moments can have either sign; no positivity
claim is made about an individual M_gamma.


14.H.5 EXACT FINITE WEIGHTED GRAPH NORMS

For the real Gaussian set

  S_r(a,tau)=sum_{alpha,beta in A_{2r}}
       c_{r,alpha}*c_{r,beta}*M_{alpha+beta}(a,tau).

By finite expansion and actual polynomial-Gaussian integrability,

  S_r=E[(1+|a+Z|^2)P_r(Z)^2]>=0.                      (R15.11)

THEOREM [R15-D: EXACT FINITE GRAPH EVALUATOR].
For every integer r>=0,

  ||H^r psi||_[1]^2=hbar^(2r)*S_r,
  ||H^r psi||_[1]=hbar^r*sqrt(S_r).                    (R15.12)

Proof.
Insert (R15.3), use |(-i*hbar)^r|=hbar^r, and expand the finite
polynomial square. Positivity hbar>0 and (R15.11) identify the unique
nonnegative square roots. There is no interchange of infinite sums.

Every index alpha+beta has degree <=4r. The extra two powers in
(R15.10) show that only moments of total degree <=4r+2 are needed.
The general quadratic-drift bound (R15.5) instead requires degree
<=6r+2. In particular:

  power r        actual NSE moment degree        generic degree bound
     0                      2                             2
     1                      6                             8
     2                     10                            14
     3                     14                            20

Put

  W=1+|a|^2+d*tau.

Then S_0=W>=1, and the requested graph quantities are

  X=||psi||_[1]=sqrt(W),
  D2=||H^2 psi||_[1]=hbar^2*sqrt(S_2),
  D3=||H^3 psi||_[1]=hbar^3*sqrt(S_3),
  Xi_N(psi)/hbar^3=sqrt(W*S_3).                        (R15.13)

For the combination used by a subsequent residual-path construction,

  T^3*D3/(12*hbar^3)+T^2*D2/(8*hbar^2)
    =T^3*sqrt(S_3)/12+T^2*sqrt(S_2)/8.                 (R15.14)

Thus X,D2,D3 and this combination require no weighted graph-norm oracle.
For the real Gaussian, S_r, W, Xi/hbar^3 and (R15.14) are independent
of hbar. All dependencies on N,nu,a,tau remain explicit.


14.H.6 OPTIONAL PHASED GAUSSIANS

For p in R^d use the already derived state
  psi_p(q)=exp(i*p.(q-a)/hbar)*psi(q).
The same construction works over complex polynomial coefficients after
replacing V by

  V_p=V+(i/hbar)*p.b(a+z).                             (R15.15)

Indeed partial_j psi_p=(-z_j/(2*tau)+i*p_j/hbar)psi_p,
so the actual product-rule proof is unchanged. The additional phase
term is quadratic, hence the actual degree bound remains 2r.

For complex coefficients define

  S_{r,p}=sum_{alpha,beta in A_{2r}}
       Re(conj(c_{r,alpha})*c_{r,beta})*M_{alpha+beta}.

This equals E[(1+|a+Z|^2)|P_r(Z)|^2]>=0 and gives (R15.12)--(R15.13)
with S_{r,p}. The weighted state norm remains X=sqrt(W).
For a momentum p fixed independently of hbar, the coefficients generally
depend on p/hbar, so hbar-independence is not asserted. Fixing the
dimensionless phase p/hbar instead recovers that independence.


14.H.7 POSITIVE COEFFICIENT MAJORANTS

These bounds are optional: the exact evaluator is already (R15.11).
They provide a conservative schedule using no cancellation in the
finite signed moment sum.

For a real or complex polynomial F=sum_alpha f_alpha z^alpha, define

  L(F)=sum_alpha |f_alpha|.

Finite coefficient convolution and the scalar triangle inequality give
  L(F+G)<=L(F)+L(G),
  L(FG)<=L(F)L(G).
If every nonzero coefficient of F has total exponent <=K, then

  sum_i L(partial_i F)
    =sum_alpha |alpha|*|f_alpha|
    <=K*L(F).                                         (R15.16)

The equality follows because alpha -> alpha-eps_i is injective on
the monomials with alpha_i>0, and the derivative multiplier alpha_i
is a nonnegative integer.

Set
  beta_i=L(b_i(a+z)),
  beta=max({0} union {beta_i:1<=i<=d}),
  eta=L(V),       or eta=L(V_p) in the phased case.
Then L(DF)<=beta*K*L(F) whenever degree F<=K.

For the actual NSE degree bound, recurrence gives
  L(P_{r+1})<=(eta+2r*beta)L(P_r).
For r=2,3, the explicit formulas (R15.4) improve the third bound:

  L(P_2)<=J_2:=eta^2+2*beta*eta,
  L(P_3)<=J_3:=eta^3+6*beta*eta^2+6*beta^2*eta.         (R15.17)

Proof of the third bound.
Since V has degree <=2, L(DV)<=2beta*eta and degree(DV)<=3.
Consequently L(D^2V)<=3beta*L(DV)<=6beta^2*eta.
Apply the product and sum bounds to V^3+3V(DV)+D^2V.

For a completely positive majorant from the original drift coefficients,
one may use

  beta_i <= betaHat_i
    :=nu*sum_j |A_ij|*(1+|a_j|)
       +sum_{j,k}|C_ijk|*(1+|a_j|)*(1+|a_k|),

  eta <= etaHat
    :=|c|/2
       +[nu*sum_{i,j}|A_ij|*(1+|a_i|)*(1+|a_j|)
          +sum_i |a_i|*betaHat_i]/(2*tau).              (R15.18)

The second estimate uses the quadratic representative (R15.6).
For V_p add sum_i |p_i|*betaHat_i/hbar to etaHat.
Replace beta by max({0} union {betaHat_i}) and eta by etaHat in
(R15.17); every expression is nonnegative and monotone in these inputs.

For every multiindex alpha,

  E[(1+|a+Z|^2)Z^(2alpha)]
    =[W+2*tau*|alpha|]*tau^|alpha|*product_i O(alpha_i).
                                                               (R15.19)

The linear cross term 2a.Z has an odd coordinate and vanishes.
The identity m_{2alpha+2eps_i}=tau*(2alpha_i+1)*m_{2alpha}
supplies the remaining sum. Weighted L2 triangle inequality now gives

  sqrt(S_r)
    <=sum_{alpha in A_{2r}} |c_{r,alpha}|*sigma^|alpha|
          *sqrt([W+2*tau*|alpha|]*product_i O(alpha_i)). (R15.20)

For k=|alpha|, product_i O(alpha_i)<=O(k). One elementary proof
partitions the ordered odd factors into consecutive blocks: the
j-th factor of a block shifted by s is 2(s+j)-1>=2j-1.
Also O(k)<=O(K) whenever 0<=k<=K. Therefore, for K=2r,

  sqrt(S_r)
    <=L(P_r)*max(1,sigma^K)
         *sqrt((W+2*tau*K)*O(K)).                      (R15.21)

This covers K=0 with O(0)=1. In particular,

  sqrt(S_2)<=J_2*max(1,sigma^4)*sqrt(105*(W+8*tau)),
  sqrt(S_3)<=J_3*max(1,sigma^6)*sqrt(10395*(W+12*tau)),

  Xi/hbar^3
    <=J_3*max(1,sigma^6)*sqrt(10395*W*(W+12*tau)).      (R15.22)

Here O(4)=7!!=105 and O(6)=11!!=10395. These constants do not omit
the extra weight moment: its contribution is exactly W+2*tau*K.

For the canonical scale
  sigma_N=1/[(N+1)*w_N*sqrt(d_N)],
one has sigma_N<=1 and W>=1. Since 11^2>=105 and 102^2>=10395,

  sqrt(S_2)<=11*(W+8*tau)*J_2,
  sqrt(S_3)<=102*(W+12*tau)*J_3,
  Xi/hbar^3<=102*(W+12*tau)*J_3.                       (R15.23)

The last inequality follows directly from the last line of (R15.22):
sqrt(W*(W+12*tau))<=W+12*tau. It does not follow by multiplying
the preceding coarse bound for sqrt(S_3) by sqrt(W).

For arbitrary sigma>0, multiplication of the right side of the last
line by max(1,sigma^6), or by (1+tau)^3, gives a valid algebraic bound.


14.H.8 EXACT AND CONSERVATIVE CAYLEY SCHEDULES

Retain the canonical real Gaussian and the exact value
  g_N=sqrt(Tr A_N)
from CP40. For finite T>=0 define

  C_{N,T}=max(w_N^2*T^3/6, g_N*T^4/48),
  J_exact=sqrt(W*S_3),
  K_exact=C_{N,T}*J_exact,

  n_exact=max(1,ceil_N(sqrt((N+1)*K_exact))).           (R15.24)

By (R15.13), K_exact is precisely K^rat in (C20). Consequently this
formula does not alter the existing Gaussian criterion or finite-product
curve. It replaces the occurrence of Xi by its proved finite expression.
The maximum factorization is valid because J_exact>=0.

An optional conservative alternative is

  J_hat=102*(W+12*tau)*J_3,
  K_hat=C_{N,T}*J_hat,
  n_hat=max(1,ceil_N(sqrt((N+1)*K_hat))).               (R15.25)

The coefficient majorants (R15.18) may replace beta and eta in J_3.
The same conclusion holds for any explicitly supplied nonnegative
J_upper>=J_exact. These upper bounds are finite formulas in specified
finite real input data, not additional analytic assumptions.

For either n=n_exact or n=n_hat,
  n>=1,
  n^2>=(N+1)*K_exact.
Hence CP44's exact errors imply

  sup_{0<=t<=T}|Q^{E,n}_N(t;psi)-Q^E_N(t;psi)|
    <=1/(N+1),
  |integral_0^T Q^{L,n}_N(t;psi)dt
     -integral_0^T Q^L_N(t;psi)dt|
    <=1/(N+1).                                       (R15.26)

For n_hat this is a newly specified finite-product curve, and its
regularity predicates are defined with exactly that same n_hat in
every occurrence. CP45's two-way additive-bound proof applies unchanged
to those predicates because 1/(N+1)<=1/2 for N>=1. It is not necessary
to assert any ordering of the observables themselves as n changes.

Zero cases.
  If S_3=0, then J_exact=K_exact=0 and n_exact=1; (C17)--(C19)
  give zero observable errors directly.
  If T=0, then C_{N,T}=0 and the same convention yields n=1.
  A positive conservative upper bound may prescribe n_hat>1 even when
  the exact graph factor vanishes; the validity of the upper error
  bounds is unaffected.
  No division by S_3, beta, eta, g_N or T is used.
  Divisions by tau and hbar use only their explicit strict positivity.

Both schedules are independent of hbar for the real canonical Gaussian.
The optional phased formula has the dependence stated in 14.H.6.

EFFECTIVITY BOUNDARY.
The formulas eliminate integral/operator-norm witnesses from the graph
data. They consist of finite real coefficient arithmetic, finite sums,
absolute values, maxima, nonnegative square roots and natural ceilings.
They do not produce exact finite-bit representations of arbitrary smooth
data, exact Fourier-integral oracles, numerical inverse solvers, or a
decision procedure for a universal cutoff bound. In particular, applying
a natural ceiling to arbitrary exact real input remains an analytic
definition unless that input has an additional effective representation.
No G3, FB or unknown uniform regularity constant appears in these formulas.

14.I ROUND 16: POSITIVE PARTITIONS, DYADIC REFINEMENT AND EXACT CRITERIA

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI43]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP48, CP49; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML43, ML47, ML58, ML59, ML65, ML66; inherited MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD19, AD21.
  APPLICATION: Chronological products and endpoint gluing yield continuous partition paths. Exact
               cubic partition mass fixes the integrated observable coefficient; geometric summation
               and natural ceilings give explicit refinement budgets.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.I.0 Frozen notation and actual domains.

Fix N>=1, nu>0 and hbar>0. Suppress N in operator notation. Retain
  Hilbert=L2(E_N,dq;C),
  D=C_c^infinity(E_N;C),
  H=H_N=closure(H_{N,min}),
  G=-(i/hbar)H,
  U(t)=U_N(t),
  Hilbert^[m]=L2(E_N,(1+|q|^2)^m dq;C),
  ||psi||_[m]^2=integral(1+|q|^2)^m|psi(q)|^2 dq,
for every integer m>=0. The weighted spaces are complete, D is dense,
and the inclusion into ordinary Hilbert space is continuous.

For h>0 define the actual bounded operators
  S_h=(Id-hG/2)^(-1)=(Id+i*h*H/(2*hbar))^(-1),
  C_h=2S_h-Id.
Set S_0=C_0=Id. Range(S_h) is contained in Dom(H) for h>0. No such range
claim is made at h=0. CP41--CP43 already establish:
  (a) C_h is unitary in ordinary Hilbert space;
  (b) S_h and C_h are contractions in Hilbert^[m] for h>0;
  (c) U(t) is a strongly continuous contraction in Hilbert^[m], t>=0;
  (d) h->C_h psi is strongly weighted-continuous for h>=0;
  (e) for phi in D and h>=0,
      ||(C_h-U(h))phi||_[m]
        <=h^3/(12*hbar^3)||H^3 phi||_[m].
The h=0 case of (e) is proved directly from C_0=U(0)=Id.

The quantitative results first apply to psi in D. Their second permitted
class consists of actual psi in Dom(H^3), with psi,H^3 psi in Hilbert^[m],
for which actual phi_l in D satisfy
  ||phi_l-psi||_[m]+||H^3 phi_l-H^3 psi||_[m] -> 0.       (R16.01)
CP39 supplies (R16.01) for every Schwartz state and every m, including the
canonical Gaussian family. A bare formal symbol H^3 psi does not replace
this domain and approximation contract.

For a state satisfying (R16.01), set
  X_m=||psi||_[m],
  D_m=||H^3 psi||_[m],
  d_m=D_m/(12*hbar^3).
For exact unbounded-observable results require, additionally,
  ||psi||_[0]=1 and psi in Hilbert^[2],
and use the third-graph condition at m=1. No third-graph condition at
m=2 is needed merely to establish the observable domains.

14.I.1 Chronological products for an arbitrary positive partition.

Let T>0 and let
  pi=(0=t_0<t_1<...<t_J=T), J>=1,
  h_j=t_j-t_{j-1}>0,
  Delta_pi=max_{1<=j<=J}h_j.
Define
  P_0=Id,
  P_j=C_{h_j}P_{j-1}=C_{h_j}...C_{h_1}.                 (R16.02)
The earliest physical step is the rightmost operator. Neither the proof
nor the definition requires commutation of different C_h.

Every P_j is unitary in ordinary Hilbert space and contractive in each
Hilbert^[m]. For psi in D, subtract the exact orbit recursively:
  P_j psi-U(t_j)psi
    =C_{h_j}(P_{j-1}psi-U(t_{j-1})psi)
       +(C_{h_j}-U(h_j))U(t_{j-1})psi.                  (R16.03)
The second vector to which the local error is applied is the actual test
state U(t_{j-1})psi. It is not an unproved H^3-domain assertion about
P_{j-1}psi. On the actual test domain,
  H^3 U(t_{j-1})psi=U(t_{j-1})H^3 psi,
so forward weighted contraction gives
  ||H^3 U(t_{j-1})psi||_[m]<=D_m.
Induction in (R16.03) yields
  ||P_j psi-U(t_j)psi||_[m]
    <=d_m sum_{i=1}^j h_i^3.                            (R16.04)

For psi satisfying (R16.01), apply (R16.04) to phi_l and pass to the weighted
limit. P_j and U(t_j) are bounded weighted contractions, and
||H^3 phi_l||_[m]->D_m. This proves (R16.04) for exactly the additional
class in (R16.01), without assuming that weighted graph approximation is
automatic for arbitrary states in Dom(H^3).

14.I.2 A continuous exact-resolvent path for the fixed partition.

For t in [t_k,t_{k+1}], 0<=k<J, put theta=t-t_k and define
  P_pi(t)=C_theta P_k,
  A_pi(t)=sum_{i=1}^k h_i^3+theta^3.                     (R16.05)
At a shared endpoint the two formulas agree because
  C_{h_{k+1}}P_k=P_{k+1}=C_0P_{k+1}.
In particular P_pi(0)=Id and P_pi(T)=P_J. The function A_pi is also
continuous at the shared endpoints. For T=0 define the path to be Id
on the singleton {0}; all error bounds are then zero.

For every t, P_pi(t) is unitary in ordinary Hilbert space and contractive
in each weighted space. For every weighted state psi, t->P_pi(t)psi is
strongly weighted-continuous: on each closed interval this follows from
strong continuity of C_theta applied to the fixed vector P_k psi; the
endpoint identities give a continuous finite gluing.

Apply the same induction as (R16.03), followed by the one partial step theta.
The partial step theta=0 is the identity case, requiring no unbounded
operator evaluation at zero. The quantitative error is
  ||P_pi(t)psi-U(t)psi||_[m]<=d_m A_pi(t).                (R16.06)
Since h_i^3<=Delta_pi^2 h_i and theta^3<=Delta_pi^2 theta,
  A_pi(t)<=t*Delta_pi^2,
and consequently
  sup_{0<=t<=T}||P_pi(t)psi-U(t)psi||_[m]
    <=d_m*T*Delta_pi^2.                                 (R16.07)
No semigroup or group law in t is asserted for P_pi.

For an arbitrary psi in Hilbert^[m] and phi in D, contraction and (R16.07)
give
  sup_{0<=t<=T}||P_pi(t)psi-U(t)psi||_[m]
    <=2||psi-phi||_[m]
       +T*Delta_pi^2||H^3 phi||_[m]/(12*hbar^3).
Choose phi first and then send Delta_pi to zero. Thus every sequence of
finite positive partitions of [0,T] with mesh tending to zero converges
strongly to U, uniformly in t, on every weighted state. No uniform rate
is asserted for a general weighted state without graph information.

14.I.3 Exact partition integral and actual unbounded observables.

Retain the actual nonnegative multipliers
  e3_N(q)=||I_N(q)||H3^2,
  ell_N(q)=||nabla I_N(q)||_infinity,
  w_N=(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(3/2),
  g_N=sqrt(Tr A_N),
with
  e3_N<=w_N^2(1+|q|^2),
  ell_N<=g_N|q|<=(g_N/2)(1+|q|^2).
Hilbert^[2] is contained in the actual maximal domain of E3_N=M_e3_N,
and Hilbert^[1] is contained in the actual maximal domain of L_N=M_ell_N.
Both the exact orbit and the partition path preserve these weighted
spaces. Their states have ordinary norm one. Therefore the expressions
  Q^E_pi(t)=<P_pi(t)psi,E3_N P_pi(t)psi>,
  Q^L_pi(t)=<P_pi(t)psi,L_N P_pi(t)psi>
are actual normalized Hilbert-space expectations.

For any real measurable f with |f|<=c(1+|q|^2), CP44 gives
  |Q_f(v)-Q_f(w)|
    <=c(||v||_[1]+||w||_[1])||v-w||_[1].                (R16.08)
Write Xi_N(psi)=X_1 D_1. Equations (R16.06),(R16.08) give
  |Q^E_pi(t)-Q^E_U(t)|
    <=w_N^2*Xi_N/(6*hbar^3)*A_pi(t),                   (R16.09)
  |Q^L_pi(t)-Q^L_U(t)|
    <=g_N*Xi_N/(12*hbar^3)*A_pi(t).                    (R16.10)
Weighted continuity at m=1 and (R16.08) prove continuity of both scalar
observable functions. Thus all finite time integrals below are ordinary
integrals of integrable functions; no totalized-integral shortcut is used.

The exact scalar partition integral is
  I_pi=integral_0^T A_pi(t)dt
      =sum_{j=1}^J [(T-t_j)h_j^3+h_j^4/4].             (R16.11)
Indeed, on [t_{j-1},t_j], the integral is
  h_j sum_{i<j}h_i^3+h_j^4/4.
Reorder this finite sum: a completed h_i^3 contributes over precisely
the remaining interval length T-t_i. Since A_pi(t)<=t Delta_pi^2,
  I_pi<=T^2 Delta_pi^2/2.
Consequently
  sup_{0<=t<=T}|Q^E_pi(t)-Q^E_U(t)|
    <=w_N^2*Xi_N*T*Delta_pi^2/(6*hbar^3),               (R16.12)
  |integral_0^T Q^L_pi(t)dt-integral_0^T Q^L_U(t)dt|
    <=g_N*Xi_N*I_pi/(12*hbar^3)
    <=g_N*Xi_N*T^2*Delta_pi^2/(24*hbar^3).              (R16.13)

For the uniform partition with J steps, h=T/J, one has exactly
  I_pi=J(2J-1)h^4/4=T^4(2J-1)/(4J^3).
Thus the exact integrated-gradient coefficient for this path is
  g_N*Xi_N*T^4(2J-1)/(48*hbar^3*J^3).
The simpler bound is g_N*Xi_N*T^4/(24*hbar^3*J^2).
The coefficient 1/24 is deliberate: this is a fixed completed-step path,
not the earlier t->C_{t/n}^n path, whose integrated coefficient was 1/48.

14.I.4 Dyadic refinement and norm-summable path errors.

Fix a positive base step count J_0. At refinement level ell>=0 use the
uniform partition pi_ell with
  J_ell=J_0*2^ell,
  Delta_ell=T/(J_0*2^ell).
It is obtained from its predecessor by bisecting every interval. Define
  B_m=T^3 D_m/(12*hbar^3).
Equation (R16.07) gives
  sup_t||P_{pi_ell}(t)psi-U(t)psi||_[m]
    <=(B_m/J_0^2)*4^(-ell).                             (R16.14)
In particular the scalar error upper bounds are summable:
  sum_{ell>=0} sup_t||P_{pi_ell}(t)psi-U(t)psi||_[m]
    <=(4/3)*B_m/J_0^2.
The triangle inequality also gives the explicit successive-path bound
  sup_t||P_{pi_{ell+1}}(t)psi-P_{pi_ell}(t)psi||_[m]
    <=(5/4)*(B_m/J_0^2)*4^(-ell),
whose sum is at most (5/3)*B_m/J_0^2. These are estimates for a fixed
finite-cutoff state. No cutoff-uniform graph bound has been assumed.

14.I.5 Explicit cutoff/refinement schedules and criterion transport.

Choose once and for all F in {canonical compact,canonical Gaussian} and
p in {1,2}. For its prescribed actual normalized state Psi^F_{N,a}, put
  delta_N=(N+1)^(-p),
  K_E=w_N^2*T^3*Xi_N(Psi^F_{N,a})/(6*hbar^3),
  K_L=g_N*T^4*Xi_N(Psi^F_{N,a})/(24*hbar^3),
  B_obs=max(K_E,K_L),
  J_0(N,a,T)=max(1,Nat.ceil(sqrt((N+1)^p*B_obs))),
  J_ell(N,a,T)=J_0(N,a,T)*2^ell.                        (R16.15)
Every input is finite and already determined by the actual finite
operator, specified packet, cutoff and horizon. Neither G3 nor FB nor a
cutoff-uniform regularity constant occurs in this definition.

Natural-ceiling positivity gives
  J_0>=1,
  J_0^2>=(N+1)^p*B_obs.
Equations (R16.12)--(R16.13) therefore give, with the same partition along the
entire horizon,
  sup_t|Q^E_{pi_ell}(t)-Q^E_U(t)|<=delta_N*4^(-ell),
  |integral_0^T(Q^L_{pi_ell}(t)-Q^L_U(t))dt|
    <=delta_N*4^(-ell).                                 (R16.16)
The case B_obs=0 gives zero errors and J_0=1. No division by zero occurs.
For real canonical profiles, H/hbar and the profiles are hbar-independent;
therefore B_obs and this schedule are hbar-independent. Profiles with
hbar-dependent phases require a separate statement.

The sum of either error bound over ell>=0 is at most (4/3)delta_N.
For p=2, summability also holds over the cutoffs, because
  sum_{N=1}^M (N+1)^(-2)
    <=sum_{N=1}^M 1/(N(N+1))=1-1/(M+1)<=1.
Thus the corresponding double sum of these certified approximation
bounds over N>=1 and ell>=0 is at most 4/3. No analogous cutoff
summability is claimed for p=1.

Retain N,a,T,ell in the approximate-observable index. For any prescribed
nonnegative refinement choice ell=ell(N,a,T), including the constant
choice zero, define QREG_part^F and QLIP_part^F by the same all-data,
all-finite-T, cutoff-uniform bounds as in Section14.G, with these exact
partition observables. The profile family and refinement prescription
are fixed before the quantifiers. Since delta_N*4^(-ell)<=1/2 for N>=1,
adding 1/2 to a common bound proves both directions of
  QREG_part^F <=> QREG_F,
  QLIP_part^F <=> QLIP_F.                               (R16.17)
Together with CP34 or CP38--CP39, and CP27,
  G3 <=> QREG_part^F <=> QLIP_part^F.                    (R16.18)
The horizon T remains an index; the partition path is not a time group.

Under G3, compose (R16.16) with the already proved exact-family continuum
bounds. The new error is bounded by
  exact_family_continuum_error_N+delta_N*4^(-ell(N,a,T)).
Both errors therefore remain O(N^(-1)) on fixed finite horizons. Choosing
p=2 or increasing ell improves the finite-resolvent approximation term;
it does not by itself improve the previously derived continuum Galerkin
rate. No finite numerical regularity checker follows from (R16.17)--(R16.18).

14.J ROUND 17: ACTUAL RESIDUAL IDENTITIES AND NODAL CERTIFICATES

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI44]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP50; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML47, ML65; MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD19, AD21.
  APPLICATION: Apply the actual affine inverse only to domain-valid vectors. The plus-sign residual
               formula gives twice the finite residual sum, with explicit weighted norm growth and a
               positive normalization denominator.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.J.0 Residual input contract.

Fix a finite positive partition as in Round16, and a reference state psi
satisfying the applicable Round16 weighted third-graph hypothesis. Permit
an approximate initial vector x_0 in Hilbert^[m], and put
  eta_m=||x_0-psi||_[m].
For each j=1,...,J supply an ACTUAL vector y_j such that
  y_j in Dom(H),
  y_j,G y_j in Hilbert^[m].                              (R17.01)
Define the actual residual and the next state by
  r_j=(Id-h_j G/2)y_j-x_{j-1},
  x_j=2y_j-x_{j-1}.                                     (R17.02)
Equivalently,
  r_j=y_j+i*h_j*H y_j/(2*hbar)-x_{j-1}.
The residual has this sign. The domain assertion applies to y_j before
H y_j is formed. No claim that H is bounded on the weighted space is used.

Inductively x_j and r_j belong to Hilbert^[m]. The same definitions may
be considered simultaneously at m=0,1,2 whenever the actual vectors have
the stated weighted graph membership. For actual E3 expectations use
m=2 membership, even if the numerical error budget uses m=1 norms.

A certificate may replace the exact residual norms by explicit bounds
  ||r_j||_[m]<=rho_{j,m}, rho_{j,m}>=0.
The theorem assumes these are proved inequalities about actual residuals.
A finite list of real numbers called residual bounds, without their
matching vector/domain/norm statements, is not such a certificate.

14.J.1 The exact one-step perturbation identity.

The residual equation says
  (Id-h_j G/2)y_j=x_{j-1}+r_j.
