Because y_j lies in the actual inverse domain, the CP41 inverse identity
implies
  y_j=S_{h_j}(x_{j-1}+r_j).
Consequently
  x_j=C_{h_j}x_{j-1}+2S_{h_j}r_j.                      (R17.03)
This is an identity in ordinary Hilbert space. All terms also belong to
the weighted space, and the continuous inclusion identifies the same
vectors there. Weighted contraction gives the one-step bound
  ||x_j-C_{h_j}x_{j-1}||_[m]<=2rho_{j,m}.                (R17.04)
The constant is 2, not 1. No residual sign cancellation has been assumed.

14.J.2 Finite residual accumulation and time-discretization error.

For 1<=ell<=j define the chronological suffix
  P_{j:ell+1}=C_{h_j}...C_{h_{ell+1}},
with the empty suffix equal to Id. Iterating (R17.03) gives exactly
  x_j=P_j x_0
       +2 sum_{ell=1}^j P_{j:ell+1}S_{h_ell}r_ell.       (R17.05)
No commutation, differentiability of the approximate vectors, or exchange
of an infinite sum with an unbounded operator enters this identity.

Set
  a_{j,m}=eta_m+2 sum_{ell=1}^j rho_{ell,m},
  s_j=sum_{ell=1}^j h_ell^3.
Since every factor in (R17.05) is a weighted contraction,
  ||x_j-P_j psi||_[m]<=a_{j,m}.                          (R17.06)
Combining with (R16.04),
  ||x_j-U(t_j)psi||_[m]
    <=a_{j,m}+d_m s_j
    <=eta_m+2 sum_{ell=1}^j rho_{ell,m}
       +t_j*Delta_pi^2 D_m/(12*hbar^3).                 (R17.07)
This is an a posteriori estimate: after actual vectors and certified
residual bounds are supplied, its right side bounds their actual error.
It is not a claim that those residual bounds can always be evaluated by
a given finite program.

The corresponding weighted norm growth is
  ||x_j||_[m]<=X_m+a_{j,m}.                             (R17.08)
For normalized psi, ordinary unitarity of P_j gives the stronger separate
normalization control
  abs(||x_j||_[0]-1)<=a_{j,0}.                          (R17.09)
Notice that (R17.09) contains no time-discretization term. Exact Cayley
products are unitary, so only initial and residual errors affect this
norm comparison. If a_{j,0}<1, then x_j is nonzero.

For x_0=psi and rho_{ell,m}<=rho_m,
  ||x_j-U(t_j)psi||_[m]
    <=2j*rho_m+d_m s_j.
In particular choosing per-step residual tolerances proportional to 1/J
controls their global accumulation; the theorem does not substitute a
maximum residual for the required finite sum without the factor J.

14.J.3 Actual multiplier domains for the approximate nodes.

For E3 and L statements require
  psi,x_0 in Hilbert^[2],
  y_j,G y_j in Hilbert^[2], y_j in Dom(H), for every j.
Then (R17.02) proves x_j in Hilbert^[2], and hence each x_j lies in the
actual maximal E3 domain and in the actual maximal L domain. No estimate
of ||H x_j|| is required for the multiplier domains.

The hypothesis y_j in D is a sufficient concrete instance: Hmin is a
polynomial-coefficient differential operator, so y_j and G y_j remain
smooth and compactly supported and have every polynomial weighted norm.
The initial compact and Gaussian states also have all required weighted
norms. This is a sufficient domain instance, not an assertion that every
numerical representation automatically is a smooth compact test vector.

If x_0 belongs to Dom(H), (R17.02) additionally proves x_j belongs to Dom(H)
by linearity; this observation is optional. The finite residual recurrence
only requires Dom(H) membership for each y_j.

14.J.4 Explicit unnormalized nodal quadratic-observable errors.

Let psi be normalized. Write
  X=X_1,
  a_j=a_{j,1},
  E_j=d_1 s_j.
Since ordinary norm is dominated by ||.||_[1], X>=1. The reference
u_j=U(t_j)psi satisfies ||u_j||_[1]<=X. Equations (R17.07)--(R17.08) give
  ||x_j-u_j||_[1]<=a_j+E_j,
  ||x_j||_[1]+||u_j||_[1]<=2X+a_j.
For every real measurable f with |f|<=c(1+|q|^2), (R16.08) implies
  |Q_f(x_j)-Q_f(u_j)|
    <=c(2X+a_j)(E_j+a_j).                               (R17.10)
For the actual E3 and L operators, this gives
  |<x_j,E3 x_j>-Q^E_U(t_j)|
    <=w_N^2(2X+a_j)(E_j+a_j),                           (R17.11)
  |<x_j,L x_j>-Q^L_U(t_j)|
    <=(g_N/2)(2X+a_j)(E_j+a_j).                         (R17.12)
The factors containing a_j account for norm growth. Omitting them and
reusing the normalized exact-Cayley factor 2X would be unjustified.

Unless ||x_j||_[0]=1 is separately proved, <x_j,M_f x_j> here denotes an
unnormalized quadratic observable. The normalized quantum expectation is
<x_j,M_f x_j>/||x_j||_[0]^2, provided x_j is nonzero. The next paragraph
controls that quantity explicitly.

14.J.5 Optional normalization with a residual-only denominator.

Assume a_{j,0}<1 and set
  xhat_j=x_j/||x_j||_[0],
  v_j=P_j psi,
  gamma_j=(a_{j,1}+a_{j,0}X)/(1-a_{j,0}).              (R17.13)
Then ||v_j||_[0]=1, ||v_j||_[1]<=X. With z=||x_j||_[0],
  xhat_j-v_j=(x_j-v_j+(1-z)v_j)/z.
Equations (R17.06),(R17.09) therefore give
  ||xhat_j-v_j||_[1]<=gamma_j,
  ||xhat_j||_[1]<=X+gamma_j,
  ||xhat_j-U(t_j)psi||_[1]<=E_j+gamma_j.                (R17.14)
Scalar normalization preserves the actual maximal multiplier domains.
Thus the actual normalized expectations satisfy
  |Q^E(xhat_j)-Q^E_U(t_j)|
    <=w_N^2(2X+gamma_j)(E_j+gamma_j),                   (R17.15)
  |Q^L(xhat_j)-Q^L_U(t_j)|
    <=(g_N/2)(2X+gamma_j)(E_j+gamma_j).                 (R17.16)
When all initial/residual errors vanish, gamma_j=0 and these are exactly
the corresponding variable-step bounds in (R16.09)--(R16.10).

A single convenient sufficient budget is a_{j,0}<=a_{j,1}<=a<1; it can
always be obtained by using the m=1 error bounds also for m=0. Then
  gamma_j<=a(1+X)/(1-a).
If a<=1/2, this simplifies to gamma_j<=2a(1+X).            (R17.17)
The strict positive denominator is part of the normalization contract.
No normalized state is defined at an unproved possibly zero vector.

14.J.6 Nodal scope and the continuous-path successor.

The finite list (R17.01)--(R17.02) certifies only the nodes t_j. No estimate
of integral_0^T Q^L(t)dt follows from a list of nodal values alone, and
no continuous path is implicitly selected by (R17.02).

Section14.K constructs the piecewise-affine path through these
nodes, proves its additional Banach chord error using H^2 psi, and then
normalizes it using an explicit positive norm lower bound. That separate
construction supplies continuous actual observable paths from finitely
many domain-certified vectors. It is the designated successor of CP50.
No continuous family of approximate inverse witnesses is required by the
present CP50 contract.

14.K ROUND 18: CORE WITNESSES, NORMALIZED CONTINUOUS PATHS AND EXACT CRITERIA

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI45]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP51, CP52; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML40, ML42--ML44, ML47, ML58, ML59, ML65; inherited MT10, MT11.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD18, AD20--AD22.
  APPLICATION: Finite-time core integrals derive arbitrarily accurate residual witnesses. Weighted
               C2 orbit approximation proves the chord kernel, and normalization gives actual
               continuous observable paths with summable cutoff error and exact criterion transport.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.K.1. Weighted residual approximation by actual compact test vectors.

Fix N>=1, nu>0, hbar>0. Retain H=H_N, G=-(i/hbar)H and the actual
core D_N=C_c^infinity(R^{d_N};C). For an integer m>=0, let
  X_m=L2((1+|q|^2)^m dq;C),
  ||.||_[m]=the actual weighted Hilbert norm.
The previous weighted construction proves completeness, dense inclusion
D_N in X_m, and forward contraction of U(t), S_h and C_h for h>0.

THEOREM [CORE_RESIDUAL_APPROXIMATION].
For every h>0, x in X_m and epsilon>0, there exists y in D_N such that
  ||(I-h*G/2)y-x||_[m]<=epsilon.                         (R18.1)
In particular, y lies in the actual domain of H; the displayed residual
is an actual X_m vector. No domain of G is required for the input x.

DERIVATION.
Weighted density supplies phi in D_N with ||phi-x||_[m]<=epsilon/2.
Set
  R=(h/2)*log(1+2*||phi||_[m]/epsilon)>=0,
  y=(2/h)*integral_0^R exp(-2*s/h)*U(s)phi ds.
The compact smooth finite-time integral construction at CP42 gives
y in D_N and the exact identity
  (I-h*G/2)y=phi-exp(-2*R/h)*U(R)phi.
Forward contraction and the chosen R yield
  ||(I-h*G/2)y-x||_[m]
    <=||phi-x||_[m]+exp(-2*R/h)*||phi||_[m]
    <=epsilon/2+||phi||_[m]/(1+2*||phi||_[m]/epsilon)
    <=epsilon.
If phi=0, then R=0 and y=0; the same formulas and bound apply.
This proves the existential statement without a solvability admission.

The construction uses a finite-time integral of the actual finite flow
and weighted density. It does not supply a finite-bit representation,
a terminating numerical solver, or a decidable residual-norm checker.
The distinction is retained in every subsequent witness statement.

14.K.2. Existence of finite sequences of core residual witnesses.

Let psi be normalized and Schwartz. This includes the prescribed compact
smooth packet and every prescribed Gaussian. Fix T>0, n>=1,
h=T/n, and epsilon>0. Set x_0=psi. Recursively apply (R18.1), with m=1,
to obtain y_j in D_N, 1<=j<=n, such that
  r_j=(I-h*G/2)y_j-x_{j-1},
  ||r_j||_[1]<=epsilon,
  x_j=2*y_j-x_{j-1}.                                    (R18.2)
Each application has a valid input in X_1: induction gives the stronger
finite identity
  x_j=(-1)^j*psi+2*sum_{k=1}^j (-1)^(j-k)*y_k.            (R18.3)
Thus every x_j is Schwartz, lies in all X_m and actual D(H^k), and has
all required maximal-multiplier domains. Normalization of intermediate
x_j is not assumed. Finite induction proves existence of the entire
tuple (y_1,...,y_n), for every prescribed epsilon>0.

The nodal residual identity of Round17 gives, with v_j=C_h^j*psi,
  ||x_j-v_j||_[1]<=2*sum_{k=1}^j ||r_k||_[1].             (R18.4)
This estimate uses only forward weighted contraction; no norm-preserving
property of the approximate x_j is used.

14.K.3. Weighted C2 orbits and the exact interpolation kernel.

Put D_{H,r}=||H^r psi||_[1], r=2,3. Both numbers are finite. The Schwartz
cutoff theorem CP39 supplies phi_l in D_N with simultaneous convergence
of phi_l, H phi_l and H^2 phi_l to psi, H psi and H^2 psi in X_1.
For each compact finite interval, weighted contraction makes
  U(t)phi_l, U(t)G phi_l, U(t)G^2 phi_l
converge uniformly in X_1 to
  U(t)psi, U(t)G psi, U(t)G^2 psi,
respectively. The compact-core orbit is twice strongly differentiable.
Pass to the limit in its two finite-interval fundamental-theorem
identities. Continuity of the limiting derivative vectors and Bochner
integration imply that f(t)=U(t)psi is C2 on [0,T], with right derivatives
at zero, and
  f''(t)=U(t)G^2 psi,
  ||f''(t)||_[1]<=D_{H,2}/hbar^2.                            (R18.5)
Actual unweighted D(H^2) membership alone is not substituted for this
weighted differentiation argument.

For a C2 Banach-valued f, s<=t<=s+h and theta=(t-s)/h, define the chord
  chord_f(t)=(1-theta)*f(s)+theta*f(s+h).
Two finite-interval integrations by parts give
  chord_f(t)-f(t)=integral_s^{s+h} K_t(r)*f''(r) dr,       (R18.6)
where
  K_t(r)=(1-theta)*(r-s)       for s<=r<=t,
  K_t(r)=theta*(s+h-r)         for t<=r<=s+h.
The two expressions agree at r=t; K_t>=0 and
  integral_s^{s+h} K_t(r)dr
    =theta*(1-theta)*h^2/2<=h^2/8.
Hence (R18.5) gives
  ||chord_f(t)-f(t)||_[1]<=h^2*D_{H,2}/(8*hbar^2).           (R18.7)
The constant 1/8 applies to the chord error; it is distinct from the
1/12 constant of the third-derivative Cayley error.

14.K.4. Continuous paths from nodal certificates.

For the uniform grid t_j=j*T/n, define the continuous X_m-valued path
  v(t)=(1-theta)*x_{j-1}+theta*x_j,
  theta=(t-t_{j-1})/h,  t in [t_{j-1},t_j].              (R18.8)
At common endpoints the two adjacent formulas give the same x_j.
Each value is Schwartz, being a finite linear combination of psi and
the compact test vectors y_k. Every fixed weighted norm is continuous
in t. The path is defined on the whole interval by the finite tuple;
there is no separate measurable-selection or continuous-residual premise.

At the nodes, (R18.4) and the exact uniform-step Cayley estimate give
  ||x_j-U(t_j)psi||_[1]
    <=T*h^2*D_{H,3}/(12*hbar^3)+2*sum_{k=1}^n ||r_k||_[1].
Compare (R18.8) first with the chord through U(t_{j-1})psi and U(t_j)psi,
then apply (R18.7). The convex triangle inequality yields
  sup_{0<=t<=T}||v(t)-U(t)psi||_[1]
    <=B_{N,psi,T}/n^2+2*sum_{k=1}^n ||r_k||_[1],         (R18.9)
where
  B_{N,psi,T}=T^3*D_{H,3}/(12*hbar^3)+T^2*D_{H,2}/(8*hbar^2).
All quantities on the right are finite at the fixed cutoff. For a real
Gaussian, Round15 gives the exact finite-moment expression
  B_{N,psi,T}=T^3*sqrt(S_3)/12+T^2*sqrt(S_2)/8.           (R18.10)
It involves moments only through degrees 14 and 10. For the real
canonical Gaussian, it is independent of hbar.

14.K.5. Exact normalization and maximal observable estimates.

Assume the right side of (R18.9) is at most e<1. Write
  X=||psi||_[1]>=||psi||_[0]=1,
  rho(t)=||v(t)||_[0].
Since ||U(t)psi||_[0]=1 and the inclusion X_1->X_0 has norm<=1,
  |rho(t)-1|<=e,
  rho(t)>=1-e>0.
Therefore the actual normalized state
  psi_hat(t)=v(t)/rho(t)                                 (R18.11)
is defined on the entire interval, is continuous in every X_m, is
Schwartz at each t, and satisfies psi_hat(0)=psi.

Forward contraction gives ||U(t)psi||_[1]<=X. Direct subtraction yields
  ||psi_hat(t)-U(t)psi||_[1]
    <=[||v(t)-U(t)psi||_[1]+|1-rho(t)|*X]/rho(t)
    <=e*(1+X)/(1-e)=:eta.                                 (R18.12)
Also ||psi_hat(t)||_[1]<=X+eta. For e<=1/2,
  eta<=2*e*(1+X).

Both psi_hat(t) and U(t)psi have the actual E3_N and L_N multiplier
domains: the former is Schwartz and the latter remains in X_2 by
forward weighted contraction. The quadratic expectation comparison
therefore proves
  sup_{0<=t<=T}|<psi_hat(t),E3_N psi_hat(t)>-Q_N^E(t;psi)|
    <=w_N^2*(2*X+eta)*eta,
  |integral_0^T <psi_hat(t),L_N psi_hat(t)>dt
       -integral_0^T Q_N^L(t;psi)dt|
    <=T*g_N*(2*X+eta)*eta/2.                              (R18.13)
The scalar functions are continuous by X_1 continuity and the same
quadratic comparison. Their integrals are actual finite integrals.
Normalization is applied after the nodal recurrence; no normalized
vector is silently substituted back into that recurrence.

14.K.6. A prescribed positive accuracy budget and finite witness contract.

For each N>=1 put
  delta_N=(N+1)^(-2),
  C_{N,T}=max(w_N^2,T*g_N/2)>=1,
  e_{N,psi,T}=delta_N/[4*C_{N,T}*(1+X)^2]>0,
  n_{N,psi,T}=max(1,ceil_N(sqrt(2*B_{N,psi,T}/e_{N,psi,T}))),
  epsilon_{N,psi,T}=e_{N,psi,T}/(4*n_{N,psi,T}).           (R18.14)
The actual natural ceiling implies
  B_{N,psi,T}/n_{N,psi,T}^2<=e_{N,psi,T}/2.
When B=0 this is immediate; the max with 1 handles that case.
If each of the n residuals has X_1 norm<=epsilon, their contribution in
(R18.9) is at most e/2. The finite tuple from (R18.2) therefore exists
and has total path error at most e.

Since delta_N<=1/4, C>=1 and X>=1, the chosen e is at most 1/64.
Thus e<=1/2 and eta<=2*e*(1+X)<=1. Consequently
  C*(2*X+eta)*eta
    <=C*(2*X+1)*2*e*(1+X)
    <=4*C*e*(1+X)^2=delta_N.
Equation (R18.13) becomes
  sup_{0<=t<=T}|<psi_hat(t),E3_N psi_hat(t)>-Q_N^E(t;psi)|
    <=delta_N,
  |integral_0^T <psi_hat(t),L_N psi_hat(t)>dt
       -integral_0^T Q_N^L(t;psi)dt|
    <=delta_N.                                           (R18.15)

The finite core-witness contract is precisely:
  n equals the prescribed integer in (R18.14);
  y_j belongs to the actual compact smooth core, 1<=j<=n;
  x_0=psi, x_j=2*y_j-x_{j-1};
  r_j=(I-(T/n)*G/2)y_j-x_{j-1};
  ||r_j||_[1]<=e/(4*n).
Its satisfiability was derived in (R18.1)--(R18.3). G3, FB, a continuum
solution, and an unknown uniform regularity constant are absent from
the contract and its existence proof. Every quantity in (R18.14) is
fixed-cutoff data. For the Gaussian, Round15 reduces the graph norms
to finite polynomial coefficient sums.

14.K.7. Exact criteria and summable approximation errors.

Fix F in {canonical compact,canonical Gaussian}, with the real canonical
Gaussian as the default phase choice. For each N,a,T choose a core tuple
W_{N,a,T} satisfying the preceding contract for psi=Psi^F_{N,a}.
The previous theorem proves nonemptiness at every parameter value;
ordinary choice gives a prescribed admissible family W. The family may
depend on N,a,T,nu,hbar,F, but is fixed before its common regularity
bound K or L is asserted. It is not selected using G3.

Let psi_hat^W_{N,a,T}(t) be the resulting actual normalized continuous
path and define its actual fluid-multiplier expectations Q_core^E and
Q_core^L. Define
  QREG_core^{F,W}(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall smooth divergence-free a, forall finite T>0,
      exists finite K>=0,
        forall N>=1, forall t in [0,T], Q_core^E(N,a,T,t)<=K;
  QLIP_core^{F,W}(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall smooth divergence-free a, forall finite T>0,
      exists finite L>=0,
        forall N>=1, integral_0^T Q_core^L(N,a,T,t)dt<=L.

For every prescribed admissible W, (R18.15) and delta_N<=1/4 imply
  QREG_core^{F,W}<=>QREG_F,
  QLIP_core^{F,W}<=>QLIP_F.                               (R18.16)
Each implication adds 1/4 to the asserted finite common bound; the
bound may depend on a,T as before, while remaining uniform in N.
Combine the two equivalences with the already derived exact-family
criterion to obtain
  G3(nu)<=>QREG_core^{F,W}(nu,hbar)
        <=>QLIP_core^{F,W}(nu,hbar).                      (R18.17)
The statement comprises both existence of admissible families and the
criterion equivalence for every such family. A supplied unresolved
core-residual existence premise is not necessary.

For every M>=1,
  sum_{N=1}^M delta_N
    <=sum_{N=1}^M 1/[N*(N+1)]
    =1-1/(M+1)<=1.                                       (R18.18)
The first inequality follows from N*(N+1)<=(N+1)^2 and positive
denominators. The equality telescopes 1/[N*(N+1)]=1/N-1/(N+1).
Monotonicity and boundedness of the nonnegative partial sums prove
  sum_{N>=1} delta_N<=1.
Thus the two numerical/model-approximation errors in (R18.15) have a
summable cutoff bound. Under G3, composition with the canonical-family
continuum estimates gives
  continuum energy error<=delta_N+E_N^E,
  continuum integrated-gradient error<=delta_N+E_N^L,
where E_N^E,E_N^L are the earlier conditional O((N+1)^(-1)) errors.
Only the added delta_N term is asserted summable. No summability of the
entire continuum error follows from the stated O((N+1)^(-1)) bound.

SCOPE.
The finite tuples contain smooth function witnesses and actual norm
inequalities. A finite number of such witnesses does not imply a
finite-bit encoding, terminating search, decidable norm verification,
a certified numerical inverse solver, or a finite witness for the
universal NSE regularity predicate. These claims are not conclusions.
The path psi_hat is a normalized approximate state path with proved
errors; no exact Schroedinger equation or time-group law is asserted
for that path. The exact quantum dynamics remains U_N(t).


14.L ROUND 19: EXPLICIT HERMITE COMPLETENESS AND WEIGHTED GRAPH DENSITY

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI46]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP53, CP54; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML13--ML15, ML40, ML47, ML49, ML50, ML52--ML57, ML60--ML69; inherited MT02, MT03, MT05.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD18, AD20, AD22, AD23.
  APPLICATION: Compact-test Fourier inversion and actual L2 density prove Hermite completeness.
               Explicit ladder tails then prove weighted graph convergence and residual-range
               density in the full actual first graph domain.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.L.0 FROZEN SCOPE.
Fix one actual finite periodic NSE cutoff N, nu>0 and hbar>0. All
coefficient coordinates, including the constant Fourier coordinates,
remain those already constructed. Set d=d_N>=1 and

  H=-i*hbar*[b(q).nabla+c/2],
  G=-(i/hbar)H=-[b(q).nabla+c/2],
  c=div b=-nu*Tr(A_N).

The sign of G is retained in every residual formula. Write
  X_m=L2((1+|q|^2)^m dq;C),
  ||.||_[m]=the actual weighted norm.
The actual unweighted domain of G is the actual Dom(H_N).

Fix once a center a in R^d and a scale sigma>0. The real Gaussian
ground state is

  psi_{a,sigma}(q)=(2*pi*sigma^2)^(-d/4)
                       *exp(-|q-a|^2/(4*sigma^2)).       (R19.1)

The center and scale do not change when the approximation degree K
changes. CP39 already proves normalization, Schwartz membership and
membership in all actual H_N powers for polynomial-Gaussian states.
No G3 premise or uniform-in-N assertion occurs below.


14.L.1 EXPLICIT ONE-DIMENSIONAL LADDER FAMILY

On the standardized real coordinate y, put
  h_0(y)=(2*pi)^(-1/4)*exp(-y^2/4),
  a_minus=partial_y+y/2,
  a_plus=-partial_y+y/2.
These are differential expressions on Schwartz functions. Define

  h_n=(a_plus)^n h_0/sqrt(n!),  n>=0.                  (R19.2)

Equivalently define real polynomials
  He_0=1,
  He_{n+1}(y)=y*He_n(y)-He_n'(y).
Then
  h_n(y)=He_n(y)*h_0(y)/sqrt(n!).                       (R19.3)

Every h_n is Schwartz. The recurrence makes He_n monic of degree n:
multiplication by y supplies the new leading term, while differentiation
has strictly lower degree. In particular this family is not introduced
by assuming a complete Hermite basis.

Direct product-rule calculation on Schwartz functions gives
  a_minus h_0=0,
  [a_minus,a_plus]=Id,
  <a_minus f,g>=<f,a_plus g>.
The last identity follows from actual integration by parts. All boundary
terms vanish and all products are integrable because the functions are
Schwartz. Thus

  a_minus h_n=sqrt(n)*h_{n-1},
  a_plus h_n=sqrt(n+1)*h_{n+1},                         (R19.4)

where h_{-1}=0. To verify the first identity before normalization, use
  a_minus(a_plus)^n=(a_plus)^n a_minus+n(a_plus)^(n-1)
and apply it to h_0.

The Gaussian integral gives ||h_0||_2=1. The adjoint identity and
commutator give inductively
  ||a_plus h_n||_2^2=<h_n,a_minus a_plus h_n>=n+1,
so ||h_n||_2=1 for every n. The symmetric expression
  N_1=a_plus a_minus=-partial_y^2+y^2/4-1/2
satisfies N_1 h_n=n h_n. For m!=n, symmetry yields
  (m-n)<h_m,h_n>=0.
Consequently

  <h_m,h_n>=1 if m=n, and 0 otherwise.                (R19.5)

Only integration by parts, Gaussian integrability and finite ladder
identities were used. No spectral or selfadjointness theorem for an
oscillator is an input.


14.L.2 TENSOR FAMILY AND FINITE POLYNOMIAL SPANS

For alpha=(alpha_1,...,alpha_d) in N^d define
  |alpha|=sum_j alpha_j,
  alpha!=product_j alpha_j!,
  h_alpha(y)=product_j h_{alpha_j}(y_j).
Finite product integration gives an orthonormal family in L2(R^d;C).
Its elements are real-valued Schwartz functions.

Let
  A_K={alpha in {0,...,K}^d:|alpha|<=K},
  W_K=span_C{h_alpha:alpha in A_K}.
Monicity of every He_n implies the exact finite-dimensional equality

  W_K={P(y)*h_0^{(d)}(y): P a complex polynomial,
                             total degree(P)<=K},
  h_0^{(d)}(y)=(2*pi)^(-d/4)*exp(-|y|^2/4).            (R19.6)

Proof.
Each tensor polynomial has leading monomial y^alpha and all other
monomials have smaller total degree. To express an arbitrary monomial
y^alpha, subtract the corresponding tensor Hermite polynomial and
induct on total degree. Normalization by sqrt(alpha!) is nonzero and
does not alter the finite span. The reverse inclusion is immediate.
In particular W_K is nested in W_{K+1}, is finite-dimensional and
contains h_0^{(d)} for every K>=0.


14.L.3 COMPLETENESS: GAUSSIAN MOMENTS, TEST INVERSION AND L2 DENSITY

The following argument proves completeness; it is not a named-basis
admission. Use the Fourier convention
  Fhat(xi)=integral exp(-2*pi*i*xi.y)*F(y)dy,
  FourierInv U(y)=integral exp(2*pi*i*xi.y)*U(xi)dxi.

LEMMA [R19-A: FOURIER INTEGRABILITY OF COMPACT SMOOTH TESTS].
If phi in C_c^infinity(R^d;C), then phi and phihat are integrable, and

  phi(y)=integral exp(2*pi*i*xi.y)*phihat(xi)dxi.        (R19.7)

Proof.
Choose an integer k with 2k>d. All derivatives of phi are compactly
supported. Dominated convergence with majorant |phi| makes phihat
continuous, hence measurable. Repeated compact integration by parts gives
  Fourier((1-Delta)^k phi)(xi)
    =(1+4*pi^2*|xi|^2)^k*phihat(xi).
Hence
  |phihat(xi)|<=||(1-Delta)^k phi||_L1
                       *(1+4*pi^2*|xi|^2)^(-k).
The majorant is integrable. On {|xi|<1} it is bounded by one and the
set has finite volume. On the annulus 2^j<=|xi|<2^(j+1), its integral
is at most
  (4*pi^2)^(-k)*2^(2d)*[2^(d-2k)]^j.
Indeed, the annulus lies in a cube of side 2^(j+2), and its denominator
is at least (4*pi^2)^k*2^(2kj). Since 0<2^(d-2k)<1, the geometric
series converges. This proves actual Integrable(phihat).

The cached exact source ML67,
  MeasureTheory.Integrable.fourierInv_fourier_eq,
now applies to phi at each point: phi is continuous, phi is integrable,
and its Fourier transform is integrable. Thus (R19.7) follows with all
source hypotheses discharged. Inversion is not applied to an arbitrary
L2 function or to a merely measurable function.

LEMMA [R19-B: THE REQUIRED FOURIER UNIQUENESS CONSEQUENCE].
If g in L1 intersection L2 and ghat=0 everywhere, then g=0 almost
everywhere.

Proof.
For every compact smooth test phi, (R19.7) and Fubini give
  integral g(y)*phi(y)dy
    =integral phihat(xi)
          *[integral exp(2*pi*i*xi.y)*g(y)dy]dxi
    =integral phihat(xi)*ghat(-xi)dxi=0.
The double integral is absolutely integrable, with bound
  ||g||_L1*||phihat||_L1,
so Fubini is legitimate. Apply this statement to phi=conj(eta), where
eta ranges over C_c^infinity. It gives <eta,g>=0 for every actual compact
test vector. CP08/ML15 already prove that those vectors are dense in
the actual L2 space. Continuity of the L2 inner product gives
<g,g>=0; hence g=0 almost everywhere.

THEOREM [R19-C: ACTUAL HERMITE L2 COMPLETENESS].
The orthogonal complement of span_C{h_alpha:alpha in N^d} is {0}.

Proof.
Let f in L2 be orthogonal to every h_alpha. By (R19.6),
  integral f(y)*y^alpha*h_0^{(d)}(y)dy=0
for every alpha; these moments are integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz and
the polynomial-Gaussian L2 bounds. Put g=f*h_0^{(d)}. Cauchy--Schwarz gives g in L1,
and boundedness of h_0^{(d)} gives g in L2.

For each R>=0, the majorant |g(y)|*exp(R|y|) is integrable. Indeed,
its integral is bounded by
  ||f||_2*[integral |h_0^{(d)}(y)|^2 exp(2R|y|)dy]^(1/2),
and
  -|y|^2/2+2R|y|<=-|y|^2/4+4R^2.
The latter Gaussian majorant has finite integral.

Fix xi. Expand exp(-2*pi*i*xi.y) by its Taylor partial sums. Each term
is a polynomial in y, so its integral against g is zero. The partial
sums have absolute value at most exp(2*pi*|xi|*|y|). The preceding
majorant and dominated convergence therefore give ghat(xi)=0.
Lemma R19-B implies g=0 almost everywhere. Since h_0^{(d)}(y)>0 at
every y, f=0 almost everywhere. This proves the theorem.

Thus ML68/HilbertBasis.mkOfOrthogonalEqBot may package the already
proved orthonormality and trivial orthogonal complement as the actual
Hilbert basis. ML69/HilbertBasis.hasSum_repr then supplies its L2
expansion. Neither source is used to assume Hermite completeness.

For F in L2, set c_alpha=<h_alpha,F> and
  Pi_K F=sum_{alpha in A_K} c_alpha*h_alpha.
The degree sets A_K exhaust all multiindices and are cofinal among
finite subsets. Consequently

  Pi_K F -> F in L2,
  ||F||_2^2=sum_alpha |c_alpha|^2.                      (R19.8)

The norm identity follows by orthogonality of finite sums and passage
to their L2 limit. Its finite-subset inequality is Bessel's inequality.


14.L.4 OSCILLATOR COEFFICIENT ESTIMATES WITHOUT A SPECTRAL ADMISSION

On Schwartz functions in y define the explicit differential expression

  A_osc=sum_j a_plus,j a_minus,j+Id
       =-Delta_y+|y|^2/4+1-d/2.

It preserves Schwartz functions and is symmetric there by integration
by parts. The ladder identities give
  A_osc h_alpha=(|alpha|+1)h_alpha.
For every integer r>=0 and every Schwartz F, repeated integration by
parts gives

  <h_alpha,A_osc^r F>=(|alpha|+1)^r*c_alpha.

Finite Bessel inequalities followed by monotone limits therefore give

  sum_alpha (|alpha|+1)^(2r)|c_alpha|^2
    <=||A_osc^r F||_2^2<infinity.                      (R19.9)

Equality also follows from (R19.8), but only the displayed bound is
needed. The oscillator is used solely as an explicit symmetric
differential expression on Schwartz functions. No unproved oscillator
domain, spectral resolution or Schwartz-density theorem is invoked.


14.L.5 LADDER WORDS AND EXPLICIT POLYNOMIAL-DERIVATIVE TAILS

The coordinate and derivative identities are
  y_j=a_minus,j+a_plus,j,
  partial_j=(a_minus,j-a_plus,j)/2.
Consider any word of length m<=4 in coordinate multiplications y_j
and coordinate derivatives partial_j, with its order retained.
It expands into at most 2^m ordered ladder words, whose coefficients
have absolute value at most one.

A fixed ladder word sends h_alpha either to zero or to a scalar
multiple of h_{alpha+delta}, where delta is fixed by that word.
The nonzero outputs for different input alpha are orthogonal. Each
of its m scalar factors is at most sqrt(|alpha|+m), so its scalar
coefficient has absolute value at most (|alpha|+m)^(m/2).
For m<=4,
  2^m*(|alpha|+m)^(m/2)<=256*(|alpha|+1)^2,
with the length-zero word treated as the identity. Finite orthogonality
and triangle inequality consequently prove, for every finite expansion,

  ||word(sum_alpha d_alpha h_alpha)||_2
    <=256*[sum_alpha (|alpha|+1)^4|d_alpha|^2]^(1/2).
                                                               (R19.10)

Extension to a Schwartz input is explicit. Formula (R19.9), with r=2,
makes the weighted coefficient tails square-summable. Hence (R19.10)
shows that word(Pi_L F) is Cauchy in L2 as L tends to infinity; call
its actual L2 limit v. For each fixed output index alpha, move the
formal adjoint word onto h_alpha by integration by parts. That adjoint
word is a finite combination of Hermite functions by the ladder
identities. Therefore, for all sufficiently large L, the coefficient
<h_alpha,word(Pi_L F)> already equals <h_alpha,word(F)>.
Continuity of the coefficient functional gives
  <h_alpha,v>=<h_alpha,word(F)>.
Completeness (R19.8) implies v=word(F) in L2. Passing to the limit
in (R19.10) proves the same bound for F. No convergence in Schwartz
topology is assumed at this step.

For R_K=F-Pi_K F, the input coefficients vanish on A_K. If s>=0 is an
integer, then |alpha|+1>=K+2 outside A_K. Use (R19.9) with r=s+2:
  sum_{|alpha|>K} (|alpha|+1)^4|c_alpha|^2
    <=(K+2)^(-2s)*||A_osc^(s+2)F||_2^2.
Applying (R19.10) gives the explicit tail theorem

  ||y^beta partial^gamma(F-Pi_K F)||_2
    <=256*(K+2)^(-s)*||A_osc^(s+2)F||_2,
  |beta|+|gamma|<=4.                                  (R19.11)

All operators in this formula act on actual Schwartz functions. Taking
s=1 proves convergence of every displayed polynomial-derivative norm.
Taking larger s gives every finite algebraic rate, with the stated
Schwartz seminorm on the right. Constants are not asserted uniform
in the cutoff or in the chosen function.


14.L.6 FIXED CENTER/SCALE AND THE ACTUAL NSE WEIGHTED GRAPH NORM

Define the ordinary L2 unitary
  (U_{a,sigma}F)(q)=sigma^(-d/2)*F((q-a)/sigma).
The substitution q=a+sigma*y has Jacobian sigma^d. This proves the
unitarity directly. It preserves Schwartz functions in both directions.
The transported basis and projection are

  e_alpha(q)=U_{a,sigma}h_alpha(q)
    =psi_{a,sigma}(q)
       *product_j He_{alpha_j}((q_j-a_j)/sigma)
          /sqrt(alpha!),
  V_K=span_C{e_alpha:alpha in A_K},
  Pi_K^{a,sigma}=U_{a,sigma} Pi_K U_{a,sigma}^{-1}.      (R19.12)

Thus e_0=psi_{a,sigma}, every e_alpha is real-valued Schwartz, the family
is unweighted orthonormal and complete, and
  V_K={P(q-a)psi_{a,sigma}(q): degree P<=K}.
The spaces are nested, finite-dimensional and use the same ground state
at every K. Each vector in V_K lies in every actual Dom(H_N^r), by CP39.

Conjugation of the actual differential expressions on Schwartz gives
  U^{-1} q_j U=a_j+sigma*y_j,
  U^{-1} partial_{q_j} U=sigma^(-1)*partial_{y_j},
  U^{-1} G U=-sum_j B_j(y)partial_{y_j}-c/2,
  B_j(y)=sigma^(-1)*b_j(a+sigma*y).                     (R19.13)
Each B_j has degree at most two.

For a finite polynomial P let L(P) be its coefficient l1 sum. Define
the explicit finite constants
  A_0=1+sum_j(|a_j|+sigma),
  C_0=|c|/2+sum_j L(B_j),
  C_graph=256*A_0*(1+C_0).

The weighted norm satisfies the exact identity
  ||f||_[1]^2=||f||_2^2+sum_j ||q_j f||_2^2.
Consequently it is at most ||f||_2+sum_j||q_j f||_2.
After conjugation, the terms for f and Gf are finite combinations of
y^beta partial^gamma F with |beta|+|gamma|<=4: G contributes degree at
most two and one derivative, and multiplication by q_j contributes
one additional coordinate. The total absolute coefficient sum is at
most A_0*(1+C_0).

THEOREM [R19-D: QUANTITATIVE SCHWARTZ GRAPH TAIL].
For every Schwartz phi, every K>=0 and integer s>=0, with
F=U_{a,sigma}^{-1}phi,

  ||phi-Pi_K^{a,sigma}phi||_[1]
    +||Gphi-G Pi_K^{a,sigma}phi||_[1]
    <=C_graph*(K+2)^(-s)*||A_osc^(s+2)F||_2.            (R19.14)

Proof.
Use (R19.13), the weighted norm decomposition and (R19.11) term by
term. The coefficient l1 sums are finite, and C_graph was defined to
include all of them. All G actions are actual domain actions because
both phi and the finite projection are Schwartz. In particular every
actual compact core vector phi has a sequence in V_K converging in
both terms of the weighted graph norm, by taking s=1.

This theorem derives the required Schwartz approximation. It does not
assume that Hermite expansions converge in Schwartz topology.


14.L.7 DENSITY IN THE FULL ACTUAL WEIGHTED FIRST GRAPH DOMAIN

Define
  Y_1={y in Dom(G): y in X_1 and Gy in X_1},
  ||y||_graph,1=||y||_[1]+||Gy||_[1].
This is an actual graph space. It is complete: a graph-Cauchy sequence
converges in X_1 in both components; the continuous inclusion X_1->X_0
and closedness of the actual G identify the ordinary limit as (y,Gy).

Fix h>0 and let
  A_h=I-h*G/2,
  S_h=A_h^(-1)
be the already derived actual inverse. CP42 gives
  ||S_h x||_[1]<=||x||_[1].
For x in X_1, the actual resolvent identity gives
  y=S_hx in Y_1,
  Gy=(2/h)(y-x).

CP51 proves that, for every epsilon>0, some phi in the actual compact
smooth core satisfies
  ||A_h phi-x||_[1]<=epsilon.
Put r=A_h phi-x. Since both phi and y are in the actual domain,
  phi-y=S_h r,
  Gphi-Gy=(2/h)[(phi-y)-r].
Thus

  ||phi-y||_[1]+||Gphi-Gy||_[1]
    <=(1+4/h)*||r||_[1].                              (R19.15)

Every y in Y_1 has this resolvent form: set x=A_hy in X_1 and use
the already proved inverse identity S_hA_hy=y. Hence the actual compact
core is dense in Y_1 in its weighted graph norm. This conclusion is
derived from CP51's proved core residual approximation; no new weighted
core hypothesis is introduced.

THEOREM [R19-E: FINITE HERMITE SPANS ARE GRAPH DENSE].
For every y in Y_1 and every epsilon>0, there are K>=0 and v in V_K with

  ||v-y||_[1]+||Gv-Gy||_[1]<epsilon.                   (R19.16)

Proof.
Use (R19.15) to select a compact core phi with graph error <epsilon/2.
Then (R19.14), with s=1, supplies a sufficiently large K for which
v=Pi_K^{a,sigma}phi has graph error from phi <epsilon/2. Add the two
errors. The oscillator seminorm of this selected compact phi is finite,
and the denominator K+2 tends to infinity. This establishes the
existential statement with no unresolved approximation witness.

The nested spaces also give the equivalent distance limit
  inf_{v in V_K} ||v-y||_graph,1 ->0.
Indeed, one successful finite degree remains available at every larger K.

For every x in X_1 and every h>0, use y=S_hx and
  ||A_h(v-y)||_[1]
    <=||v-y||_[1]+(h/2)||Gv-Gy||_[1].
Then

  inf_{v in V_K} ||A_hv-x||_[1] ->0.                  (R19.17)

This is the exact finite-span residual-density interface. Every candidate
v belongs to the actual domain, and its residual is an actual X_1 vector.
The ground, center and scale remain fixed through the entire sequence.


14.L.8 FINITE POLYNOMIAL/GAUSSIAN INTERFACE FOR THE NEXT CHECKPOINT

The Hermite polynomials have the explicit finite coefficients

  He_n(y)=n!*sum_{k=0}^{floor(n/2)}
               (-1)^k*y^(n-2k)/[2^k*k!*(n-2k)!].       (R19.18)

This is proved by induction in He_{n+1}=yHe_n-He_n': coefficients of
the same monomial are combined using the two adjacent factorial terms.
After a common denominator is chosen, their numerator factors are
(n+1-2k) and 2k, whose sum is n+1. Missing endpoint terms are zero.
The base n=0 is one, and the induction reproduces every coefficient.
All factorial denominators are positive integers. Thus each basis
vector is an explicit finite polynomial times the fixed Gaussian.

The unnormalized monomials (q-a)^alpha psi, |alpha|<=K, form another
basis of the same space V_K. Their use avoids Hermite normalization
square roots when those are inconvenient for coefficient enclosures.
This change of finite basis does not change density or actual domains.

For tau=sigma^2, use the already derived actual quadratic multiplier
  V(z)=c/2+[nu*(a+z).A_N*(a+z)+a.b(a+z)]/(2*tau),
and D=b(a+z).nabla_z. For every polynomial P,

  G(P(z)psi)=-[DP+VP](z)psi,
  A_h(P(z)psi)=[P+(h/2)(DP+VP)](z)psi.                (R19.19)

For degree P<=K, the polynomial in the last line has degree <=K+2.
The source of this improvement is the actual NSE energy identity,
not degree-two drift alone. Weighted inner products between any two
such residual basis vectors therefore use Gaussian moments of total
degree at most 2K+6. They are exact finite sums using R15.9/R15.10.
Inner products with any specified polynomial-Gaussian x are likewise
finite moment sums with their corresponding explicit degree bound.
The finite least-residual construction is assigned to the subsequent
checkpoint; no inverse or matrix claim is assumed here.


14.L.9 OPTIONAL FIXED PHASE TRANSPORT

If a fixed momentum p is required, multiply every e_alpha by
exp(i*p.(q-a)/hbar). This is an ordinary and weighted unitary map,
preserves Schwartz functions, and retains orthonormality and the finite
polynomial-span identity with the phased Gaussian ground.
After removing the phase, G acquires the additional zeroth-order term
  -(i/hbar)*p.b(a+sigma*y),
which has degree at most two. The polynomial-derivative order bound
<=4 still holds. Add
  sum_j |p_j|*L(b_j(a+sigma*y))/hbar
to C_0 in (R19.14). All density conclusions then hold with the same
fixed phase at every K. The real family p=0 is the default interface.

14.M ROUND 20: FINITE LEAST RESIDUALS AND RATIONAL POLYNOMIAL TRIALS

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI47]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP55, CP56; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML47, ML53, ML55, ML56, ML60--ML65, ML70--ML72; inherited MT02, MT03, MT05, MT06.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD20--AD24.
  APPLICATION: Actual weighted dissipativity gives Q_K>=Id in normalized Hermite coordinates. Exact
               finite moments give the unique least residual; proved graph density gives convergence
               and rational monomial witnesses with strict margins.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.M.0 EXACT PREDECESSOR INTERFACE AND FROZEN GAUSSIAN

Fix N>=1, nu>0, hbar>0, d=d_N, a in R^d, and sigma>0. Set tau=sigma^2,
z=q-a, and fix the SAME normalized real Gaussian for all trial spaces:
  psi(q)=(2*pi*tau)^(-d/4) exp(-|q-a|^2/(4*tau)).        (R20.01)
Its squared modulus gives the centered Gaussian moment table from CP46.
Retain the actual complex Hilbert space and real subspace of real-valued
states, the closed operator H=H_N, G=-(i/hbar)H, U(t), and
  X_m=L2((1+|q|^2)^m dq;C),
  ||f||_[m]^2=integral (1+|q|^2)^m |f(q)|^2 dq.
Inner products are linear in their second argument. In formulas with
real vectors, the complex Hilbert pairing has a real value.

For h>0, retain the actual bounded inverse and Cayley step
  L_h=Id-hG/2 on Dom(H),
  S_h=L_h^(-1),
  C_h=2S_h-Id.
CP41--CP42 prove the ordinary inverse identities and weighted contraction
of S_h. Its weighted image satisfies
  S_h x in Dom(H),
  G S_h x=(2/h)(S_h x-x) in X_1, x in X_1.              (R20.02)
Thus the actual resolvent maps X_1 to the actual weighted graph domain.
This uses the unbounded inverse identity, not a bounded replacement of G.

The precise CP53--CP54 interfaces used here are:

(HERMITE_INTERFACE)
  Let He_n denote the probabilists' real Hermite polynomial, with
  He_0=1, He_(n+1)(u)=u He_n(u)-He_n'(u), leading coefficient one.
  For alpha in N^d define
    p_alpha(z)=prod_i He_(alpha_i)(z_i/sigma)
                    /sqrt(prod_i alpha_i!),
    e_alpha(q)=p_alpha(q-a)psi(q).
  The states e_alpha are real Schwartz states, unweighted orthonormal,
  and e_0=psi. For I_K={alpha:sum_i alpha_i<=K},
    V_K=span_R{e_alpha:alpha in I_K}
       ={P(q-a)psi(q): P real polynomial, degree P<=K}.  (R20.03)
  The I_K are finite, V_K subset V_(K+1), and the same center and scale
  are used for every K. The monomial/Hermite change of coefficients is
  invertible because the leading coefficient of p_alpha is the nonzero
  number sigma^(-|alpha|)/sqrt(prod_i alpha_i!).

(WEIGHTED_GRAPH_DENSITY_INTERFACE)
  For every real compact smooth phi and every eta>0 there exist K and
  y in V_K with
    ||y-phi||_[1]+||Gy-Gphi||_[1]<eta.                 (R20.04)
  The actual G actions and all weighted memberships are part of the
  predecessor theorem. A stronger Schwartz Hermite-tail theorem may be
  used to prove R20.04; only this explicit consequence is required here.

CP39 supplies actual Schwartz membership in every Dom(H^r), weighted
integrability of every polynomial times psi, and compact smooth cutoff
approximation of Schwartz states simultaneously with H^r in every
polynomial weighted norm. In particular, all vectors in V_K have actual
G actions, not merely formal polynomial derivatives.

The main real theorem below uses x in the real subspace of X_1. A
complex-target extension is stated separately after the real proof.
Real-valuedness is preserved by the drift, its flow, S_h, and L_h on
Schwartz states. If a predecessor graph approximation is initially
complex-valued, taking its real part preserves the real trial space and
does not increase the weighted error for a real target.

14.M.1 ACTUAL WEIGHTED COERCIVITY

For compact smooth phi, CP42 proves
  Re<phi,Gphi>_[1]
    =-nu integral(q.A_N q)|phi(q)|^2 dq<=0.
For a Schwartz y, CP39 supplies phi_l in the actual compact core with
  ||phi_l-y||_[1]+||Gphi_l-Gy||_[1] ->0.
Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz shows convergence of the paired inner products.
Taking limits gives
  Re<y,Gy>_[1]<=0.                                     (R20.05)
The exact integral identity also extends, since the polynomial growth
of q.A_N q is dominated by the available Schwartz weighted tails; the
inequality alone is sufficient for the following proof.

For y in V_K and h>0,
  ||L_h y||_[1]^2
    =||y||_[1]^2-h Re<y,Gy>_[1]+(h^2/4)||Gy||_[1]^2
    >=||y||_[1]^2+(h^2/4)||Gy||_[1]^2
    >=||y||_[1]^2>=||y||_[0]^2.                       (R20.06)
Every term is an actual finite norm or inner product. This is a coercive
estimate on actual domain vectors; it does not assert that G is bounded.

Enumerate I_K once and write
  y(c)=sum_{alpha in I_K} c_alpha e_alpha,
  u_alpha=L_h e_alpha,
  Q_(alpha,beta)=<u_alpha,u_beta>_[1].                  (R20.07)
Here c is real and Q is a real matrix, because the basis states and L_h
are real. Q is symmetric. Unweighted orthonormality gives
  c^T Q c=||L_h y(c)||_[1]^2
    >=||y(c)||_[0]^2=sum_alpha c_alpha^2.
Thus
  Q>=Id, and Q is positive definite.                   (R20.08)
No dimension-dependent coercivity constant is hidden in this statement.
The matrix representation is specifically the orthonormal Hermite one.

Finite Cauchy--Schwarz also gives, for every c,
  ||sum_alpha c_alpha u_alpha||_[1]^2
    <=(sum_alpha c_alpha^2)(sum_alpha||u_alpha||_[1]^2).
Since the second sum is Tr(Q),
  Id<=Q<=Tr(Q)*Id.                                     (R20.09)
The coefficient dimension is finite and nonzero, so Tr(Q)>=1. These
bounds do not claim that Tr(Q) is uniformly bounded in K, h, N or a.

14.M.2 UNIQUE FINITE LEAST-RESIDUAL VECTOR

For x in the real subspace of X_1 define the finite vector
  v_alpha=<u_alpha,x>_[1],
  B_x=||x||_[1]^2.
Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz ensures every entry is finite. By R20.08, Q has
zero kernel; finite-dimensionality makes it invertible. Define
  c_star=Q^(-1)v,
  y_K(x)=sum_alpha(c_star)_alpha e_alpha.              (R20.10)
This is an exact finite-algebraic definition. It does not specify a
numerical inverse oracle.

Expand the actual residual norm:
  F_K(c)=||L_h y(c)-x||_[1]^2
        =B_x-2*c^T v+c^T Q c.
Since Qc_star=v and Q is symmetric, completion of the square yields
  F_K(c)=B_x-v^T Q^(-1)v
           +(c-c_star)^T Q(c-c_star).                  (R20.11)
Hence y_K(x) is the unique least-residual vector in V_K, and
  d_K(x)^2=min_{y in V_K}||L_h y-x||_[1]^2
           =B_x-v^T Q^(-1)v>=0.                       (R20.12)
The nonnegativity is proved by the equality with an actual squared norm;
it is not assumed from a potentially cancellation-sensitive subtraction.
Uniqueness follows from
  F_K(c)-F_K(c_star)>=||c-c_star||_Euclidean^2.

The normal equations are precisely the weighted orthogonality identities
  <L_h e_alpha,L_h y_K(x)-x>_[1]=0 for every alpha.
Taking their linear combination corresponding to y_K(x) gives
  <L_h y_K(x),x>=||L_h y_K(x)||_[1]^2.
Therefore
  ||L_h y_K(x)||_[1]<=||x||_[1],
  ||y_K(x)||_[1]<=||x||_[1],
  ||c_star||_Euclidean<=||x||_[1].                    (R20.13)
The first inequality includes L_h y_K(x)=0 by direct inspection. The
remaining two follow from coercivity and unweighted orthonormality.

Nested trial spaces imply
  0<=d_(K+1)(x)<=d_K(x).                               (R20.14)
This monotonicity concerns the same fixed h, x, Gaussian center and
Gaussian scale. Changing the target x between steps is a separate
application of the theorem, not an instance of R20.14.

14.M.3 FINITE NORMAL-EQUATION RESIDUAL CERTIFICATES

For any finite coefficient vector c, define its normal-equation residual
  s=Qc-v.
Then Q(c-c_star)=s. Write z=c-c_star. Coercivity and Euclidean
Cauchy--Schwarz give
  ||z||^2<=z^TQz=z^Ts<=||z|| ||s||.
If z=0 the next inequality is immediate; otherwise divide by ||z||>0.
Thus
  ||c-c_star||<=||s||,
  F_K(c)-d_K(x)^2=s^TQ^(-1)s<=||s||^2.                (R20.15)
Equivalently, ||Q^(-1)||_Euclidean<=1 and
  ||L_h(y(c)-y_K(x))||_[1]<=||s||,
  ||L_h y(c)-x||_[1]<=d_K(x)+||s||.
These are finite-dimensional a posteriori statements conditional on the
actual coefficient and matrix residual values. They add no algorithm
for solving or verifying exact real equations.

A direct acceptance test can instead use F_K(c), obtained from finite
Gaussian moments below. It requires no evaluation of Q^(-1), c_star or
d_K. The minimizer is useful for the optimality and existence theorem;
the finite coefficient residual itself is sufficient for a certificate.

14.M.4 FINITE POLYNOMIAL ACTION AND EXACT MOMENT MATRICES

Retain the actual NSE polynomial drift b and its constant divergence
c_div=div b. Use the notation from CP46:
  (D P)(z)=b(a+z).nabla_z P(z),
  V(z)=c_div/2-b(a+z).z/(2*tau).
The actual energy identity b(q).q=-nu*q.A_N q gives the equal quadratic
representative
  V(z)=c_div/2+[nu*(a+z).A_N*(a+z)+a.b(a+z)]/(2*tau).
Thus V has degree at most 2. On every polynomial-Gaussian state,
  G(Ppsi)=-(D P+V P)psi,
  L_h(Ppsi)=(T_h P)psi,
  T_h P=P+(h/2)(D P+V P).                             (R20.16)
The plus sign in T_h is forced by G=-(D+V). The equality is an actual
operator equality on Schwartz states supplied by CP39, not a formal
replacement of H. If degree P<=K, then degree(T_h P)<=K+2. The derivative
term has degree at most K+1 when nonzero; the multiplication term has
degree at most K+2. This remains true at K=0.

For a multiindex gamma define the actual centered moment
  m_gamma(tau)=0 if any gamma_i is odd;
  m_(2beta)(tau)=tau^|beta| prod_i (2*beta_i-1)!!,
where (-1)!!=1. Define the weighted moment
  M_gamma(a,tau)=(1+|a|^2)m_gamma
       +2 sum_i a_i m_(gamma+epsilon_i)
       +sum_i m_(gamma+2epsilon_i).                    (R20.17)
CP46 proves actual absolute integrability and
  M_gamma=integral(1+|q|^2)(q-a)^gamma |psi(q)|^2 dq.
No infinite summation or unjustified integral factorization occurs.

Write the finite coefficient tables
  T_h p_alpha=sum_gamma t_(alpha,gamma) z^gamma,
  R=sum_beta R_beta z^beta,
and suppose x=Rpsi. Then
  Q_(alpha,beta)
    =sum_(gamma,delta)t_(alpha,gamma)t_(beta,delta)
                        M_(gamma+delta),
  v_alpha=sum_(gamma,delta)t_(alpha,gamma)R_delta
                        M_(gamma+delta),
  B_x=sum_(gamma,delta)R_gamma R_delta M_(gamma+delta).
                                                               (R20.18)
All sums are finite and have the actual weighted values stated earlier.
The individual off-diagonal M_gamma and matrix entries need not be
nonnegative. Positivity of Q and residual norms follows from their
actual Gram/norm representation.

If degree R<=L, the necessary centered Gaussian moment degrees are:
  Q entries:                    <=2K+6;
  v entries:                    <=K+L+4;
  B_x:                          <=2L+2;
  ||L_h(Ppsi)-Rpsi||_[1]^2:      <=2*max(K+2,L)+2.
                                                               (R20.19)
In particular, choosing K>=L makes degree 2K+6 sufficient for every
entry and residual norm. A target of degree L>K cannot silently be
assigned the smaller 2K+6 bound.

For an arbitrary polynomial trial P with coefficients p_alpha, put
  F=T_h P-R=sum_gamma f_gamma z^gamma.
Its residual has the exact inverse-free expression
  ||L_h(Ppsi)-x||_[1]^2
    =sum_(gamma,delta) f_gamma f_delta M_(gamma+delta).
                                                               (R20.20)
For positive epsilon, proving the finite right side <=epsilon^2 proves
an actual residual norm <=epsilon. The proof also provides every actual
operator-domain and integrability assertion, since Ppsi is Schwartz.

The normalized Gaussian factor cancels in these moment expressions.
Monomial formulas use finite arithmetic in a,tau,h and the actual drift
coefficients, with the fixed nonzero denominator tau in V; no numerical
Gaussian quadrature is needed to state the exact formula. The actual
physical coefficients remain exact real data and are not automatically
finite-bit numbers. The formulas are independent of hbar for the fixed
real Gaussian, since G and T_h are independent of hbar.

14.M.5 LEAST RESIDUALS CONVERGE TO ZERO AND TO THE ACTUAL RESOLVENT

Fix real x in X_1, h>0 and epsilon>0. CP51 already derives a real compact
smooth vector w with
  ||L_h w-x||_[1]<epsilon/2.
For example invoke its non-strict theorem at tolerance epsilon/4. Its
core integral preserves real values; the initial core-density approximant
can be replaced by its real part. There is no new range-density premise.

By R20.04 choose K and y in V_K with
  ||y-w||_[1]+||Gy-Gw||_[1]
    <epsilon/[2*max(1,h/2)].
Then
  ||L_h(y-w)||_[1]
    <=||y-w||_[1]+(h/2)||Gy-Gw||_[1]<epsilon/2,
so
  ||L_h y-x||_[1]<epsilon.
Optimality yields d_K(x)<epsilon. Nestedness now proves
  d_K(x) ->0 as K->infinity.                           (R20.21)
The same conclusion holds when K is restricted to K>=L for any fixed
finite L. No quantitative K(epsilon,x,h) estimate is claimed here.

Let z=S_h x, which has the actual weighted graph membership R20.02.
For r_K=L_h y_K(x)-x, the actual inverse identity gives
  y_K(x)-z=S_h r_K.
Consequently
  ||y_K(x)-S_h x||_[1]<=d_K(x),
  ||G y_K(x)-G S_h x||_[1]<=(4/h)d_K(x).               (R20.22)
The second inequality follows from
  G(y_K-z)=(2/h)[(y_K-z)-r_K].
Thus the finite-dimensional minimizers converge in the actual weighted
G graph to the already derived resolvent vector. This is not merely
weak convergence of coefficient lists.

This argument needs Hermite graph approximation only for compact smooth
w. It does not assume, without proof, that every vector in the actual
weighted graph domain already has a convergent Hermite graph expansion.
The latter density consequence can be recovered from R20.22 afterwards.

14.M.6 MONOMIAL COORDINATES AND RATIONAL TRIAL DENSITY

For alpha in I_K let f_alpha=z^alpha psi. These form a basis of the same
V_K. Let B0 be their unweighted Gaussian moment Gram matrix and Qmon the
weighted image Gram matrix:
  (B0)_(alpha,beta)=m_(alpha+beta),
  (Qmon)_(alpha,beta)=<L_h f_alpha,L_h f_beta>_[1].
If J is the invertible Hermite-coordinate matrix of the monomial basis,
then
  B0=J^T J,
  Qmon=J^T Q J.
Therefore
  Qmon>=B0>0.                                          (R20.23)
In general B0 is not Id. Consequently Qmon>=Id and the unit inverse-norm
bound from R20.15 must NOT be asserted in monomial coefficient norm.
The actual least-residual vector is basis-independent; its coordinates
are related by J. Normal equations in monomial coordinates use Qmon and
the corresponding weighted image moments, with the same minimizer.

Hermite coefficients contain sigma powers and square roots of factorials.
A rational Hermite coefficient vector therefore need not give rational
monomial coefficients. Conversely rational monomial coefficients need
not give rational Hermite coefficients. Each finite rational coefficient
class is separately dense in its finite real coefficient space.

For a chosen real basis f_1,...,f_r of V_K, put
  A_K=sum_i||L_h f_i||_[1].
It is finite and strictly positive: r>=1 and coercivity prevents any
basis image from being zero. For coefficients c and rational q,
  ||L_h sum_i(q_i-c_i)f_i||_[1]
    <=sum_i |q_i-c_i| ||L_h f_i||_[1]
    <=A_K max_i|q_i-c_i|.                              (R20.24)
Scalar rational density supplies arbitrarily small simultaneous finite
coordinate errors. This proves density after applying L_h for either
the Hermite or the monomial basis.

Given real x in X_1 and epsilon>0, R20.21 gives K and a real polynomial
P of degree <=K with residual norm <epsilon/4. Approximate its monomial
coefficients by rationals so that the R20.24 image error is <epsilon/4.
The resulting rational polynomial P_rat satisfies
  P_rat in Q[z_1,...,z_d],
  ||L_h(P_rat psi)-x||_[1]<epsilon/2.                  (R20.25)
A degree constraint K>=L on a polynomial target remains permissible.
The strict margin in R20.25 is available for later certified upper-bound
constructions; it is not merely existence at a possibly undecidable
boundary equality.

For polynomial x=Rpsi, R20.20 is a finite coefficient-and-moment witness
for R20.25. The candidate P_rat itself requires no exact matrix inverse.
The least-residual theorem proves optimality and density; direct finite
residual values suffice to accept any particular rational candidate.

14.M.7 FINITE RATIONAL POLYNOMIAL RECURRENCES AND PATHS

Fix the real Gaussian psi, a finite time grid, and a positive residual
tolerance at each step. Start with R_0=1 and x_0=psi. Inductively choose
by R20.25 a rational polynomial P_j such that, for x_(j-1)=R_(j-1)psi,
  ||[T_(h_j)P_j-R_(j-1)]psi||_[1]<epsilon_j.
Set
  y_j=P_j psi,
  R_j=2P_j-R_(j-1),
  x_j=R_j psi.                                         (R20.26)
Every R_j has rational coefficients. Every y_j and x_j is Schwartz,
lies in every actual Dom(H^r), and has every polynomial weighted norm.
The residual equation is the actual CP50 equation, with
  r_j=[T_(h_j)P_j-R_(j-1)]psi.
Each residual norm is exactly the finite moment sum R20.20. In particular,
  ||x_j-P_j^{Cayley}psi||_[m]
    <=2 sum_(i<=j)||r_i||_[m]
whenever the corresponding weighted residual bounds are supplied. For
the m=1 accuracy budget, CP50 applies directly with no new domain witness.
Here P_j^{Cayley}=C_(h_j)...C_(h_1); it is distinct from the polynomial
trial P_j. Actual weighted2 membership follows from Schwartz regularity,
although only m=1 residual values are budgeted.

A nondecreasing degree choice is available: at step j require the trial
degree K_j to be at least degree R_(j-1), and increase it as needed.
Then degree R_j<=K_j and degree r_j's polynomial<=K_j+2. The moments
through degree 2K_j+6 suffice for each step's weighted residual check.
The degree required at a later step is not inferred from monotonicity
R20.14 for a different target; R20.25 is applied anew to that actual target.

For uniform h=T/n, the piecewise-affine path through the nodes is
  v(t)=[(1-theta)R_(j-1)+theta R_j]psi,
  theta=(t-t_(j-1))/h, t in [t_(j-1),t_j].             (R20.27)
It is continuous in every weighted norm and is Schwartz at every time.
It is defined by finitely many polynomial coefficient tables and the
same actual Gaussian parameters. The unweighted norm squared is the
finite expression
  ||v(t)||_[0]^2
    =sum_(alpha,beta)R_t,alpha R_t,beta m_(alpha+beta)(tau),
  R_t=(1-theta)R_(j-1)+theta R_j.                       (R20.28)
Whenever the CP51/Section14.K state-error estimate is <=e<1, this norm
is >=(1-e)^2>0 and the normalized path v(t)/||v(t)||_[0] is defined.

The actual chord and normalization proofs of Section14.K require only
Schwartz nodes, the residual equations and their weighted budgets.
They therefore give, with the same
  B=T^3||H^3 psi||_[1]/(12*hbar^3)
       +T^2||H^2 psi||_[1]/(8*hbar^2),
  X=||psi||_[1],
  e_bound=B/n^2+2 sum_j||r_j||_[1],
all previously derived affine-path, normalization and unbounded-observable
error estimates whenever the chosen positive accuracy contract holds.
This is a reuse of the inequalities and actual domains, not a claim
that polynomial-Gaussian vectors are compactly supported.

The witness class must be named separately from CORE_W. A polynomial
Gaussian with nonzero polynomial is generally noncompact, so it does
not meet the old CORE_W membership y_j in C_c^infinity. Define POLY_W
using the finite rational polynomial tables, R20.26 and actual residual
moment inequalities. The later rational-box/criterion theorem can use
this new class with its own fixed-family quantifiers. The present
construction is Gaussian-specific and does not narrow or replace the
previous compact-packet conclusions.

14.M.8 COUNTABLE PRESCRIPTION AND COMPLEX-TARGET COROLLARY

Rational polynomials in fixed finitely many variables admit a countable
surjective enumeration: for increasing integer B>=1 enumerate all
coefficient tables of degree <=B whose numerators have absolute value
<=B and denominators lie in {1,...,B}. Each block is finite; every
rational polynomial appears in some block. Duplicate representations
are harmless.

For actual fixed x,h,epsilon, R20.25 shows that the indices with residual
norm <epsilon/2 form a nonempty subset of the natural numbers. Its least
index prescribes a rational trial without a G3 premise. Finite induction
then prescribes a finite sequence. This is a mathematical selection;
no decidability of exact real residual comparisons is inferred. A later
verified refining-box procedure must explicitly supply its own input
semantics and acceptance proof before an effective stopping claim.

For completeness, permit complex target x and complex coefficients in
the span of the same real Hermite basis. The matrix Q remains real
symmetric and acts on complex coefficients by scalar extension. Its
quadratic form satisfies c*Qc>=||c||^2, by applying the real estimate
to the real and imaginary coefficient vectors and adding. The inverse
exists by the same real matrix inverse, and
  v_alpha=<L_h e_alpha,x>_[1],
  c_star=Q^(-1)v,
  d_K(x)^2=||x||_[1]^2-v*Q^(-1)v,                       (R20.29)
where star is conjugate transpose. The value v*Q^(-1)v is real and
nonnegative. Completing the Hermitian square proves all corresponding
least-residual and normal-defect bounds. Graph approximation and rational
trial density follow by separate real and imaginary parts; coefficients
then lie in Q+iQ. The real canonical recurrence R20.26 uses Q coefficients
and requires no complex-rational extension.

14.N ROUND 21: TOTAL RATIONAL RESIDUAL CHECKING AND INPUT ENCLOSURES

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI48]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP57, CP58; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML59--ML65, ML72; inherited MT02, MT03, MT05, MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD20--AD25.
  APPLICATION: Finite rational interval operations enclose exact Gaussian residual squares and
               converge under shrinking input boxes. The total residual checker retains actual-input
               containment as an explicit separate semantic premise.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.N.1. Actual finite data and the distinct polynomial witness class.

Fix N>=1, nu>0, hbar>0 and T>0. Let d=d_N, a=a_N and let the initial
state psi be the real canonical Gaussian, with tau=sigma_N^2>0. Retain
  z=q-a,
  b_i(a+z)=sum_{beta in A_2} b_{i,beta} z^beta,
  V(z)=sum_{beta in A_2} v_beta z^beta,
  (D P)(z)=sum_i b_i(a+z)*partial_i P(z),
  G(P psi)=-(D P+V P)psi.
The actual quadratic multiplier V is the one derived from the exact NSE
energy identity at CP46. These are fixed actual coefficients, not arbitrary
symbols standing in for an unproved flow or generator.

Set E=w_N^2>=1 and g=g_N>=0. Package the finite real parameter vector
  theta=(a,tau,(b_{i,beta}),(v_beta),T,E,g).              (R21.1)
The dimension and coefficient-table shapes are fixed by the actual cutoff.
All interval and polynomial algorithms below operate on these finite shapes.
Their soundness theorem is instantiated at this actual theta.

A trial vector has the form y=P(z)psi with P in Q[z_1,...,z_d]. Its
coefficient table is finite rational data. Such a vector is Schwartz,
but generally is not compactly supported. Define a new POLY witness class;
it is not the earlier CORE class requiring y in C_c^infinity.
The residual identities of CP50 and the interpolation/normalization
inequalities of CP51--CP52 apply because their relevant vector hypotheses
are actual domains and weighted norms. Their use below does not change
the original CORE predicate.

14.N.2. Rational interval arithmetic and its two exact properties.

A rational interval is I=[l,u], l,u in Q, l<=u. Write x in I for its
ordinary real interpretation. Define
  [l,u]+[r,s]=[l+r,u+s],
  -[l,u]=[-u,-l],
  [l,u]*[r,s]=[min(lr,ls,ur,us),max(lr,ls,ur,us)].       (R21.2)
Represent a rational constant c by [c,c]. Define finite sums and natural
powers by iteration, with empty sum [0,0] and empty product [1,1].
Every operation is exact rational arithmetic. Malformed intervals are
rejected before evaluation; no floating-point comparison is used.

For any fixed finite rational polynomial expression F(theta), let
  IntervalEval(F,Box)
be the result obtained by this syntax-directed evaluation.

ENCLOSURE THEOREM.
If every component of theta belongs to its component interval in Box,
then
  F(theta) in IntervalEval(F,Box).                       (R21.3)
Proof: the constant and variable cases are immediate. Addition and
negation preserve the stated endpoint inclusions. A bilinear scalar
product on a rectangle attains its extrema at corners, giving exactly
the multiplication rule. Structural induction proves all finite sums,
products and powers. Repeated occurrences of the same variable may widen
the enclosure but do not invalidate it.

SHRINKING-BOX THEOREM.
Let Box_m contain theta, be contained in a fixed bounded box, and have
maximum component width tending to zero. Then the lower and upper
endpoints of IntervalEval(F,Box_m) both tend to F(theta).  (R21.4)
Proof: every variable interval has both endpoints tending to the same
actual component. The constant case is exact. Addition and negation are
continuous on endpoints. For multiplication, all four corner products
tend to the same product; their finite minimum and maximum therefore
have that limit. Structural induction proves the claim. No derivative
bound, complex root finder or infinite-expression evaluation is used.

14.N.3. Exact weighted residual expressions.

For a rational polynomial P and a current rational polynomial X, define
  L_h^pol P=P+(h/2)*(D P+V P),
  R(P,X,h)=L_h^pol P-X.                                  (R21.5)
Then, as an equality of actual weighted Hilbert vectors,
  (I-hG/2)(P psi)-X psi=R(P,X,h)psi.
The left side is defined because P psi is Schwartz and in actual Dom(H).
If degree(P)<=K and degree(X)<=L, the residual degree is at most
  D_res=max(K+2,L).
All its coefficients are finite rational polynomial expressions in the
actual coefficient data and h. The fixed scalar division by 2 is exact.

For gamma in N^d let m_gamma(tau) denote the centered Gaussian moment
table of CP46 (independent of a), and let
  M_gamma(a,tau)=(1+|a|^2)m_gamma
      +2*sum_i a_i*m_(gamma+eps_i)+sum_i m_(gamma+2eps_i).
These are finite polynomial expressions in a,tau with integer coefficients.
For a real coefficient polynomial R=sum_alpha r_alpha z^alpha, set
  NormSq_1(R;theta)=sum_{alpha,beta} r_alpha*r_beta*M_(alpha+beta).
The established Gaussian moment identity gives
  NormSq_1(R;theta)=||R psi||_[1]^2>=0.                  (R21.6)
Only moments through degree 2*D_res+2 occur. The square is expanded as
the whole finite quadratic expression, including all off-diagonal terms;
an individual interval contribution need not be nonnegative.

For the following interval evaluation, fix a positive integer n and set
h=T/n. Its interval is Box.T divided by n. Hence every residual
coefficient is a finite rational polynomial expression in exactly theta;
the general operator identity R21.5 remains valid for every h>0.

Use finite interval polynomial arithmetic to obtain the coefficient
intervals of R(P,X,h), and then evaluate the finite quadratic moment
expression. The resulting upper endpoint U satisfies
  ||R(P,X,h)psi||_[1]^2<=U                               (R21.7)
whenever the actual inputs lie in the box. For any fixed rational P,X,
U converges to the exact norm square under shrinking boxes, by R21.4.
The nested coefficient evaluation is itself a finite polynomial syntax
tree, so the enclosure and convergence arguments apply without change.

14.N.4. A total finite residual checker.

Inputs: a finite ordered rational box Box for the actual finite parameter
shape; a positive rational tolerance epsilon; a positive natural n; and
a list (P_1,...,P_n) of finite rational polynomials in d variables.
Let h=T/n. In interval evaluation, its interval is Box.T divided by the
already checked positive integer n. Start X_0=1 and repeat, for j=1,...,n:
  R_j=P_j+(T/(2*n))*(D P_j+V P_j)-X_(j-1),
  U_j=upper endpoint of the interval NormSq_1(R_j),
  require U_j<epsilon^2,
  X_j=2*P_j-X_(j-1).                                    (R21.8)
Reject if a shape, interval order, dimension, positive n or positive
epsilon check fails. Reject if Box.tau or Box.T fails its required
strictly positive lower-endpoint test. Accept exactly when all finite
tests pass. This defines a total Boolean function ResidualCheck:
every loop ranges over an explicit finite input list, support set,
multiindex, exponent or coefficient table.

For actual theta in Box, ResidualCheck=true implies
  y_j=P_j psi in Schwartz subset Dom(H),
  x_j=X_j psi=2*y_j-x_(j-1),
  ||(I-hG/2)y_j-x_(j-1)||_[1]<epsilon,    1<=j<=n.       (R21.9)
Proof: each exact polynomial identity is R21.5, and R21.7 plus the
strict acceptance inequality gives the nonnegative norm bound. Every
polynomial-Gaussian vector is Schwartz by CP39. The rational update
X_j=2P_j-X_(j-1) proves actual recurrence and finite representability.

The input-enclosure statement theta in Box is an explicit semantic
premise. ResidualCheck does not itself prove that a rational interval
contains a specified noncomputable Fourier coefficient or other exact
real input. A successful rational comparison is not substituted for
this premise.

14.O ROUND 22: FINITE ACCURACY CERTIFICATES, EXISTENCE AND CONDITIONAL SEARCH

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI49]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP58, CP59; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML47, ML59, ML65, ML72; inherited MT10, MT11.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD17, AD20--AD25.
  APPLICATION: Freeze a rational coarse budget before refining the input enclosure. Strict rational
               residual witnesses yield finite accuracy certificates; a total certified-enclosure
               procedure gives terminating search. Every admitted family retains the exact
               regularity equivalence.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.O.1. Rational coarse budgets without an exact-real ceiling.

Let Box0 be an ordered rational box enclosing actual theta, with strictly
positive lower endpoints for tau and T. From Box0 compute rational upper
endpoints for the finite expressions W=1+|a|^2+d*tau, S_2 and S_3 of CP46.
Set
  Xbar=max(1,upper(W)),
  A2=max(1,upper(S_2)),   A3=max(1,upper(S_3)),
  Tbar=upper(T)>0,
  Ebar=max(1,upper(E)),   gbar=max(0,upper(g)),
  Cbar=max(Ebar,Tbar*gbar/2)>=1,
  Bbar=Tbar^3*A3/12+Tbar^2*A2/8,
  delta_N=1/(N+1)^2,
  e0=delta_N/[4*Cbar*(1+Xbar)^2],
  n=1+ceil_Q_to_N(2*Bbar/e0),
  epsilon=e0/(4*n).                                     (R22.1)
Here ceil_Q_to_N is the ceiling of a nonnegative rational, computed by
integer numerator/positive-denominator division. No exact-real ceiling
comparison occurs. Every denominator is proved positive before division.

Because W>=1 and S_r>=0 at actual theta,
  X=||psi||_[1]=sqrt(W)<=Xbar,
  sqrt(S_2)<=A2,   sqrt(S_3)<=A3,
  C=max(E,T*g/2)<=Cbar,
  B=T^3*sqrt(S_3)/12+T^2*sqrt(S_2)/8<=Bbar.             (R22.2)
The elementary bound sqrt(s)<=max(1,s), s>=0, proves the square-root
steps. Thus all coarse bounds are certified even when a Gram-sum interval
has a negative lower endpoint. The upper endpoints still enclose the
nonnegative actual values.

The rational n satisfies n>=1 and n>=2*Bbar/e0. Hence n^2>=2*Bbar/e0,
and
  B/n^2<=e0/2,
  2*n*epsilon=e0/2,
  0<e0<=1/64.                                           (R22.3)
The last bound uses N>=1, Cbar>=1 and Xbar>=1. Zero actual graph norms
cause no division by zero: the coarse majorants A2,A3 remain at least one.
No division by Bbar or a graph norm is used.

14.O.2. Complete finite certificate and exact soundness theorem.

A certificate W consists of:
  an ordered rational coarse box Box0;
  an ordered rational fine box Box1 componentwise contained in Box0;
  the finite polynomial list (P_1,...,P_n), with n prescribed by R22.1.
The cutoff/dimension and finite coefficient-table shapes are fixed inputs.
All remaining fields are integers and rational finite tables.

Define AccuracyCheck_N(W) to perform the finite shape/order/positivity
and subset tests, compute R22.1 from Box0, and invoke
  ResidualCheck(Box1,epsilon,n,(P_1,...,P_n)).            (R22.4)
It rejects invalid input before any partial denominator operation.
Its arithmetic and control flow are finite; it is a total rational checker.

Define the separate semantic relation
  EnclosesActualData(theta,W) :<=> theta in Box1.         (R22.5)
The checked subset then proves theta in Box0 as well. In particular,
merely knowing theta in Box0 does not discharge R22.5.

SOUNDNESS THEOREM.
For actual NSE Gaussian data theta,
  AccuracyCheck_N(W)=true /\ EnclosesActualData(theta,W)
implies existence of the explicitly specified normalized continuous
polynomial-Gaussian path psi_hat^W with
  sup_(0<=t<=T)|<psi_hat^W(t),E3_N psi_hat^W(t)>-Q_U^E(t)|
    <=delta_N,
  |integral_0^T <psi_hat^W(t),L_N psi_hat^W(t)>dt
       -integral_0^T Q_U^L(t)dt|<=delta_N.              (R22.6)

DERIVATION.
ResidualCheck gives actual Schwartz nodes x_j=X_j psi and residuals
of norm<epsilon. Use the piecewise-affine interpolant through these
nodes on the uniform grid t_j=j*T/n. CP50's residual identity and the
weighted chord proof in CP51 give
  sup_t||v(t)-U(t)psi||_[1]
    <=B/n^2+2*sum_j||r_j||_[1]<=e0.
No compact-support property of y_j is used in this estimate. The old
CORE predicate is not invoked; the current nodes are in POLY.
The ordinary norm is at least 1-e0>0. Define
  psi_hat^W(t)=v(t)/||v(t)||_[0].
Each value remains Schwartz, has actual E3/L multiplier domains, and
the path is continuous in every polynomial weighted norm. As before,
  eta=sup_t||psi_hat^W(t)-U(t)psi||_[1]
    <=e0*(1+X)/(1-e0)<=2*e0*(1+Xbar)<=1.
The two observable errors are bounded by
  C*(2*X+eta)*eta
    <=Cbar*(2*Xbar+1)*2*e0*(1+Xbar)
    <=4*Cbar*e0*(1+Xbar)^2=delta_N.
This proves R22.6, including actual time integrability by continuity.
The normalization is semantic decoding of the finite coefficient path;
its denominator is proved nonzero, not assumed or rounded by the checker.

14.O.3. Certificate existence for every actual finite input.

THEOREM [FINITE_ACCURACY_CERTIFICATE_EXISTENCE].
For every actual theta at fixed N,nu,a_N,T with positive tau,T,
  exists finite W:
    AccuracyCheck_N(W)=true /\ EnclosesActualData(theta,W). (R22.7)

DERIVATION.
Choose a finite rational Box0 whose interior contains theta and whose
tau/T lower endpoints are positive. Density of Q in R supplies every
endpoint; the vector has finitely many components. Fix the rational
numbers n,e0,epsilon computed from this coarse box.

Starting with X_0=1, the rational polynomial-Gaussian residual-density
theorem of CP56 supplies successively P_j in Q[z] with
  ||(I-(T/n)G/2)(P_j psi)-X_(j-1)psi||_[1]<epsilon/2,
  X_j=2*P_j-X_(j-1).
Finite induction completes the entire rational polynomial list. Its
length is the fixed n; its finite degrees need not be known in advance.
Each actual residual square is strictly below epsilon^2/4.

Hold this list, n and the coarse budget fixed. Choose a sequence of
rational fine boxes containing theta, contained in Box0, and shrinking
to theta. R21.4 implies that each computed residual-square upper bound
converges to its actual value. Because the number of residuals is finite
and each has the strict margin epsilon^2/4<epsilon^2, one sufficiently
small fine box makes all U_j<epsilon^2. Choose it as Box1. Every test in
R22.4 passes, proving R22.7.

The coarse and fine boxes have different roles. Refining the fine box
does not change n or epsilon. This avoids a circular search in which a
new enclosure simultaneously changes the target residual tolerance.
No G3 or cutoff-uniform regularity bound enters the construction.

14.O.4. Conditional terminating search from certified refining input boxes.

An EffectiveEnclosure(theta) is an explicit finite-input access contract:
a total procedure terminates on each requested integer m>=0 and returns
a finite ordered rational box B_m containing theta, with its maximum
component width at most 2^(-m), and with the containment and width proofs
retained for each output. Once a coarse box is fixed, use nested boxes
or intersections with it. Every produced box contains the same actual
theta. This contract is not inferred for arbitrary smooth initial data.

Under this contract, the following search terminates at every fixed
cutoff and horizon:
  1. Refine until the tau and T lower endpoints are strictly positive;
     use that box as Box0 and freeze n,e0,epsilon from R22.1.
  2. At stage m, obtain a certified refinement Box_m subset Box0 with
     width tending to zero.
  3. Enumerate all n-tuples of polynomials of total degree<=m, each
     coefficient drawn from the finite set
       Q_m={p/q: p in Z, |p|<=2^m, q in N, 1<=q<=2^m}.
  4. Run AccuracyCheck_N with this fixed Box0, the current Box_m and
     each tuple. Return the first accepted certificate.              (R22.8)

Each stage is finite and uses only rational operations and the stated
input-enclosure procedure. Step1 terminates because tau,T are strictly
positive and the enclosure widths tend to zero. For the fixed coarse
budget, the strict rational tuple constructed in R22.7 has finite degree
and finitely many rational numerators/denominators. It therefore appears
at every sufficiently large stage. R21.4 makes all its residual interval
tests pass at every sufficiently large refinement. A stage satisfying
both requirements exists; the deterministic finite enumeration reaches
an accepted tuple at or before that stage. The returned certificate is
sound by R22.6 and the retained actual enclosure evidence.

No uniform time/space complexity bound is asserted. Termination depends
on the explicit EffectiveEnclosure contract; finite certificate existence
R22.7 does not by itself provide that access for a noncomputable datum.
The checker remains total on every finite input regardless of this search
contract. The search and checker are distinct mathematical functions.

14.O.5. Exact regularity criteria for admitted rational certificate families.

For each N,a,T let theta_(N,a,T) be the actual real canonical Gaussian
data. A family W=(W_(N,a,T)) is admissible exactly when
  AccuracyCheck_N(W_(N,a,T))=true,
  EnclosesActualData(theta_(N,a,T),W_(N,a,T))             (R22.9)
for every indicated cutoff, smooth divergence-free datum and positive
finite horizon. The family is fixed before a common regularity bound
is asserted. R22.7 and ordinary choice prove the class of such families
is nonempty. No effective simultaneous access to all smooth data is
needed for this mathematical existence statement.

Decode the actual normalized continuous paths from each certificate and
define the actual expectations
  Q_cert^E(N,a,T,t)=<psi_hat^W_(N,a,T)(t),
                        E3_N psi_hat^W_(N,a,T)(t)>,
  Q_cert^L(N,a,T,t)=<psi_hat^W_(N,a,T)(t),
                        L_N psi_hat^W_(N,a,T)(t)>.
The exact quantified predicates are
  QREG_cert^W(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall a in C^infinity_sigma(T^3;R^3), forall finite T>0,
      exists finite K>=0,
        forall N>=1, forall t in [0,T], Q_cert^E(N,a,T,t)<=K;
  QLIP_cert^W(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall a in C^infinity_sigma(T^3;R^3), forall finite T>0,
      exists finite L>=0,
        forall N>=1, integral_0^T Q_cert^L(N,a,T,t)dt<=L.
The bounds may depend on nu,hbar,W,a,T, but not on N. The datum retains
its arbitrary conserved mean. Different horizons may decode different
paths; all displayed indices are retained. Since delta_N<=1/4, R22.6
gives, for every prescribed admissible family W,
  QREG_cert^W<=>QREG_Gauss,
  QLIP_cert^W<=>QLIP_Gauss,
  G3<=>QREG_cert^W<=>QLIP_cert^W.                        (R22.10)
Each direction adds 1/4 to the finite common bound. Enclosure admission
is part of the admissible-family definition and is not omitted.

The approximation envelope is summable:
  sum_(N>=1)delta_N<=1,
by the already derived telescoping comparison. Under G3, each continuum
observable error is at most delta_N plus the previously established
conditional exact-Gaussian continuum error. Only delta_N is asserted
summable; the full O(N^(-1)) continuum term retains its earlier scope.

SCOPE AND EVIDENCE.
  Finite rational accuracy checker: explicitly defined and B-tier sound.
  Actual input enclosure: explicit semantic premise of checker soundness.
  Finite certificate plus actual enclosure: exists at every finite input.
  Terminating search: conditional on EffectiveEnclosure(theta).
  Universal regularity bound: unresolved.
  Finite checker for universal NSE regularity: not constructed.
  Local Lean/lake/CI executions: zero.
  Matching external checker/kernel/axiom evidence: absent.
  No A-tier or unconditional NSE-regularity promotion follows.


14.P ROUND 23: CERTIFIED REAL NAMES AND FINITE EXPRESSION ACCESS

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI50]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP60; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML43, ML60--ML65, ML73--ML77.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD25, AD26.
  APPLICATION: Guarded rational reciprocals, zero-safe root bisection and a finite-geometric
