               actual-pi enclosure yield total certified names for well-formed finite circuits.
               Actual input-name semantics and every operation domain remain explicit.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.P.0 SCOPE.
All statements concern actual real numbers and finite rational programs.
No numerical enclosure is interpreted as proof that it contains an
unrelated actual parameter. Correctness of an input name is retained
explicitly; the subsequent Fourier construction discharges it for its
specified finite input class.

14.P.1. Exact representation and finite interval operations.

A certified rational name for x in R is a finite program A such that
every call A(p), p in N, terminates and returns ordered rationals
  l_p<=u_p,   x in [l_p,u_p],   u_p-l_p<=2^(-p).          (R23.1)
The containment and width assertions are mathematical correctness
properties of this program. They are not inferred merely from its
returning two rationals. A name may be supplied with these proofs or
constructed by the derivations below. Arbitrary smooth data are not
assumed to have such finite programs.

Any name can be made nested. For request p run the finitely many calls
A(0),...,A(p) and return
  [max_(j<=p) l_j, min_(j<=p) u_j].
The actual x belongs to every interval, so their intersection is
nonempty. It is contained in the p-th interval and retains its width
bound. The finite maximum/minimum calculations and all calls terminate.
For finitely many names, use this operation coordinatewise. The result
is a total nested rational-box name for the actual vector, with maximum
component width at most 2^(-p).                         (R23.2)

Use the rational addition, negation, multiplication and natural-power
operations of R21.2. Their soundness is R21.3. For bounded intervals I,J,
with M_I=max(|left I|,|right I|) and similarly M_J,
  width(I+J)=width(I)+width(J),
  width(-I)=width(I),
  width(I*J)<=M_I*width(J)+M_J*width(I).                 (R23.3)
To prove the product bound, compare any two corner products:
  |xy-x'y'|<=|x|*|y-y'|+|y'|*|x-x'|.
The extremal corners defining I*J satisfy the same inequality.

For the extra real operations used below define
  max(I,J)=[max(left I,left J),max(right I,right J)],
  min(I,J)=[min(left I,left J),min(right I,right J)].
For abs(I), the upper endpoint is M_I; the lower endpoint is zero if
I contains zero and otherwise min(|left I|,|right I|).
These operations enclose the respective actual values. If both input
endpoints tend to their actual values, their output endpoints do too,
by the elementary continuity of min,max and absolute value. In
particular, none requires deciding a comparison between exact reals.

14.P.2. Reciprocal access with an explicit nonzero premise.

For I=[l,u] satisfying l>0 or u<0, define
  Inv(I)=[1/u,1/l].                                    (R23.4)
The rational sign test is decidable and its two denominators are
nonzero. The reciprocal map is decreasing on either component of
R\{0}; hence x in I implies 1/x in Inv(I). Its exact width is
  width(Inv(I))=(u-l)/|l*u|.
If dist(I,0)>=kappa>0, this is at most width(I)/kappa^2.

Suppose the actual named x is nonzero. Since l_p,u_p tend to x,
every sufficiently fine interval lies strictly on its side of zero.
On that tail its distance from zero is at least |x|/2. The inverse
width therefore tends to zero. For requested precision r, enumerate
p=0,1,... until the sign test passes and width(Inv(I_p))<=2^(-r).
Each stage terminates, the success tests use exact rational arithmetic,
and a successful stage exists. This proves a total certified name
for 1/x under the stated nonzero premise.

No computable lower bound for |x| is silently assumed. The search
discovers a positive rational separation and terminates because x!=0.

14.P.3. Rational square-root brackets and real-name transport.

For rational a>=0, start the interval [0,B] with B=max(1,a). Then
  0<=a<=B^2.
For any current [l,u] with l,u>=0 and l^2<=a<=u^2, let b=(l+u)/2.
If b^2<=a replace l by b; otherwise replace u by b. The new interval
retains the invariant and halves its width. Thus the loop stopping
when u-l<=2^(-r) terminates and returns
  l<=sqrt(a)<=u,   l,u in Q,   u-l<=2^(-r).             (R23.5)
The lower and upper implications are the nonnegative square comparisons
of ML77/Real.le_sqrt and ML76/Real.sqrt_le_iff. Their nonnegativity
hypotheses are supplied by the bisection invariant.
Termination also follows directly: after k iterations the width is
B*2^(-k), eventually below the prescribed positive rational tolerance.
Every test is a rational square comparison.

For actual named x>=0, obtain an input interval I=[l,u] at precision
2*r+4 and put L=max(0,l), U=max(0,u). Then
  0<=L<=x<=U,   U-L<=2^(-2*r-4).
Use R23.5 to enclose sqrt(L) and sqrt(U), each with width<=2^(-r-2),
and return the lower endpoint for sqrt(L) and upper endpoint for sqrt(U).
The actual sqrt(x) lies between them. Moreover
  sqrt(U)-sqrt(L)<=sqrt(U-L).                          (R23.6)
For a direct proof, square the nonnegative left side:
  (sqrt(U)-sqrt(L))^2
    =U+L-2sqrt(U*L)<=U-L,
because sqrt(U*L)>=L follows from U>=L>=0.
The returned interval consequently has width at most
  2^(-r-2)+2*2^(-r-2)=3*2^(-r-2)<2^(-r).
This is a total name for sqrt(x), including x=0. A strictly positive
lower bound is required only when a later reciprocal uses this root.

14.P.4. Actual pi from finite rational sums with an explicit error.

For an integer m>=1, the finite geometric identity is
  1/(1+x^2)
    =sum_(k<m)(-1)^k*x^(2*k)+(-1)^m*x^(2*m)/(1+x^2).
All terms are continuous on [0,1]. Integrating termwise in this finite
sum, and using 1+x^2>=1, gives
  integral_0^1 1/(1+x^2)dx
    =S_m+(-1)^m R_m,
  S_m=sum_(k<m)(-1)^k/(2*k+1),
  R_m=integral_0^1 x^(2*m)/(1+x^2)dx,
  0<=R_m<=1/(2*m+1).                                  (R23.7)
The monomial integral follows from its explicit polynomial
antiderivative. No infinite-series interchange is used.

ML73/Real.hasDerivAt_arctan and ML43 give
  integral_0^1 1/(1+x^2)dx=arctan(1)-arctan(0).
ML74/Real.arctan_zero and ML75/Real.arctan_one identify this actual
number as pi/4. For even m,
  pi in [4*S_m,4*S_m+4/(2*m+1)].                       (R23.8)

For requested p>=0 set m=2^(p+1), an even integer at least two.
Then the interval in R23.8 has rational endpoints and width
  4/(2*m+1)<2^(-p).
The finite sum is computed by rational integer arithmetic. Its lower
endpoint is at least 4*S_2=8/3: every additional even pair has sum
1/(4*j+1)-1/(4*j+3)>0. The upper endpoint equals 4*S_(m+1);
these odd partial sums decrease when two more terms are added.
Thus the prescribed pi intervals are nested, strictly positive and
constitute a certified rational name for the actual pi.              (R23.9)
No convergence rate for an unproved pi representation is assumed.

14.P.5. Total access to finite arithmetic circuits.

A circuit is a finite expression tree built from rational constants,
actual input reals with certified rational names, pi, addition, negation,
multiplication, natural powers, reciprocal, square root, abs, min and
max. At every reciprocal node require the actual denominator nonzero;
at every square-root node require the actual radicand nonnegative.
These are explicit semantic domain premises.

THEOREM [FINITE_CIRCUIT_NAME].
Every such circuit has a total certified rational name.              (R23.10)

Proof.
Rational constants have singleton names and pi has R23.9. The finite
interval operations for addition, negation, multiplication and powers
are sound; their endpoints converge by finite induction as all input
precision indices tend to infinity. For any requested output width,
enumerate common input precisions until the rational width test passes.
R23.3 and boundedness of the convergent input intervals prove termination.
The same reasoning applies to abs,min,max by their endpoint continuity.
Reciprocal and square-root nodes use the total procedures R23.4--R23.6,
with their stated actual-domain hypotheses. Structural induction over
the finite circuit proves soundness, totality and the output width.
There is no recursive call to the theorem being constructed and no
unbounded loop without a proved eventual rational acceptance condition.

For a finite vector of circuits, evaluate each to precision p, then
intersect previous returned boxes to obtain R23.2. Therefore
  finite certified input names + proved circuit domain conditions
    => total EffectiveEnclosure(actual circuit vector).             (R23.11)
The vector dimension is fixed by its finite syntactic input.

For later guarded algorithms one may generate a nested stream one box
at a time. If a coarse box B is frozen at some index, each subsequent
box is intersected with B. Actual containment is retained; widths still
tend to zero. Positivity of any actual component ensures that its lower
endpoint is eventually positive. These assertions are derived from
the named actual values, not from an assumption that the program has
recognized an arbitrary real's sign.

14.Q ROUND 24: EXPLICIT FOURIER COEFFICIENT CIRCUITS AND ACTUAL INPUT ACCESS

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI51]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP61, CP62; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML01--ML03, ML60--ML64, ML73--ML78; MT02, MT03, MT05, MT10.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD01--AD04, AD20, AD26, AD27.
  APPLICATION: An integer-enumerable real transverse frame computes actual projected interactions by
               finite character resonances. Canonical Gaussian parameters then have certified names;
               the finite rational-trigonometric class supplies its own exact Fourier lookup.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.Q.0 SCOPE.
Construct certified refining rational enclosures of the actual parameter
vector theta used by the Gaussian accuracy checker. The construction
uses a specified enumerable real Fourier basis, retains all mean modes,
and obtains every interaction coefficient by a finite character sum.
It does not infer effective access from smoothness alone.

The arithmetic predecessor is CP60 / Section14.P: total certified names
are closed under finite rational arithmetic, positive reciprocals and
positive square roots, and a total certified name for pi is constructed
there. Those arithmetic conclusions are derived predecessors, not new
input-access assumptions in the finite rational-data theorem below.


14.Q.1 A FIXED ENUMERABLE FULL REAL FOURIER BASIS

Use the unit torus T^3=(R/Z)^3 with volume one and characters
  chi_k(x)=exp(2*pi*i*k.x),   k in Z^3.
For N>=1 put
  F_N={k in Z^3:0<r(k)<=N^2},
  r(k)=k_1^2+k_2^2+k_3^2,
  K_N={k in F_N:the first nonzero coordinate of k is positive}.
                                                              (R24.1)
Thus exactly one of k,-k belongs to K_N for every k in F_N.
Enumerate K_N by the lexicographic order on the finite integer box
[-N,N]^3, filtering by the two displayed integer predicates.
Every mode in F_N lies in that box, since |k_j|<=|k|<=N.
All mode-membership and ordering tests are exact finite integer tests.

For a nonzero k put s(k)=k_1^2+k_2^2. If s(k)>0, define

  p_1(k)=(-k_2,k_1,0)/sqrt(s(k)),
  p_2(k)=(-k_1*k_3,-k_2*k_3,s(k))/sqrt(s(k)*r(k)).       (R24.2)

If s(k)=0, define p_1(k)=(1,0,0), p_2(k)=(0,1,0).
The branch is decided on integers. In the first branch, both radical
arguments are positive integers. In the second branch, k_3!=0 and the
two displayed standard vectors are transverse to k.

Direct coordinate identities give, in the first branch,
  k.(-k_2,k_1,0)=0,
  k.(-k_1*k_3,-k_2*k_3,s)=0,
  (-k_2,k_1,0).(-k_1*k_3,-k_2*k_3,s)=0,
  |(-k_2,k_1,0)|^2=s,
  |(-k_1*k_3,-k_2*k_3,s)|^2=s*r.
Positivity of the radicals therefore proves
  p_u(k).p_v(k)=delta_uv,  k.p_u(k)=0.
These identities also hold in the second branch. Consequently p_1,p_2
are an explicitly chosen real orthonormal basis of the two-dimensional
plane k^perp. No spectral decomposition or arbitrary polarization
selection is used. The polarization rule depends on k, not on N.

Define the basis fields as follows:
  e_{mean,j}(x)=the j-th standard vector, j=1,2,3;
  e_{k,u,c}(x)=sqrt(2)*p_u(k)*cos(2*pi*k.x);
  e_{k,u,s}(x)=sqrt(2)*p_u(k)*sin(2*pi*k.x),
    k in K_N, u in {1,2}.                              (R24.3)
Order the three means first, followed by lexicographic k, polarization
u and the order c,s. This specifies a concrete finite label set and a
concrete bijection with Fin(d_N).

THEOREM [R24-A: EXPLICIT FULL REAL EIGENBASIS].
The fields in (R24.3) form a real L2-orthonormal Fourier eigenbasis of
the actual full space V_N of Section2, with

  d_N=3+4*card(K_N),
  lambda_mean=0,
  lambda_{k,u,c}=lambda_{k,u,s}=4*pi^2*r(k).             (R24.4)

Proof.
The constant fields are orthonormal because the torus has volume one.
For nonzero integer k, character orthogonality gives
  integral cos(2*pi*k.x)^2 dx=1/2,
  integral sin(2*pi*k.x)^2 dx=1/2,
  integral sin(2*pi*k.x)cos(2*pi*k.x)dx=0.
Different representatives in K_N are neither equal nor negatives, so
all mixed-frequency inner products vanish. Transverse polarization
orthogonality gives the remaining vector inner products. The factors
sqrt(2) give norm one. Each field has zero divergence, since k.p_u=0,
and differentiating twice gives the eigenvalues in (R24.4).

A real solenoidal Fourier field supported on |k|<=N has arbitrary real
mean and, on each pair +/-k, two independent real transverse cosine
coefficients and two independent real transverse sine coefficients.
The p_u span k^perp, so those coefficients lie in the span of (R24.3).
This proves spanning of the actual V_N and the dimension formula.
In particular, the mean coordinates are included rather than restored
by an unproved zero-mode convention.

Selected sources: existing ML02/UnitAddTorus.orthonormal_mFourier and
the CP02/CP03 realification interfaces; the real sine/cosine transport
and the displayed coordinate identities are new explicit adapters.


14.Q.2 EXACT FINITE INTERACTION COEFFICIENTS

For each real basis label j write
  e_j(x)=sum_{r in S_j} zeta_j(r)*chi_r(x),
with zeta_j(r) a complex three-vector. Extend zeta_j(r)=0 outside S_j.
The exact finite tables are:
  mean j: S_j={0}, zeta_j(0)=the j-th standard vector;
  cosine (k,u): S_j={k,-k},
    zeta_j(k)=p_u(k)/sqrt(2),
    zeta_j(-k)=p_u(k)/sqrt(2);
  sine (k,u): S_j={k,-k},
    zeta_j(k)=-i*p_u(k)/sqrt(2),
    zeta_j(-k)= i*p_u(k)/sqrt(2).                       (R24.5)
Thus zeta_j(-r)=conj(zeta_j(r)). Each real and imaginary component
is a finite expression in integers, rational arithmetic and positive
integer square roots and their inverses.

Character multiplication and torus orthogonality give
  chi_r*chi_s=chi_{r+s},
  integral conj(chi_t)*chi_{r+s}=1 if t=r+s, else 0.
The first identity is the exact pointwise ML78 endpoint
UnitAddTorus.mFourier_add; the second follows from existing ML02.
Differentiation gives partial_m chi_s=2*pi*i*s_m*chi_s.

THEOREM [R24-B: FINITE RESONANCE FORMULA].
The actual coefficients of Section2, with the advecting argument first,
are

  C_{ell,i,j}
    =Re[2*pi*i*sum_{r in S_i, s in S_j}
         (zeta_i(r).s)
         *sum_m conj(zeta_ell(r+s)_m)*zeta_j(s)_m].     (R24.6)

All dots before complex conjugation denote the ordinary complex-bilinear
coordinate sum; the conjugated output amplitude is written explicitly.
There are at most four frequency pairs in the displayed sum. A missing
output frequency contributes zero by the stated table convention.

Proof.
Expand the finite product (e_i.nabla)e_j using (R24.5). Its coefficient
at frequency r+s is
  2*pi*i*(zeta_i(r).s)*zeta_j(s).
Pairing with the real field e_ell is the complex Hilbert pairing with
that same real field. Fourier orthogonality therefore leaves exactly
the terms (R24.6). The integral is real because every field in its
original definition is real; taking its real part consequently preserves
its value. No limiting Fourier series or numerical integration is used.

These are also the exact projected coefficients. Since e_ell belongs
to V_N and is divergence free, orthogonal projection gives
  <e_ell,Pi_N P((e_i.nabla)e_j)>
    =<e_ell,(e_i.nabla)e_j>.
Thus the computed tensor realizes the exact B_N and actual drift,
including the source Leray projection, rather than an unprojected
replacement equation.

For a constant output field, the only surviving frequencies satisfy
r+s=0. The term zeta_i(r).s then vanishes by transversality, including
the case r=s=0 where the derivative frequency is zero. Hence the three
constant output rows C_{mean,i,j} are exactly zero, consistently with
mean conservation.

Complex arithmetic in (R24.6) is a finite abbreviation: represent each
component by its real and imaginary parts and use
(x+i*y)(u+i*v)=(xu-yv)+i(xv+yu). Therefore every C_{ell,i,j} is a
finite real expression using rational constants, pi, arithmetic and
positive integer radicals/inverses. No trigonometric integral remains
in the parameter-construction algorithm.


14.Q.3 DIMENSION, TRACES AND THE CANONICAL GAUSSIAN SCALES

Let
  S_N=sum_{k in K_N} r(k).
The mode (1,0,0) belongs to K_N for N>=1, so S_N>=1. From (R24.4),

  Tr(A_N)=16*pi^2*S_N
         =8*pi^2*sum_{k in F_N}r(k),
  c=div b_N=-nu*Tr(A_N),
  g_N=sqrt(Tr(A_N))=4*pi*sqrt(S_N),
  E_N=w_N^2=(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^3,
  tau_N=sigma_N^2=1/[(N+1)^2*E_N*d_N].                (R24.7)

The positive square root in the formula for g_N is unambiguous because
pi>0 and S_N>0. The divergence equality is the already proved actual
CP07 trace identity, now specialized to this explicit basis. The
pointwise gradient bound with g_N is the already proved CP40 identity.

All quantities in (R24.7) are finite expression values. In particular,
E_N>=1, d_N>=3 and (N+1)^2 E_N d_N>0. The only reciprocal used to
construct tau_N has a structurally positive denominator. The canonical
variance agrees exactly with CP39 and is not an independently selected
width. No fractional real power is required to construct E_N.


14.Q.4 ACTUAL INITIAL COORDINATES FROM FINITELY MANY FOURIER COEFFICIENTS

Use the document's Fourier convention
  a_hat(k)=integral_T^3 exp(-2*pi*i*k.x)*a(x)dx.
For real smooth divergence-free a,
  a_hat(-k)=conj(a_hat(k)),
  k.a_hat(k)=0,
and a_hat(0) is the actual arbitrary conserved mean.

In the basis (R24.3), the exact coordinates of Pi_N a are

  (a_N)_{mean,j}=Re(a_hat(0)_j),
  (a_N)_{k,u,c}=sqrt(2)*p_u(k).Re(a_hat(k)),
  (a_N)_{k,u,s}=-sqrt(2)*p_u(k).Im(a_hat(k)).           (R24.8)

Proof.
Re(a_hat(k))=integral cos(2*pi*k.x)*a(x)dx and
Im(a_hat(k))=-integral sin(2*pi*k.x)*a(x)dx. Pair these identities
with the real polarization and the sqrt(2) normalization. The mean
formula follows by the constant basis pairing. This is exactly
a_N=I_N^(-1)(Pi_N a), by CP03 and ML03's coefficient identification.
The negative sign in the sine coordinate is fixed by the stated
Fourier convention.

Only the modes {0} union K_N are needed. No Fourier tail bound is an
input to (R24.8), because Pi_N is the exact finite cutoff. The existence
of an actual coefficient integral does not itself provide an algorithm
for enclosing its value; the input-access contract is specified below.


14.Q.5 THE COMPLETE ACTUAL CHECKER PARAMETER CIRCUIT

Use the basis (R24.3) and coefficients (R24.6) to define
  b_j(q)=-nu*lambda_j*q_j-sum_{k,l}C_{jkl}q_k q_l.
All sums are finite. For z=q-a_N expand
  b_j(a_N+z)=sum_{beta in A_2} b_{j,beta} z^beta.
Explicitly, the shifted coefficients are
  constant: b_j(a_N);
  z_m: -nu*lambda_j*delta_jm
                  -sum_l(C_{jml}+C_{jlm})(a_N)_l;
  z_m^2: -C_{jmm};
  z_m*z_n, m<n: -(C_{jmn}+C_{jnm}).                   (R24.9)
No symmetry of C in its last two indices is assumed.

Construct the actual Gaussian multiplier by the proved energy identity:

  V_N(z)=c/2+
    [nu*(a_N+z).A_N*(a_N+z)+a_N.b_N(a_N+z)]/(2*tau_N)
        =sum_{beta in A_2}v_beta z^beta.                (R24.10)

Its coefficients are obtained by finite polynomial addition and
multiplication. Its degree is at most two structurally; no numerical
test of cubic cancellation is required. Equation (R24.10) is the exact
CP46 multiplier, since b_N(q).q=-nu*q.A_N*q.

Now form exactly the parameter vector of R21.1:

  theta_N=(a_N,tau_N,(b_{j,beta}),(v_beta),T,E_N,g_N).   (R24.11)

For the fixed finite shapes, every component of theta_N is a finite
expression in:
  the real and imaginary input Fourier coefficients at {0} union K_N;
  nu and T;
  rational constants and the fixed real constant pi;
  addition, subtraction, multiplication, positive reciprocals and
  positive square roots.

All radical denominators in the frame have positive integer arguments;
the denominator for tau_N is positive by (R24.7). The multiplier may
equivalently use 1/(2*tau_N)=(N+1)^2 E_N d_N/2, removing its reciprocal
node entirely. The circuit therefore includes explicit proofs of every
strict positivity condition required by the arithmetic predecessor.

The dimension, coefficient-table shapes and finite circuit syntax are
computed by integer enumeration from N. The actual tensor and projection
identities are proved before these expressions are supplied to the
checker. Thus a parameter-circuit output is not an arbitrary polynomial
vector standing in for an unproved NSE realization.

The vector theta_N contains no hbar. In the real canonical Gaussian
route, G, H/hbar and the normalized graph quantities used by the
schedule are independent of hbar. No name or finite representation of
hbar is required; hbar may remain an arbitrary positive real number.


14.Q.6 TOTAL CERTIFIED INPUT NAMES AND THE ENCLOSURE CONSTRUCTION

A certified real input name for x is a total procedure Name_x(m),
m>=0, which terminates and returns a finite ordered rational interval
I_m containing x, together with the containment and width guarantees
  width(I_m)<=2^(-m).
A complex three-vector name supplies such names for its six real and
imaginary components. This is an explicit access hypothesis, not a
consequence of the existence of an exact real number.

At one fixed cutoff N, assume certified names for:
  nu>0 and T>0;
  a_hat(0), and a_hat(k) for the finitely many k in K_N,
where the names are certified to enclose the actual Fourier coefficients
of the same given real smooth divergence-free datum a.

THEOREM [R24-C: EFFECTIVE FINITE PARAMETER ENCLOSURE].
Under precisely these finite input-name assumptions, the actual
theta_N in (R24.11) has an EffectiveEnclosure(theta_N) procedure in the
exact sense of R22.8: every requested integer precision terminates,
returns a finite ordered rational box containing theta_N, and retains
the containment and requested width guarantees.                 (R24.12)

Proof.
Build the finite syntax for (R24.1)--(R24.11). All integer filters,
polarization branches, table lookups and finite coefficient loops
terminate. Instantiate CP60's certified pi name and positive-radical
procedures at the explicit integer frame arguments and S_N. Compose
the given Fourier/nu/T names with the finite arithmetic circuits.
CP60 proves totality, actual-value enclosure and arbitrarily small
requested widths for each resulting scalar name, including all
positive inverse/root nodes. On request m, call the finitely many
component names at precision m and concatenate the intervals.
Their maximum width is at most 2^(-m), and each actual component is
contained. Finite composition of terminating calls terminates.

Equivalently, one may refine a common leaf precision until every
expression is defined on its positive interval domain and every output
width is <=2^(-m). CP60's convergence and the proved positive arguments
ensure termination. No exact-real equality test or integration oracle
is introduced by either implementation.

The resulting boxes need not be nested. Intersections of finitely many
previous boxes remain rational, contain the same actual vector and do
not increase widths. Thus the coarse/fine refinement convention of
Section14.O is satisfied without changing any actual parameter.

Uniform-cutoff version.
If one total provider accepts (k,m) and supplies the certified actual
Fourier coefficient box at every k in Z^3, the same construction is
one total procedure accepting (N,m). Each call queries only the finite
set {0} union K_N. A collection of nonuniform existential names is not
silently promoted to this single uniform provider.

There is no need for an effective bound on the Fourier tail or on a
continuum solution to construct one finite theta_N. Conversely, ordinary
smoothness, reality and solenoidality do not imply that the supplied
Fourier coefficient integrals are computable. They remain semantic
admissibility facts about a; effective access is the stated additional
name hypothesis.


14.Q.7 FINITE RATIONAL-TRIGONOMETRIC INPUT CLASS

A finite datum consists of:
  m in Q^3;
  a finite list of distinct representatives k in Z^3 with first nonzero
    coordinate positive;
  A_k,B_k in Q^3 with k.A_k=k.B_k=0;
  rational nu>0 and rational T>0.
All frequencies are nonzero. The finite shape, distinctness, positivity
and transverse dot-product conditions are decidable integer/rational
tests. Define the actual periodic field

  a(x)=m+sum_{k in the list}
       [A_k cos(2*pi*k.x)+B_k sin(2*pi*k.x)].           (R24.13)

Finite trigonometric differentiation proves that a is real, periodic,
smooth and divergence free. Its mean is exactly m; it need not vanish.
Character orthogonality computes its actual Fourier coefficients:

  a_hat(0)=m,
  a_hat(k)=(A_k-i B_k)/2 for a listed positive representative,
  a_hat(-k)=(A_k+i B_k)/2 for its negative,
  a_hat(l)=0 at every other frequency.                 (R24.14)

Every coefficient in (R24.14) is an exact complex rational vector.
An integer lookup in the finite list returns its value. Singleton
rational intervals therefore give total certified coefficient names
uniformly in the queried frequency and requested precision. Singleton
intervals also name nu and T.

THEOREM [R24-D: UNCONDITIONAL ACCESS WITHIN THE FINITE INPUT CLASS].
For every valid finite datum (R24.13), every N>=1 and every requested
precision, a specified total procedure constructs a certified rational
box for the actual theta_N, uniformly in N and precision, without any
additional Fourier-input or real-number access premise.           (R24.15)

Proof.
Use the exact finite lookup names (R24.14), the rational nu/T names,
and the already constructed pi/root/arithmetic procedures in R24-C.
All positivity and transverse conditions are the verified finite input
conditions or the derived identities (R24.2)/(R24.7). Every coordinate
of a_N is given explicitly by
  (a_N)_{mean,j}=m_j,
  (a_N)_{k,u,c}=p_u(k).A_k/sqrt(2),
  (a_N)_{k,u,s}=p_u(k).B_k/sqrt(2),
with zero values for unlisted modes and exact cutoff restriction to
r(k)<=N^2. The actual projected datum is therefore identified without
integration or approximation of the original physical field.

The resulting a_N and drift coefficients need not be rational: the
normalizations contain radicals and the derivative coefficients contain
pi. Their effective enclosures are derived by the finite circuits;
rationality of those physical parameter values is not asserted.

Composition with CP59's already proved conditional search theorem now
gives a terminating accepted finite accuracy certificate at each finite
cutoff and positive rational horizon for this input class, with actual
fine-box enclosure proved by construction. This composition requires
no supplied enclosure oracle. It is a theorem about this declared finite
input class, not an unconditional-closure or NSE-regularity promotion.


14.Q.8 BASIS AGREEMENT AND THE LIMIT OF EFFECTIVE TRANSPORT

The effective construction fixes precisely the basis (R24.3) as the
CP02 eigenbasis for this computational realization. Section2 permits
such an orthonormal eigenbasis, and every required normalization,
projection and drift identity has been proved above. Thus the computed
theta_N is the actual R21.1 vector for that specified realization.

For comparison with an earlier independently fixed real orthonormal
basis, let I_old be its coordinate map and I_eff the map (R24.3).
There is an orthogonal matrix O_N such that
  I_eff(r)=I_old(O_N r).
CP14 / Section7.A.1 then gives

  b_eff(r)=O_N^T b_old(O_N r),
  a_eff=O_N^T a_old,
  H_eff=W_O H_old W_O^(-1),
  U_eff(t)=W_O U_old(t) W_O^(-1).                     (R24.16)

The canonical Gaussian is isotropic. Therefore its real profiles
transform exactly under O_N with the transformed center, while the
canonical sigma_N, d_N, E_N and g_N are unchanged. The |q|-weighted
norms and actual physical multiplier expectations are preserved by
this orthogonal coordinate transport. The previous mathematical
equivalences and domain statements consequently apply to the explicit
realization without changing the periodic NSE equation or datum class.

This mathematical covariance does not by itself produce a computable
name for O_N. If enclosure of the old arbitrary-basis coefficient vector
is requested, certified effective access to O_N is an additional input
unless it has been explicitly constructed. Given such names, all
coefficient transports are finite arithmetic and CP60 supplies the
old-coordinate names. Without them, R24.12/R24.15 assert effective
access only in the specified explicit realization. No arbitrary-basis
computability claim is hidden in CP14.


14.Q.9 REGULARITY AND EFFECTIVITY BOUNDARIES

The construction derives finite data access, actual finite coefficient
circuits and terminating finite-accuracy search on the stated effective
input class. It supplies no bound uniform in N for the exact or decoded
fluid observables. No G3, FB or continuum solution is an input, and no
universal regularity conclusion is inferred.

In particular, density of rational trigonometric fields does not extend
the effective-input theorem to all smooth data and does not supply a

Its arbitrary-mean and all-finite-horizon quantifiers are unchanged.

For more general data, the exact access premise is the certified total

For the explicit finite rational-trigonometric class, these names are

14.R.0 FROZEN ACTUAL DATA AND THE ALGORITHM'S INPUT CONTRACT

Fix N>=1, nu>0, hbar>0, T>0 and the same real canonical Gaussian psi
used by CP55--CP59. Write z=q-a, tau=sigma_N^2>0. The finite actual data
are the established vector theta=(a,tau,b coefficients,V coefficients,
T,E,g), where E=w_N^2 and g=g_N. The operator remains the actual
  G=-(i/hbar)H_N,
  L_h=Id-hG/2, h>0.
For a polynomial P,
  L_h(Ppsi)=[P+(h/2)(DP+VP)]psi,
with the plus sign, the actual quadratic V, and all actual domains.

A fixed coarse rational box Box0 contains theta and has strictly positive
lower endpoints for tau and T. Fix a positive natural n and a positive
rational epsilon. They remain unchanged during all fine-box refinement
for this run. The actual step is h=T/n. They may be the original
CP58 accuracy schedule, or the later refined-horizon schedule; the
algorithm below only needs their stated positivity and frozen values.

The effective input premise is a TOTAL certified box-producing procedure:
for every requested integer p, that request terminates and returns a finite
rational box B_p containing the same theta, contained in Box0, with
maximum component width tending to zero. A merely given mathematical
shrinking sequence is insufficient for effective termination. Nested boxes can always be
constructed by finite intersections with all preceding boxes and Box0:
  B_p=Box0 intersect Braw_0 intersect ... intersect Braw_p.
Componentwise this is rational maximum of lower endpoints and minimum
of upper endpoints. Actual containment proves every intersection nonempty.
The intersections remain shrinking because B_p is contained in Braw_p.
No computability of arbitrary smooth data is inferred from this premise.

At a single step the current target is x=X(z)psi, where X is a fixed
rational polynomial. Let L>=0 be a known degree bound for X, using L=0
for the zero polynomial. During this single-step solve, X, n, epsilon,
the Gaussian center/scale, and the coarse box are fixed. Once a candidate
is accepted, the next target is X_new=2P-X, again a rational polynomial.

For every K>=L let I_K be the finite set of multiindices of total degree
at most K, with a fixed order, and r=card(I_K)>=1. Use the monomial basis
  f_alpha=z^alpha psi, alpha in I_K.
CP55 proves that the actual matrix and vector
  Q_(alpha,beta)=<L_h f_alpha,L_h f_beta>_[1],
  v_alpha=<L_h f_alpha,x>_[1],
  B_x=||x||_[1]^2                                       (R25.1)
are finite exact Gaussian moment expressions in theta, and Q is a REAL
symmetric positive-definite matrix. Its monomial-coordinate lower bound
is Q>=B0>0, not Q>=Id. Its unique least-residual coefficient vector is
c_star=Q^(-1)v. For this fixed target,
  d_K^2=min_c ||L_h(sum_alpha c_alpha f_alpha)-x||_[1]^2,
  d_K ->0 as K->infinity.                              (R25.2)
These are already proved analytic facts, not numerical inverse oracles.

14.R.1 EXACT RATIONAL ROW-SUM NORMS

For a real or rational finite vector u and finite matrix A define
  |u|_infty=max_i |u_i|,
  kappa(A)=max_i sum_j |A_ij|.                         (R25.3)
The index sets are nonempty. For rational data these are exact rational
numbers, obtained using finitely many absolute values, additions and
comparisons. Rational-to-real interpretation preserves their values.

Finite triangle inequalities prove
  |Au|_infty<=kappa(A)|u|_infty,
  kappa(A+B)<=kappa(A)+kappa(B),
  kappa(AB)<=kappa(A)kappa(B).                          (R25.4)
For the product inequality, for each row i,
  sum_j |sum_k A_ik B_kj|
    <=sum_k |A_ik| sum_j|B_kj|
    <=kappa(B)sum_k|A_ik|
    <=kappa(B)kappa(A).
Thus no implicit choice of a default matrix norm is needed. The selected
Mathlib sources ML79--ML81 package exactly this row-sup/L1 norm through
their explicit local matrix norm instance; the entrywise Pi sup norm
would not satisfy the same formulas without dimension factors.

14.R.2 A GENERAL INVERSE-DEFECT CERTIFICATE

Let Q be the actual positive-definite Gram matrix, R any real matrix,
and q_def a real number satisfying
  0<=q_def<1,
  kappa(Id-RQ)<=q_def.
Set Edef=Id-RQ. Actual invertibility of Q is supplied by CP55. The
identity
  Q^(-1)=R+Edef Q^(-1)
and R25.4 give
  kappa(Q^(-1))<=kappa(R)/(1-q_def),
  kappa(Q^(-1)-R)<=q_def*kappa(R)/(1-q_def).            (R25.5)
All quantities are finite; the rearrangement divides only by the proved
positive number 1-q_def. The argument does not use a Neumann-series
assumption or an unverified inverse supplied by a numerical routine.

For any coefficient vector c, put zeta=v-Qc and d=c_star-c. Then
  Qd=zeta,
  d=Edef d+R zeta.
Consequently
  |c-c_star|_infty<=|R zeta|_infty/(1-q_def).           (R25.6)
This is a posteriori coefficient control in MONOMIAL coordinates. It
replaces the Hermite-coordinate unit inverse bound, which is not valid
in an arbitrary monomial basis.

14.R.3 TOTAL EXACT RATIONAL MATRIX INVERSION

Define RationalInverse(M) for an r-by-r rational matrix M by the following
finite Gauss--Jordan routine. Its result is either FAIL or a rational R.

  A:=M; B:=Id.
  For k=0,...,r-1:
    Search the finite rows i=k,...,r-1 for A_ik!=0.
    If no such row exists, return FAIL.
    Swap rows i and k in A and B.
    Store pivot:=A_kk, which is a checked nonzero rational.
    Divide row k of both A and B by the stored pivot.
    For every row l!=k:
      Store factor:=A_lk before changing that row.
      Subtract factor times row k from row l in both A and B.
  Return B, after the exact rational checks BM=Id and MB=Id.
                                                               (R25.7)
A failed final identity test also returns FAIL. Every comparison is an
exact rational equality/inequality, and every division occurs after a
nonzero-pivot check. There are r pivot rounds and finite row/column loops.
Hence this is a total finite rational algorithm, including singular input.

Correctness follows from the invariant A=B M and invertibility of every
performed elementary row operation. After k successful rounds the first
k columns of A are the corresponding identity columns. At successful
completion, A=Id and BM=Id. Because the matrices are square over a field,
this also gives MB=Id, so both final tests pass.

If M is nonsingular, a missing pivot is impossible. At such a failure,
column k has zero entries in rows k,...,r-1; its remaining entries make
it a linear combination of the previous k identity columns. That would
make A singular, contradicting its invertible row-equivalence with M.
Therefore RationalInverse succeeds on every nonsingular rational M and
returns its actual rational inverse. No real-valued comparison is used.

An implementation may provide R by any other finite rational method, but
the two exact product checks in R25.7 remain a sufficient output contract.
The existence/termination proof here specifically supplies the complete
Gauss--Jordan method rather than assuming an inverse subroutine.

14.R.4 RATIONAL MIDPOINTS AND AN EXPLICIT DEFECT BOUND

For a fixed degree K and one actual-input box B, use CP57/CP60 finite
interval arithmetic to enclose every entry of Q and v. Compute the upper
triangular Gram entries once and mirror their intervals across the
diagonal. Since the actual Q is symmetric, this preserves containment.
Let
  Q_ij in [l_ij,u_ij],
  v_i in [s_i,t_i],
  M_ij=(l_ij+u_ij)/2,
  rho_ij=(u_ij-l_ij)/2>=0,
  vhat_i=(s_i+t_i)/2,
  eta_i=(t_i-s_i)/2>=0.                                (R25.8)
M and rho are symmetric rational matrices. The actual inequalities are
  |Q_ij-M_ij|<=rho_ij,  |v_i-vhat_i|<=eta_i.

Run RationalInverse(M). On FAIL the current degree/precision pair is
rejected, and the finite stage continues. On success let R be the exact
rational inverse. Define the rational number
  q_def=max_i sum_j sum_k |R_ik|rho_kj.                 (R25.9)
Because RM=Id,
  Id-RQ=R(M-Q),
  kappa(Id-RQ)<=q_def.
This bound uses actual entry radii and the exact rational inverse. It is
not obtained by applying a fixed-polynomial convergence theorem to an
unbounded or otherwise uncontrolled varying inverse.

Require q_def<1/2 for this degree/precision pair. The stronger threshold
is a convenient rational stopping rule; R25.5--R25.6 only require q_def<1.
If the threshold fails, reject this pair and continue to the next degree
or the next finite precision stage. There is no unbounded local loop.

Set the rational candidate coefficient vector and polynomial
  c=R vhat,
  P_c(z)=sum_(alpha in I_K)c_alpha z^alpha.             (R25.10)
Because MR=Id, Mc=vhat. The exact normal residual obeys
  zeta=v-Qc=(v-vhat)+(M-Q)c.
Therefore, with rational bounds
  a_i=eta_i+sum_j rho_ij |c_j|,
  beta=max_i sum_k |R_ik|a_k,
  b_coef=beta/(1-q_def),                               (R25.11)
one has |zeta_i|<=a_i, |R zeta|_infty<=beta and
  |c-c_star|_infty<=b_coef.
All denominators have already been certified positive.

14.R.5 INVERSE-FREE RESIDUAL ACCEPTANCE AND OPTIONAL DEGREE EXCLUSION

Use the actual polynomial residual, not merely the normal-equation
residual, for acceptance:
  F_c(z)=P_c+(T/(2n))(D P_c+V P_c)-X.
Its exact squared weighted norm is the established finite moment sum
  J(c)=||F_c psi||_[1]^2
      =sum_(alpha,beta)(F_c)_alpha(F_c)_beta M_(alpha+beta)(a,tau).
                                                               (R25.12)
Evaluate this entire expression by the IDENTICAL canonical coefficient/
moment interval evaluator used inside ResidualCheck, at B and with the
computed c treated as exact rational constants. Retain that evaluator's
coefficient normalization, finite support, and summation/product order
conventions. Let [L_J,U_J] be its output. An algebraically equal real
expression evaluated by different interval syntax is not substituted.
Accept this candidate only if
  U_J<epsilon^2/4.                                     (R25.13)
The strict rational comparison proves the actual residual norm is less
than epsilon/2. In particular it satisfies the earlier residual checker
with tolerance epsilon. The acceptance inequality uses no exact Q inverse,
unknown least-residual value, or real comparison oracle.

The coefficient certificate also supplies an OPTIONAL lower bound on the
best achievable residual at this degree. Compute
  S_Q=sum_(i,j)max(|l_ij|,|u_ij|),
  L_min=max(0,L_J-S_Q*b_coef^2).
The least-squares square completion gives
  0<=J(c)-d_K^2=(c-c_star)^T Q(c-c_star)
      <=S_Q*b_coef^2,
so
  L_min<=d_K^2<=U_J.                                   (R25.14)
If L_min>=epsilon^2/4, no polynomial in V_K can pass R25.13 in actual
residual norm. For the SAME target, nestedness makes this an exclusion
certificate for every degree <=K. Exclusions are cleared when the target
changes at the next physical step. Boundary cases need not be decided:
the degree/precision dovetail below terminates without this pruning rule.

The physical state residual and the finite normal-equation residual are
different quantities. A small normal residual alone certifies proximity
to the finite-degree least-squares vector, not that this degree resolves
the actual inverse to the required tolerance. R25.13 is always retained.

14.R.6 FIXED-DEGREE CONSISTENCY UNDER REFINING INPUT BOXES

Fix K and the current target X once. Along shrinking certified B_p,
CP57/CP60 polynomial interval convergence gives entrywise
  l_ij,p,u_ij,p -> Q_ij,
  s_i,p,t_i,p -> v_i,
  M_p->Q, rho_p->0, vhat_p->v, eta_p->0.
                                                               (R25.15)
All matrices have the same finite dimension in this assertion.

Use the already proved actual Q^(-1) only as an analytic constant. Define
  Fproof_p=Id-Q^(-1)M_p=Q^(-1)(Q-M_p),
  omega_p=kappa(Fproof_p).
The finite row-sum product bound and M_p->Q give omega_p->0. Once
omega_p<1, a vector satisfying M_p z=0 satisfies z=Fproof_p z, whence
  |z|_infty<=omega_p|z|_infty
forces z=0. The square matrix M_p is therefore nonsingular; the exact
rational RationalInverse routine succeeds and returns R_p=M_p^(-1).
Its inverse identity gives
  R_p-Q^(-1)=Fproof_p R_p.
Rearranging the finite row-sum inequalities yields
  kappa(R_p)<=kappa(Q^(-1))/(1-omega_p),
  kappa(R_p-Q^(-1))
    <=omega_p*kappa(Q^(-1))/(1-omega_p) ->0.
This proves R_p->Q^(-1) directly, using only the selected finite matrix
norm identities. The algorithm never queries Q^(-1), omega_p, a real
determinant, or a modulus of this neighborhood.

The R_p are consequently bounded in every finite entry/row-sum norm.
Equation R25.9 and rho_p->0 imply
  q_def,p->0.
The inverse-defect threshold q_def,p<1/2 therefore eventually passes.
Moreover,
  c_p=R_p vhat_p->c_star,
  a_p->0, beta_p->0, b_coef,p->0.                      (R25.16)

It remains essential to justify residual interval convergence although
c_p changes with p. It is NOT an instance of a fixed-candidate hypothesis
without further proof. Expand R25.12 as a finite polynomial expression
jointly in the model parameters theta and the coefficient vector c.
The endpoints for theta tend to its actual components, while the exact
degenerate coefficient intervals [c_p,c_p] have both endpoints tending
to c_star. Addition, multiplication, negation and finite min/max of corner
products are continuous in their endpoints. Structural induction on this
joint finite expression yields
  L_J,p,U_J,p -> J(c_star)=d_K^2.                       (R25.17)
Containment of c_star in each [c_p,c_p] is not required for this endpoint-
limit statement; each interval still soundly encloses J(c_p) at that stage.
Equivalently, the same conclusion follows by the finite Q/v/B_x quadratic
formula and c_p->c_star. No unbounded-degree or unbounded-coefficient limit
is passed through a fixed-degree convergence theorem.

14.R.7 A DEGREE/PRECISION DOVETAIL THAT CANNOT STALL AT ONE DEGREE

Define ValidatedTrial(X,n,epsilon,p_start) as follows. The actual Gaussian,
coarse box and certified nested enclosure procedure are fixed inputs.
Let L be the stated nonnegative degree bound for X.

  For stage s=0,1,2,...:
    Obtain the certified nested box B_(p_start+s).
    For K=L,L+1,...,L+s, in that fixed order:
      Form the finite Q/v interval tables at this degree and box.
      Perform the single finite RationalInverse call R25.7.
      On FAIL, continue to the next K.
      Compute q_def; if q_def>=1/2, continue to the next K.
      Form c=R vhat and its finite polynomial P_c.
      Compute the actual-residual moment interval [L_J,U_J].
      If U_J<epsilon^2/4, return (P_c,p_start+s).
    Continue to the next stage.
                                                               (R25.18)
The optional valid degree exclusions R25.14 may be used, but are not
needed. Each stage has finitely many degrees, finitely many matrix
entries, one finite rational solve per degree, and finitely many moment
operations. A singular midpoint or an insufficient degree consumes only
that finite attempt. No branch waits forever for a fixed K to improve.
The algorithm enumerates degree/precision pairs; it does not enumerate
rational coefficient tuples. Each trial vector is derived by one finite
matrix solve.

TERMINATION THEOREM FOR ONE TARGET.
By R25.2 choose a fixed finite K_star>=L with
  d_(K_star)<epsilon/4.
For this SAME degree and target, R25.15--R25.17 imply that at all
sufficiently large precision indices the rational inverse exists,
q_def<1/2, and
  U_J<epsilon^2/4,
since its limit is d_(K_star)^2<epsilon^2/16. The degree K_star is
included at every stage s>=K_star-L. A stage meeting both finite lower
bounds therefore exists. The inner finite loop reaches an accepted
candidate no later than that stage. Thus ValidatedTrial terminates
under the explicit certified enclosure-access contract.

A diagonal-only policy K=p is not used: growing matrix dimension could
outrun the available enclosure precision. Repeated access to each fixed
finite degree is the mechanism used in the termination proof.

14.R.8 FINITE TUPLES, ONE FINAL FINE BOX, AND THE EXISTING CHECKER

Start with X_0=1. For j=1,...,n, apply ValidatedTrial to the fixed current
X_(j-1), with the same n, epsilon and coarse box. Begin the next call at
at least the preceding successful precision index, so all accepted boxes
lie in the same nested sequence. For the returned rational polynomial
P_j set
  X_j=2P_j-X_(j-1),
  y_j=P_j psi,
  x_j=X_j psi.
Every call terminates by R25.18 and every step is an actual polynomial-
Gaussian residual equation with residual norm<epsilon/2. Finite induction
proves termination of the entire n-step procedure and Schwartz membership
of every node. Weighted2 and actual H/E3/L domain requirements therefore
hold, even though only weighted1 residual errors were budgeted.

Let B_final be the last successful box. For each earlier accepted P_j
and its fixed prior target X_(j-1), the physical residual expression is
now fixed. Rational interval operations are inclusion-monotone:
if every component interval is narrowed, its output interval is contained
in the former output interval. This follows directly for addition and
negation; for multiplication, the smaller rectangle's product range is
contained in the larger rectangle's product range; finite syntax induction
handles all sums and powers. Thus the upper residual bound cannot increase
when reevaluated on B_final. It remains strictly below epsilon^2/4.
Consequently
  ResidualCheck(B_final,epsilon,n,(P_1,...,P_n))=true.   (R25.19)

If n and epsilon were frozen from the original coarse accuracy contract,
then W=(Box0,B_final,(P_1,...,P_n)) satisfies
  AccuracyCheck_N(W)=true,
  EnclosesActualData(theta,W),
with exactly the existing checker and its original semantic input premise.
For a refined accuracy contract with the same residual interface, the
same conclusion holds for that distinct checker after its own n and
epsilon have been frozen. The algorithm does not substitute the original
checker for the refined checker or change the required accuracy target.

Its normalized continuous path is the established interpolation of the
finite rational polynomial nodes. With B the actual graph coefficient,
  sup_t||v(t)-U(t)psi||_[1]
    <=B/n^2+2 sum_j||r_j||_[1]
    <B/n^2+n*epsilon.                                  (R25.20)
This is stronger than the earlier sufficient residual budget
B/n^2+2n*epsilon. The same positive normalization denominator and actual
unbounded-observable error theorem therefore apply to the caller's
specified accuracy contract. No compact support is asserted: these are
POLY witnesses, and the earlier CORE predicate is unchanged.

The output may retain the finite per-step inverse/defect records as audit
data, but the existing residual accuracy checker already accepts the
returned coefficient tuple and final box. Inverse certificates do not
replace or weaken its actual residual comparisons.

14.R.9 EXISTENCE, EFFECTIVE TERMINATION, AND THE EXACT BOUNDARY

Even without an effective enclosure procedure, every actual finite theta
admits a successful finite midpoint-matrix certificate at each step.
Choose an actual K_star using d_K->0, then a sufficiently small rational
box containing theta inside the fixed coarse box. The fixed-degree
convergence proof gives a nonsingular rational midpoint, q_def<1/2, and
R25.13. The output polynomial coefficients are rational. Finite induction
constructs a complete tuple. This proves mathematical nonemptiness of the
more structured matrix-generated witness class; it does not provide a
uniform effective procedure for arbitrary exact real inputs.

Under the certified shrinking-input contract, the explicit procedure
R25.18 and the finite recurrence do terminate. No exact-real inverse,
exact-real eigenvalue comparison, fixed-degree success oracle, or uniform
condition-number estimate is used. The analytic limit proofs use only
actual SPD, derived d_K->0, finite row-sum estimates, and continuity of
the finite arithmetic interval expressions.
No rate for the required degree, precision, runtime or storage is claimed.

The theorem is independent of G3. It supplies finite approximate quantum
state paths at every fixed cutoff and horizon under the stated access
contract; the universal cutoff-regularity bound remains a separate
criterion. All prior actual-domain and family-quantifier distinctions
are preserved.

14.S ROUND 26: REFINED ACCURACY, EFFECTIVE STATE ACCESS AND EXACT ENERGY NAMES

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI53]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP65, CP66; exact contracts in Section21.

  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD17, AD20--AD29.

               Continuous hat reconstruction gives a finite Gaussian energy quotient; certified
               arithmetic and the error envelope yield a rational name of the actual finite quantum
               energy. All-data regularity criteria retain their original quantifier order.
  DETAILS: Section18; exact source hypotheses and adapter boundaries retained.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge formal bodies and external evidence pending.

14.S.1. A distinct precision-indexed checker.

Fix the same actual real canonical Gaussian input theta, N>=1 and T>0.
For r in N define the positive rational accuracy target
  delta_(N,r)=(N+1)^(-2)*4^(-r).                         (R26.1)
Let Box0 be a fixed ordered rational coarse box containing theta, with
positive lower endpoints for tau,T. Compute Xbar,A2,A3,Tbar,Ebar,gbar,
Cbar,Bbar exactly as in R22.1. The same coarse box and these same
majorants can be retained for every r. Define
  e_r=delta_(N,r)/[4*Cbar*(1+Xbar)^2],
  n_r=1+ceil_Q_to_N(2*Bbar/e_r),
  epsilon_r=e_r/(4*n_r).                                (R26.2)
All these are finite rational or integer calculations and
  0<e_r<=1/64,   n_r>=1.
For a fixed r, n_r and epsilon_r remain fixed while its fine box and
trial coefficients are refined.

Define RefinedAccuracyCheck_(N,r)(W) by R22.4 with precisely these
replacement budgets. It retains the finite shape/order/positivity,
fine-box subset, and residual upper-bound tests. The semantic premise
is still actual theta in the fine box.

This is a distinct precision-indexed Boolean function. Its r=0 member
is exactly AccuracyCheck_N; for r>0, the changed prescribed tuple
length need not satisfy the old checker's length test. No such
identification is used. Every RefinedAccuracyCheck_(N,r) is total
on finite rational inputs for the same finite-control-flow reasons.

14.S.2. Soundness, existence and effective finite construction.

The proof R22.2--R22.6 applies with delta_(N,r), giving
  RefinedAccuracyCheck_(N,r)(W)=true /\ theta in FineBox(W)
    => sup_t ||v_r(t)-U_N(t)psi||_[1]<=e_r,
       ||v_r(t)||_[0]>=1-e_r>0.                         (R26.3)
Thus psi_hat_r(t)=v_r(t)/||v_r(t)||_[0] is defined, normalized,
continuous and in the actual observable domains. Put
  Zbar=delta_(N,0)/[2*Cbar*(1+Xbar)]<=1/16.
The normalization estimate yields the explicit bound
  sup_(0<=t<=T)||psi_hat_r(t)-U_N(t)psi||_[1]
    <=2*e_r*(1+Xbar)=Zbar*4^(-r).                       (R26.4)
Both actual observable errors obey
  sup_(0<=t<=T)|Q_r^E(t)-Q_U^E(t)|<=delta_(N,r),
  |integral_0^T Q_r^L(t)dt-integral_0^T Q_U^L(t)dt|
      <=delta_(N,r).                                    (R26.5)
The same actual-domain and time-integrability arguments are retained.

For every actual finite input and r, a certificate satisfying both
premises in R26.3 exists. Indeed choose a rational coarse box with
actual theta in its interior and positive tau,T lower endpoints;
freeze the new positive n_r,epsilon_r. CP56 gives a finite rational
trial tuple with strict residuals below epsilon_r/2. Keeping this
tuple and budget fixed, CP57 shrinking interval convergence gives a
fine box in which every residual-square upper bound is below
epsilon_r^2. This proves
  forall actual theta, forall r,
    exists finite W:
      RefinedAccuracyCheck_(N,r)(W)=true
        /\ theta in FineBox(W).                         (R26.6)
No effective input-access or G3 premise is required for this
mathematical existence statement.

If a total certified name for actual theta is available, CP64 supplies
the adaptive finite least-residual tuple procedure at these same
fixed budgets. It uses nested input boxes and freezes each accepted
rational polynomial. After the finite n_r steps the final fine box
is contained in every earlier accepted box. Inclusion-monotonicity
of the finite interval residual arithmetic preserves those strict
tests, so the resulting certificate passes RefinedAccuracyCheck.
CP64 proves that each of the finitely many searches terminates.
Therefore
  EffectiveEnclosure(theta)
    => TotalRefinedCertificateAlgorithm(theta,N,r).     (R26.7)
The output consists of finite rational boxes and polynomial tables.
It does not require an exact-real solve or an unproved residual oracle.

14.S.3. Uniform state and observable Cauchy bounds.

Choose certificates for all r with one coarse box, either by R26.6
or by R26.7. For r,s>=p, the triangle inequality and R26.4 give
  sup_t ||psi_hat_r(t)-psi_hat_s(t)||_[1]
    <=Zbar*(4^(-r)+4^(-s))
    <=2*Zbar*4^(-p)<=2^(-p).                            (R26.8)
Likewise,
  sup_t |Q_r^E(t)-Q_s^E(t)|
    <=2*delta_(N,0)*4^(-p)<=2^(-p),
  |integral_0^T Q_r^L-integral_0^T Q_s^L|
    <=2*delta_(N,0)*4^(-p)<=2^(-p).                     (R26.9)
Here 2*Zbar<=1/8, 2*delta_(N,0)<=1/2, and 4^(-p)<=2^(-p).
The error bounds also identify the limits directly as the already
constructed actual U_N orbit and its actual observables. No unknown
continuum solution or G3 premise identifies these finite-cutoff limits.
Only the state and energy-expectation limits above are uniform in time;
the gradient assertion concerns its integrated scalar expectation.

14.S.4. Branch-free finite reconstruction and an explicit path modulus.

Use normalized time s=t/T in [0,1] and n=n_r. For j=0,...,n put
  lambda_j(s)=max(0,1-|n*s-j|).                         (R26.10)
For every s in [0,1], these weights are nonnegative, sum to one and
at most two adjacent weights are nonzero. For a proof, locate n*s
between two adjacent integers j,j+1: the two values are
j+1-n*s and n*s-j; at s=1 the sole value is lambda_n=1.
This case distinction proves the identity; evaluating R26.10 itself
uses only abs,max and finite arithmetic, without comparing an exact
real time with grid boundaries.

If x_j=X_j(z)psi are the polynomial nodes, the affine interpolant is
exactly
  v_r(T*s)=sum_(j=0)^n lambda_j(s)*x_j
          =P_s(z)psi,
  P_s=sum_(j=0)^n lambda_j(s)*X_j.                      (R26.11)
The normalized state uses the same positive denominator as R26.3.

For each node, its weighted norm square is a finite Gaussian moment
expression. Evaluate it over the certified final box and let U_j
be its rational upper endpoint. Define
  B_j=max(1,U_j),   Mbar=sum_(j=0)^n B_j,
  rho=1-e_r>0.
Since U_j>=||x_j||_[1]^2>=0, sqrt(s)<=max(1,s) for s>=0 gives
  ||x_j||_[1]<=B_j.
Each lambda_j is n-Lipschitz, and their sum is one. Hence
  ||v_r(T*s)-v_r(T*s')||_[1]
    <=n*Mbar*|s-s'|,
  ||v_r(T*s)||_[1]<=Mbar.
The ordinary norm is rho-separated from zero. The reverse triangle
inequality for that norm and direct subtraction of the two quotients
therefore give
  ||psi_hat_r(T*s)-psi_hat_r(T*s')||_[1]
    <=Lbar_r*|s-s'|,
  Lbar_r=n*Mbar*(1/rho+Mbar/rho^2).                    (R26.12)
This is a finite rational Lipschitz majorant in normalized time.
For physical time, a certified positive lower bound T_lower from the
coarse box gives the rational majorant Lbar_r/T_lower.

14.S.5. Exact finite-moment energy evaluation and actual energy names.

In the explicit Fourier eigenbasis of CP61, define
  W3_N=(Id+A_N)^3,
  e3_N(q)=q^T W3_N q.
Its diagonal entries are one on the constant modes and
(1+4*pi^2*|k|^2)^3 on each corresponding oscillatory coordinate.
They are finite actual arithmetic circuits from N and pi.

Let P_s=sum_alpha p_alpha(s)z^alpha be R26.11. With the actual centered
Gaussian moment table m_gamma(tau), define the finite quantities
  D_r(s)=sum_(alpha,beta) p_alpha(s)*p_beta(s)
                              *m_(alpha+beta)(tau),
  F_r(s)=integral e3_N(a+z)*P_s(z)^2*|psi(a+z)|^2 dz.   (R26.13)
The second expression is evaluated by expanding its finite polynomial:
if e3_N(a+z)*P_s(z)^2=sum_gamma f_gamma(s)z^gamma, then
  F_r(s)=sum_gamma f_gamma(s)*m_gamma(tau).
All integrals are justified by the polynomial-Gaussian bounds.
These are actual finite moment equalities, and
  D_r(s)=||v_r(T*s)||_[0]^2>=rho^2>0,
  Q_r^E(T*s)=F_r(s)/D_r(s).                            (R26.14)
If P_s has degree at most K, moments through degree 2*K+2 suffice.

For named actual input parameters and a named s in [0,1], CP60 applies
to the finite coefficient circuits, abs/max hat weights, Gaussian
moments and the positive reciprocal in R26.14. It therefore produces
a total rational name for the actual approximate energy Q_r^E(T*s).
No evaluation of the Gaussian exponential or infinite quadrature is
needed for this scalar: normalization and polynomial moments give the
displayed finite quotient.

THEOREM [EXACT_FINITE_QUANTUM_ENERGY_NAME].
For the actual named finite data and named s in [0,1], the exact scalar
  Q_U^E(T*s)=<U_N(T*s)psi,E3_N U_N(T*s)psi>
has a total certified rational name.                   (R26.15)

Proof.
For requested p>=0 choose r=p, construct the finite certificate by
R26.7, and evaluate R26.14 to a rational interval J_p of width at most
2^(-p-2). Enlarge it on both sides by the rational delta_(N,p).
R26.5 proves containment of the actual exact-orbit energy.
The final interval width is at most
  2^(-p-2)+2*delta_(N,0)*4^(-p)
    <=(1/4+1/2)*2^(-p)<2^(-p).
All constituent procedures terminate. Intersect finitely many previous
outputs if a nested name is required. For named physical t with
0<=t<=T, first form the named s=t/T using the positive T premise.
This proves R26.15 from the derived finite algorithms.

The L_N gradient-supremum multiplier is not generally polynomial.
R26.5/R26.9 retain its actual semantic error and integrated convergence
statements. The polynomial quotient R26.14 is asserted only for E3_N.

14.S.6. Derived input classes and retained all-data regularity equivalence.

For the effective construction, instantiate the preceding canonical
Gaussian model and all residual/checker predicates in the explicit
CP61 frame. Write theta^eff for its actual R21.1 parameter vector.
The previous theorems apply to this valid realization with their same
formulas and hypotheses. CP14 supplies mathematical covariance to
another orthonormal frame; effective access in that other frame also
requires certified names for its transition matrix. No rational trial
table is transported as rational data through an arbitrary real matrix.

CP62 proves the exact actual theta enclosure contract from:
  finite N, positive nu and T with certified rational names;
  the finitely many actual Fourier coefficients required for P_N a,
    with certified names in the explicit CP61 Fourier frame.
All program-domain premises are derived there. The actual hbar>0 is
arbitrary; it is absent from theta and all these procedures because
G=-(i/hbar)H_N and the relevant graph-norm ratios cancel hbar.
Combining CP62, CP64 and R26.7 gives a total finite certificate algorithm
for every such represented input. Combining it with R26.15 gives
actual exact-energy access at every represented admissible time.

In particular, if nu,T are positive rationals and
  a(x)=m+sum_(k in a finite K+)
       [A_k*cos(2*pi*k.x)+B_k*sin(2*pi*k.x)],
  m,A_k,B_k in Q^3,
  k.A_k=k.B_k=0,
then every required actual Fourier coefficient has the CP62 finite
arithmetic name. This class consists of smooth arbitrary-mean
divergence-free periodic fields. Its finite rational code, N,r and
the specified algorithms suffice:
  finite rational-trigonometric input
    => total accepted finite accuracy certificate,
  additionally a rational or certified named admissible time
    => total actual finite-cutoff energy name.          (R26.16)
The first implication has no supplied EffectiveEnclosure premise:
that access contract has been constructed from this exact input class.
No effective representation is inferred for an arbitrary smooth field.

For the all-data theorem, define an admitted refinement family W by
  forall N>=1, forall smooth divergence-free arbitrary-mean a,
  forall finite T>0, forall r>=0:
    RefinedAccuracyCheck_(N,r)(W_(N,a,T,r))=true,
    theta_(N,a,T) in FineBox(W_(N,a,T,r)).              (R26.17)
R26.6 and ordinary choice prove such families exist. Effective
procedures on represented inputs are compatible with this existence;
an all-data family need not have a finite program.

Fix any such family and any prescribed selector
  kappa:(N,a,T)->N,
before a common regularity bound is asserted. Decode its selected
paths and define
  QREG_ref^(W,kappa)(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall a in C^infinity_sigma(T^3;R^3), forall finite T>0,
      exists finite K>=0,
        forall N>=1, forall t in [0,T],
          Q_(kappa(N,a,T))^E(N,a,T,t)<=K;
  QLIP_ref^(W,kappa)(nu,hbar) :<=>
    forall a in C^infinity_sigma(T^3;R^3), forall finite T>0,
      exists finite L>=0,
        forall N>=1,
          integral_0^T Q_(kappa(N,a,T))^L(N,a,T,t)dt<=L.
The bounds may depend on nu,hbar,W,kappa,a,T, but not on N.
Since delta_(N,kappa)<=delta_(N,0)<=1/4, R26.5 gives both directions
by adding at most 1/4 to the corresponding exact-Gaussian bound:
  G3<=>QREG_ref^(W,kappa)<=>QLIP_ref^(W,kappa).           (R26.18)
This uses all smooth data in the predicates. Density of the rational
trigonometric subclass is not used to infer a missing universal bound.

For each fixed r, sum_(N>=1) delta_(N,r)<=4^(-r).
For each fixed N, sum_(r>=0) delta_(N,r)=(4/3)delta_(N,0).
Finite partial sums and nonnegativity therefore give
  sum_(N>=1,r>=0) delta_(N,r)<=4/3.                     (R26.19)
The geometric factor follows from the already indexed ML66; the cutoff
bound is the earlier telescoping estimate R18.18.
Under G3, continuum-observable errors are the prior conditional
exact-Gaussian errors plus delta_(N,r). Only this added approximation
envelope is asserted doubly summable.


14.T ROUND 27: EFFECTIVE SPATIAL GRADIENT SUPREMA

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI54]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP67, CP68; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML59, ML60, ML65, ML66, ML76, ML82, ML83, ML88--ML92;
              MT22, MT23.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD30.
  APPLICATION: Actual Hessian traces and finite torus grids; total elementary
               names and the actual nonpolynomial gradient-supremum name.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new formal bridge bodies pending.

Scope.
  N>=1; d=d_N; explicit real Fourier eigenbasis (R24.3);
  A=A_N; I=I_N; q in R^d; all constants and mean coordinates retained.
  |nabla I(q)(x)| means the Frobenius matrix norm fixed in Section1.
  |nabla^2 I(q)(x)| means the full ordered-index Frobenius tensor norm.
  g_N=sqrt(Tr(A_N)); k_N=sqrt(Tr(A_N^2)).
  The parameter k_N is independent of the quantum parameter hbar.

14.T.1. The exact second-derivative kernel trace.

For every x in T^3,
  sum_j |nabla^2 e_j(x)|_F^2=Tr(A_N^2).                 (R27.1)

Derivation.
For a nonzero representative k and one unit transverse polarization p,
  e_c=sqrt(2)*p*cos(2*pi*k.x),
  e_s=sqrt(2)*p*sin(2*pi*k.x),
  lambda_k=4*pi^2*|k|^2.
Differentiating in the two ordered spatial indices alpha,beta gives
  |nabla^2 e_c(x)|_F^2+|nabla^2 e_s(x)|_F^2
    =2*(2*pi)^4*sum_(alpha,beta) k_alpha^2*k_beta^2
    =2*lambda_k^2.
The two basis vectors contribute precisely 2*lambda_k^2 to Tr(A_N^2).
Sum over the two transverse polarizations and the frequency pairs.
The constant modes contribute zero. This proves (R27.1) in the explicit
basis; orthogonal coordinate covariance also preserves both sides.

Cauchy--Schwarz in the finite coordinate index then gives
  |nabla^2 I(q)(x)|_F<=k_N*|q|.                        (R27.2)
For x,y represented by a shortest periodic segment,
  |nabla I(q)(x)-nabla I(q)(y)|_F
      <=k_N*|q|*dist_T3(x,y).
Consequently f_q(x)=|nabla I(q)(x)|_F is continuous and
k_N*|q|-Lipschitz on the unit flat torus. The continuous maximum equals
its essential supremum: every strict submaximum level has a nonempty
open superlevel set of positive Haar measure. Thus the actual multiplier
ell_N(q) has the pointwise maximum representation used below.

14.T.2. A finite spatial maximum with a certified error.

For m>=1 an integer, define the exact periodic grid
  G_m={ (j_1/m,j_2/m,j_3/m) mod Z^3 : 0<=j_i<m },
  ell_(N,m)(q)=max_(x in G_m)|nabla I_N(q)(x)|_F.        (R27.3)
The grid is finite and nonempty. Each x in T^3 has a grid point at
periodic distance at most sqrt(3)/(2*m). Hence
  0<=ell_N(q)-ell_(N,m)(q)
      <=sqrt(3)*k_N*|q|/(2*m)<=k_N*|q|/m.             (R27.4)
This follows by applying (R27.2) to a maximum point and its nearest
grid point; the opposite inequality follows because G_m is a subset.

The pointwise first-derivative trace (R12T.3) gives, uniformly in m,
  0<=ell_(N,m)(q)<=g_N*|q|,
  |ell_(N,m)(q)-ell_(N,m)(q')|<=g_N*|q-q'|.           (R27.5)
Indeed each grid norm is g_N-Lipschitz in q; taking a finite maximum
preserves the same Lipschitz constant. No differentiability of ell_N
or ell_(N,m) is asserted or needed.

14.T.3. Elementary certified function access.

Extend the certified rational-name operations of CP60 by the following
three total procedures:
  x in R with a certified rational name -> sin(x), cos(x);
  x>=0 with a certified rational name -> exp(-x).      (R27.6)
The nonnegativity premise in the third line is semantic and proved for
the Gaussian arguments below; no comparison of an unknown real with
zero is a branch in the algorithm.

Explicit construction.
Choose rational M>=max(1,|x|) from one certified input enclosure.
For f in {sin,cos,exp(-.)}, use its actual power series from
ML89--ML92. The ordinary degree-K polynomial includes precisely powers
n<=K, with zero coefficients in the unused parity for sin or cos.
Its coefficients are rational and satisfy |c_n|<=1/n!. If K+2>=2*M,
the absolute omitted tail is bounded by
  sum_(n>=K+1) M^n/n! <= 2*M^(K+1)/(K+1)!.
Indeed successive majorant terms have ratio M/(n+1)<=1/2.
The geometric sum (ML66) gives the factor 2 and absolute convergence
identifies the sum with the actual function. This uses actual
Real.exp=NormedSpace.exp for the exponential, not a new formal series
standing for an unidentified function.

The rational bound tends effectively to zero: after K+2>=2*M,
each successor bound is at most half the previous one. Search by
rational comparisons for a K with the required strict tail budget.
Freeze that K, evaluate its finite polynomial by interval arithmetic,
and refine the input name until the polynomial interval width meets
the remaining budget. CP60 proves this last search terminates.
Enlarge the result by the symmetric rational tail bound. It contains
the actual f(x), and finite intersections give a nested name.
The semantic nonnegative argument premise for Gaussian exp(-x) is
retained, although this absolute-series construction also handles
arbitrary real x.

All operations needed in the formula (R27.3) now have certified names:
  pi; rational grid coordinates; explicit polarization coefficients;
  finite sums/products; sine/cosine; square roots of nonnegative sums;
  finite max, realized through max(x,y)=(x+y+|x-y|)/2.
Therefore named q gives a total certified name of ell_(N,m)(q).
For requested precision, obtain rational Qbar>=|q|, Kbar>=k_N and take
m so large that Kbar*Qbar/m meets the chosen error budget. Enlarge an
interval for ell_(N,m)(q) by [0,Kbar*Qbar/m]. This proves
  CertifiedName(q) => CertifiedName(ell_N(q)).         (R27.7)
It is a fixed-cutoff scalar access theorem, with no universal regularity
premise and no assertion of a finite polynomial formula for ell_N.

Prospective checkpoint split.
  CP67: second-derivative kernel trace; periodic distance adapter;
        continuous maximum/essential-supremum agreement; finite-grid error.
  CP68: Taylor enclosures and termination; finite matrix Frobenius norm;
        finite maximum names; actual spatial-gradient supremum names.
Sources: ML82, ML83, ML88 for grid calculus/maxima; ML66, ML89--ML92
for actual series and explicit tails; MT22--MT23 for coordinate derivatives,
Frobenius normalization and exact 2*pi multipliers. CP02/CP03/CP40/CP60/CP61
are inherited semantic predecessors. Source limitations: Section18.10.


14.U ROUND 28: FINITE GRADIENT QUADRATURE AND ACTUAL QUANTUM NAMES

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI55]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP69, CP70; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML47, ML52--ML57, ML59--ML65, ML84--ML87;
              inherited MT22, MT23 through CP67.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD31.
  APPLICATION: Finite Gaussian moments bound the spatial error and phase-space tail;
               explicit midpoint quadrature and the actual weighted orbit error
               give total gradient-expectation names.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new formal bridge bodies pending.

14.U.0. Exact input and finite moments.

Retain the canonical real Gaussian, one valid refined certificate W_r,
and the branch-free path of (R26.10)--(R26.14):
  psi(a+z)^2=c_tau*exp(-|z|^2/(2*tau)),
  c_tau=(2*pi*tau)^(-d/2), tau>0,
  P_s(z)=sum_(j=0)^n lambda_j(s)*X_j(z), 0<=s<=1,
  v_r(T*s)=P_s*psi,
  D_s=E[P_s(Z)^2]>=rho^2, rho=1-e_r>0,
  psi_hat_r(T*s)=P_s*psi/sqrt(D_s),
  Z distributed as N(0,tau*Id).                         (R28.1)
All X_j have real rational coefficients and finite support; X_0=1.
The degree bound K=max_j deg(X_j) is finite.
The actual approximate gradient expectation is
  Q_r^L(T*s)=E[ell_N(a+Z)*P_s(Z)^2]/D_s.              (R28.2)
Polynomial-Gaussian moment finiteness and ell_N(q)<=g_N|q| justify
absolute integrability and the actual multiplier expectation.

Define, for each node,
  W_j=E[(1+|a+Z|^2)*X_j(Z)^2],
  V_j=E[|Z|^2*(1+|a+Z|^2)*X_j(Z)^2].                (R28.3)
These are nonnegative finite Gaussian moment expressions. Moments
through degree 2*K+4 suffice. Let Wbar,Vbar be rational upper bounds
for sum_j W_j and sum_j V_j, obtained by the existing finite moment
interval evaluator; replacing the bounds by max(1,bound) is allowed.
Since lambda_j>=0 and sum_j lambda_j=1,
  P_s(z)^2<=(sum_j lambda_j(s)*X_j(z)^2)
             <=sum_j X_j(z)^2.
Consequently, uniformly for s in [0,1],
  E[(1+|a+Z|^2)*P_s(Z)^2]<=Wbar,
  E[|Z|^2*(1+|a+Z|^2)*P_s(Z)^2]<=Vbar.              (R28.4)
This is pointwise convexity of a real square, followed by integration;
it does not assume any coefficientwise sign condition on X_j.

14.U.1. Two uniform analytic truncation bounds.

Let Gbar>=g_N and Kbar>=k_N be rational certified majorants.
Using |q|<=(1+|q|^2)/2 and (R27.4),
  0<=Q_r^L(T*s)-E[ell_(N,m)(a+Z)*P_s(Z)^2]/D_s
      <=Kbar*Wbar/(2*m*rho^2).                         (R28.5)

For R>=1 rational and C_R=[-R,R]^d, the complement has |z|>=R,
except for irrelevant boundary conventions. Therefore
  0<=E[1_(Z notin C_R)*ell_(N,m)(a+Z)*P_s(Z)^2]/D_s
      <=Gbar*Vbar/(2*R^2*rho^2).                       (R28.6)
Indeed 1_(z notin C_R)<=|z|^2/R^2 and
ell_(N,m)(a+z)<=g_N*(1+|a+z|^2)/2. Multiplying the two pointwise
inequalities and applying (R28.4) proves the bound. This tail bound
uses only finite polynomial moments, not a tail-probability oracle.
Both bounds hold uniformly in the normalized time s and in the
chosen finite spatial grid size m.

14.U.2. Explicit phase-space midpoint error.

Write X_j(z)=sum_alpha x_(j,alpha) z^alpha and define rational
  A_alpha=sum_j |x_(j,alpha)|,
  B_0(R)=sum_alpha A_alpha*R^|alpha|,
  B_1(R)=sum_(|alpha|>=1) |alpha|*A_alpha*R^(|alpha|-1).
Then, throughout C_R and uniformly in s,
  |P_s(z)|<=B_0(R), |nabla_z P_s(z)|<=B_1(R).         (R28.7)
The derivative bound follows by summing the absolute values of all
coordinate derivatives; the Euclidean norm is at most that sum.

From a certified coarse parameter box obtain positive rational tau_-
with tau_->0 and tau>=tau_-, rational Abar>=|a|, and positive rational
Cbar_gauss>=c_tau. Such Cbar_gauss is a finite arithmetic/radical name
bound: for integral d, c_tau=(2*pi*tau)^(-d/2) is a product of powers
and at most one positive square root followed by positive reciprocal.
Define the following rational majorants:
  Qbar_R=Abar+d*R,
  L_R=Cbar_gauss*Gbar*
       [B_0(R)^2+Qbar_R*(2*B_0(R)*B_1(R)
                             +B_0(R)^2*d*R/tau_-)].  (R28.8)
For
  f_(m,s)(z)=ell_(N,m)(a+z)*P_s(z)^2
                   *c_tau*exp(-|z|^2/(2*tau)),
we have, on C_R,
  |f_(m,s)(z)-f_(m,s)(z')|<=L_R*|z-z'|.              (R28.9)

Derivation.
  ell_(N,m)(a+z)<=Gbar*Qbar_R;
  Lip_z ell_(N,m)(a+z)<=Gbar;
  |P_s|^2<=B_0^2;
  Lip(P_s^2)<=2*B_0*B_1;
  density<=Cbar_gauss;
  |nabla density|=|z|*density/tau
      <=d*R*Cbar_gauss/tau_-.
Apply |ABC-A'B'C'| <= |A-A'||B||C|
 + |A'||B-B'||C| + |A'||B'||C-C'| on the convex cube.
This proves exactly (R28.8)--(R28.9), without differentiating a maximum.

Partition each coordinate interval [-R,R] into J>=1 equal pieces.
For beta in {0,...,J-1}^d let
  z_beta=(-R+(2*beta_i+1)*R/J)_i,
  S_(m,R,J)(s)=(2*R/J)^d*sum_beta f_(m,s)(z_beta).
Every point in a cell is within sqrt(d)*R/J<=d*R/J of its midpoint.
Integrating (R28.9) over the disjoint cells gives
  |integral_(C_R) f_(m,s)(z)dz-S_(m,R,J)(s)|
      <=(2*R)^d*L_R*d*R/J.                            (R28.10)
Cell boundaries have zero Lebesgue measure; all integrands are continuous.
Dividing by D_s>=rho^2 proves the normalized quadrature error bound
  |Q_r^L(T*s)-S_(m,R,J)(s)/D_s|
   <=Kbar*Wbar/(2*m*rho^2)
      +Gbar*Vbar/(2*R^2*rho^2)
      +(2*R)^d*L_R*d*R/(J*rho^2).                    (R28.11)
This is an explicit finite upper bound; its constants may depend on
N,r,a,nu,T,W_r, but no continuum regularity bound enters them.

14.U.3. Total named evaluation of the non-polynomial expectation.

For every rational eta>0 choose integers R,m,J>=1 in this order:
  Gbar*Vbar/(2*R^2*rho^2)<=eta,
  Kbar*Wbar/(2*m*rho^2)<=eta,
  (2*R)^d*L_R*d*R/(J*rho^2)<=eta.                     (R28.12)
All comparisons are rational and the searches terminate. R determines
L_R; no dependence of L_R on m or J occurs. The sampling count J^d
is finite; no practical complexity bound is asserted.

For named actual theta and named s in [0,1], the quotient
  Z_(m,R,J)(s)=S_(m,R,J)(s)/D_s
has a total certified rational name. Its finite formula uses only:
  the input names; rational midpoint coordinates; the hat weights;
  finite polynomial evaluation and moment sums; the R27.6 elementary
  names; finite maxima and nonnegative square roots; D_s>=rho^2.
In particular, the Gaussian argument |z_beta|^2/(2*tau) is proved
nonnegative, so the semantic premise in R27.6 is discharged.

Evaluate Z_(m,R,J)(s) to a rational interval J_eta of width<=eta,
and enlarge by [-3*eta,3*eta]. By (R28.11)--(R28.12), this interval
contains Q_r^L(T*s) and has width<=7*eta. Choosing eta=2^(-p-3)
gives width<2^(-p). Therefore
  named theta + valid W_r + named s in [0,1]
     => CertifiedName(Q_r^L(T*s)).                    (R28.13)
The input box enclosures are still semantic premises of W_r; a Boolean
check alone is not identified with enclosure of the actual data.

14.U.4. Actual exact-orbit pointwise gradient names.

Retain the rational Xbar,Zbar of (R26.4), so
  ||U_N(t)psi||_[1]<=Xbar,
  ||psi_hat_r(t)-U_N(t)psi||_[1]<=Zbar*4^(-r).
The first inequality is the already established weighted forward
contraction. Since ell_N(q)<=(g_N/2)*(1+|q|^2), weighted Cauchy--Schwarz
and the difference-of-squares identity give
  |Q_r^L(t)-Q_U^L(t)|
    <=(Gbar/2)*(2*Xbar+Zbar)*Zbar*4^(-r)
    =Abar_L*4^(-r),                                   (R28.14)
where Abar_L is a known nonnegative rational. This proves a uniform
pointwise bound; no restriction T>=1 is required. It is distinct from
the previously recorded integrated bound delta_(N,r).

Fix one actual enclosing coarse Box0 before varying r, as in CP65.
All certificates below use this same Box0, so Xbar,Zbar,Abar_L are
independent of r. For requested name width 2^(-p), put eta=2^(-p-4).
Choose r by finite rational search so Abar_L*4^(-r)<=eta. Construct
W_r by the total refined certificate algorithm. Choose R,m,J by
(R28.12) and evaluate its quotient to width<=eta. Enlarge by
[-4*eta,4*eta]; (R28.11) and (R28.14) prove containment of Q_U^L(T*s).
The resulting width is <=9*eta<2^(-p). All subprocedures terminate.
Thus
  EffectiveEnclosure(theta), CertifiedName(s), 0<=s<=1
    => CertifiedName(<U_N(T*s)psi,L_N U_N(T*s)psi>).    (R28.15)
The same holds for named physical time t in [0,T] by s=t/T, T>0.
For the CP62 finite rational-trigonometric input class, the effective
parameter enclosure premise is itself derived, as in (R26.16).
All statements concern fixed finite N. They do not discharge a uniform
bound over all cutoffs, all smooth data or all finite horizons.

  CP70: total gradient-expectation name; actual weighted pointwise error;

14.V ROUND 29: EXACT-ORBIT TIME MODULI, EXTREMA AND INTEGRAL NAMES

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI56]
