  STATUS: B_TIER_DERIVED; formal proof bodies and external evidence pending.

14.V.1. A first-graph-norm temporal modulus.

Fix one actual finite cutoff N>=1, nu>0, T>0 and the canonical real
Gaussian psi. This round uses the actual finite-cutoff group U_N, not
an unknown continuum NSE solution. Write
  X=||psi||_[1], B1=||G psi||_[1], E=w_N^2, g=g_N,
  weight(q)=1+|q|^2, u(t)=U_N(t)psi.
The actual Schwartz graph computation R15.11 at r=1 gives
  B1=sqrt(S_1),
where S_1 is an explicit finite Gaussian moment expression of degree
at most 6. The same identity follows directly by expanding
weight*P_1^2; no hbar name is required, since G=-(i/hbar)H_N.

The weighted orbit C1 theorem already proved in R18.5 and the forward
weighted contraction of CP42 imply
  u'(t)=U_N(t)G psi in X_1, ||u'(t)||_[1]<=B1 (t>=0).
Integrating on [s,t], with s<=t, and using the Bochner norm inequality
gives
  ||u(t)-u(s)||_[1]<=B1*|t-s|,
  ||u(t)||_[1]<=X.                                      (R29.1)
At t=0 the derivative is the inherited right derivative. For a closed
interval the one-sided endpoint formulation suffices for this integral
identity. Interchanging s,t proves the stated absolute-value bound.

For any multiplier f with |f(q)|<=c*weight(q), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
  |<v,fv>-<w,fw>|
    <=c*(||v||_[1]+||w||_[1])*||v-w||_[1].
The actual multipliers satisfy
  0<=e3_N(q)<=E*weight(q),
  0<=ell_N(q)<=g*|q|<=g*weight(q)/2.
All orbit vectors have the actual maximal multiplier domains by the
earlier Gaussian propagation theorem. Therefore
  |Q_U^E(t)-Q_U^E(s)|<=2*E*X*B1*|t-s|,
  |Q_U^L(t)-Q_U^L(s)|<=g*X*B1*|t-s|.                    (R29.2)
These are pointwise bounds, including t=0, without G3. Positivity is
retained and both functions are continuous on every finite horizon.

14.V.2. Rational majorants from actual finite input.

Use the fixed CP65 coarse box with positive tau,T lower endpoints.
Its finite moment interval arithmetic encloses S_1 in [L1,U1], with
U1>=S_1>=0. Define Bbar1=max(1,U1); then B1<=Bbar1.
Retain rational Xbar>=X, Ebar>=E, gbar>=g and Tbar>=T from that box.
For normalized time s in [0,1], put
  f_E(s)=Q_U^E(T*s), f_L(s)=Q_U^L(T*s),
  L_E=2*Ebar*Xbar*Bbar1*Tbar,
  L_L=gbar*Xbar*Bbar1*Tbar.                             (R29.3)
Both L constants are nonnegative rationals. Equations R29.1--R29.2
prove |f_F(s)-f_F(s')|<=L_F*|s-s'| for F in {E,L}.
The complete parameters used here belong to the same actual finite
model as the point evaluators CP66 and CP70. No generic input box is
treated as actual without its enclosure premise.

14.V.3. A finite maximum enclosure.

Lemma. Let f:[0,1]->R be L-Lipschitz, L>=0 rational. For m>=1 let
J_j=[a_j,b_j] contain f(j/m), 0<=j<=m, with width(J_j)<=eta.
Then
  max_j a_j <= max_(s in [0,1]) f(s)
             <= max_j b_j+L/(2*m).                     (R29.4)
Proof. Continuity on [0,1] gives a maximum. Each grid value is at most
that maximum, proving the lower bound. For any s choose a nearest
integer j to m*s, with 0<=j<=m and |s-j/m|<=1/(2*m).
The Lipschitz inequality gives f(s)<=b_j+L/(2*m). Take the maximum.
For the width estimate, b_j<=a_j+eta for every j, whence
max b_j<=max a_j+eta. Thus R29.4 has width<=eta+L/(2*m).

Given p>=0 choose
  eta=2^(-p-2), m=1+ceil_Q_to_N(2^(p+2)*L).             (R29.5)
Then m>=1 and L/(2*m)<2^(-p-3) when L>0; for L=0 the
term vanishes. The interval in R29.4 has width<2^(-p).
All its operations are finite rational operations and finite calls to
the point-name procedure. Apply CP66 for f_E and CP70 for f_L.
Therefore both exact values
  M_N^E(a,T)=max_(0<=t<=T) Q_U^E(t),
  M_N^L(a,T)=max_(0<=t<=T) Q_U^L(t)                     (R29.6)
have total certified rational names on the represented input class.
No maximizer, root search or differentiability of ell_N is required.

14.V.4. A finite midpoint integral enclosure.

Under the same scalar hypotheses, let J_j=[a_j,b_j] contain
f((j+1/2)/m), 0<=j<m, each with width<=eta. Partition [0,1]
into m cells. On cell j the integrated point error is bounded by
  integral_cell L*|s-(j+1/2)/m| ds=L/(4*m^2).
Finite additivity and the triangle inequality give
  (sum_j a_j)/m-L/(4*m)
     <=integral_0^1 f(s)ds
     <=(sum_j b_j)/m+L/(4*m).                         (R29.7)
The width is at most eta+L/(2*m). The same R29.5 schedule yields
a total name of the normalized-time integral. With actual named T>0,
the guarded finite arithmetic name theorem gives a name for its product
with T. The change of variables t=T*s identifies that product exactly:
  I_N^F(a,T)=integral_0^T Q_U^F(t)dt,
  F in {E,L}.                                         (R29.8)
For an output width 2^(-p), request the product procedure at p; its
adaptive precision requests call the already total normalized-integral
procedure. No unjustified fixed precision is used for multiplying by
an arbitrarily large T.

The name algorithms may intersect their first p+1 intervals to enforce
nestedness. Every intersection contains the actual value and has width
no larger than the newest interval. Nonnegative exact quantities permit
intersection with [0,infinity), implemented by replacing the lower
endpoint by max(0,lower). These operations preserve totality.

14.V.5. Scope.

For each represented finite input, R29.6 and R29.8 are exact finite-
cutoff scalar access theorems. They apply in particular to the checked
finite rational-trigonometric data of CP62. Every cutoff calculation
terminates. No uniform runtime, polynomial complexity, cutoff bound,
universal NSE regularity or exact equality decision is asserted.

14.W ROUND 30: FINITE THRESHOLD WITNESSES AND EXACT RATIONAL BOUNDEDNESS

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI57]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP73, CP74; exact contracts in Section21.
  REFERENCES: ML59, ML72; inherited point-name and finite-grid endpoints;
              MT10 observable normalization through CP72.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD33.
  APPLICATION: Certified scalar names expose sound finite strict-threshold witnesses
               and an exact countable rational reformulation of cutoff boundedness.
  STATUS: B_TIER_DERIVED; no universal bound or decision procedure asserted.

14.W.1. Uniform input representation and interval contract.

Fix actual positive named nu,T and one smooth arbitrary-mean divergence-
free datum a with a total certified Fourier-name provider: on finite
input (N,coordinate,precision), it supplies the actual CP61 coordinate
name with the required containment and width guarantee. The finite
rational-trigonometric input class supplies this provider by exact
finite lookup and the derived arithmetic circuits.

For F in {energy_max,gradient_max,energy_integral,gradient_integral}
let x_N^F be respectively the R29.6/R29.8 nonnegative scalar, N>=1.
CP72 yields a total finite procedure producing
  J_(N,p)^F=[l_(N,p)^F,u_(N,p)^F], p>=0,
  0<=l_(N,p)^F<=x_N^F<=u_(N,p)^F,
  u_(N,p)^F-l_(N,p)^F<=2^(-p).                        (R30.1)
Use finite intersections as above to make the intervals nested.
These are actual-model enclosures, not arbitrary rational intervals.
The generic correctness premise includes correctness of the input
names. A finite source code alone does not establish its semantic
correctness. The CP62 finite rational input instance derives it.

14.W.2. Sound and complete finite witnesses for strict excess.

For a fixed rational B define a positive witness to be finite integers
N>=1,p>=0 together with a completed trace of the fixed R30.1 procedure,
whose checked rational output has
  l_(N,p)^F>B.                                         (R30.2)
A trace is checked against the exact prescribed finite arithmetic/name
procedures and actual certified input calls; a freely supplied endpoint
is not accepted merely because it exceeds B. Conditional on the named
input contract, verification and comparison of a supplied finite trace
terminate. For the explicit rational data instance, all calls expand
to the derived total elementary algorithms.

Soundness is immediate from l<=x: a passing witness implies x_N^F>B.
Conversely, if x_N^F>B, choose p with 2^(-p)<x_N^F-B. From R30.1,
  l_(N,p)^F>=x_N^F-2^(-p)>B.
The total evaluation has a finite completed trace. Hence
  exists finite strict-excess witness for B
    <=> exists N>=1: x_N^F>B.                          (R30.3)

An explicit search enumerates the finite pairs with N+p<=s for
s=1,2,... and evaluates each pair in a fixed order. Every evaluation
terminates and every pair occurs at a finite stage. It stops exactly
when it finds the rational comparison R30.2. Thus the strict-excess
predicate is semidecidable. If it is false, termination is not claimed.
In particular, equality x_N^F=B cannot be classified as strict excess.

For a fixed finite cutoff K>=1, the analogous finite strict-upper test
  max_(1<=N<=K) u_(N,p)^F<B                            (R30.4)
is sound for max_(N<=K)x_N^F<B and succeeds for some p iff that strict
inequality holds. The finite positive margin permits one common p.
This is a finite-cutoff statement; it contains no infinite-tail claim.

14.W.3. Exact rational reformulation of boundedness.

For each F and the same fixed represented datum and horizon,
  (exists real C>=0, forall N>=1: x_N^F<=C)
  <=> (exists B in N, forall N>=1,p>=0: u_(N,p)^F<=B)
  <=> (exists B in N, forall N>=1,p>=0: l_(N,p)^F<=B).
                                                           (R30.5)
Proof. If x_N<=C uniformly, R30.1 gives u_(N,p)<=x_N+1<=C+1.
Choose a natural B>=C+1 by the Archimedean property. The upper
condition implies the lower condition. If all lower endpoints are
at most B, then x_N<=l_(N,p)+2^(-p)<=B+2^(-p) for each p;
letting p tend to infinity gives x_N<=B for every N. Finally the
upper condition directly implies x_N<=B. This proves both equivalences
with all quantifiers in their displayed order.

Each fixed comparison u_(N,p)<=B or l_(N,p)<=B is decidable rational
arithmetic once its total interval calculation finishes. The remaining
existential B and universal N,p are unbounded quantifiers. Equation
R30.5 does not replace them by a finite witness, nor make their truth
decidable. Equation R30.3 only semidecides one prescribed strict-bound
violation. Neither formula proves that any common B exists.

14.W.4. Relation to the root and the unresolved analytic endpoint.

For energy_max and gradient_integral, R30.5 reformulates the corresponding
fixed-datum, fixed-horizon Gaussian cutoff bounds. The universal smooth-
data equivalences R3--R20 remain unchanged. Their a-quantifier is all
C-infinity_sigma data; the effective procedures in R30.1 require the
explicit total representation contract. No inference from the rational
subclass, its density, or all represented data to the universal smooth-
data bound is made. Generic mathematical all-data admitted families
remain governed by R26.17--R26.18.

The conclusion added by this round is exact access and strict-threshold
semidecision at represented data, together with R30.5. The unresolved
quantity is the common bound across all cutoffs; neither the finite
Hamiltonian construction nor the terminating per-cutoff solver supplies it.


15. QUANTUM INTERPRETATION AND NONCOERCIVITY

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI31]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP14, CP15; exact contracts in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML19--ML26.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD07--AD09.
  APPLICATION: These are operator foundations; the spectrum and noncoercivity proofs require the stated bridge domain and spectral-theorem endpoints.
  DETAILS: Section 18; adapter contracts: Section 19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; no bridge compiler or axiom-audit evidence.


15.1 hbar independence of the fluid transport.

  H_{N,min}^{hbar} = hbar H_{N,min}^{1}.

Positive scalar multiplication commutes with closure, so

  H_N^{hbar} = hbar H_N^1,
  U_N^{hbar}(t) = exp(-it H_N^1).

For smooth states,

  partial_t |psi|^2 + div_q(b_N |psi|^2)=0.                  (15.1)

Thus the fluid probability law has no additional hbar-dependent
fluctuation term. The construction gives exact canonical quantum
kinematics for enlarged variables and an exact classical fluid sector.

15.2 No global expectation-value closure.

For suitable states,

  d<Q_j>/dt = <b_{N,j}(Q)>.

For quadratic b_N,

  <b_N(Q)> != b_N(<Q>)

in general. Deterministic reconstruction uses (8.1) or (8.6), not
an unsupported closure of the first moments.

15.3 Spectrum of the derived Hamiltonian.

For N>=1 and nu>0, b_N is not identically zero. Choose a real normalized
chi in mathcal D_N and xi in R^{d_N} such that

  c = \int b_N(q).xi |chi(q)|^2 dq != 0.

Such a choice exists by continuity of b_N near a point at which it
is nonzero.

For real chi,

  <chi,H_N chi>
    = -(i hbar/2)\int div_q(b_N chi^2)dq
    = 0.

Let

  psi_m(q)=exp(i m xi.q)chi(q),  m in R.

Then

  <psi_m,H_N psi_m> = hbar m c.

The spectral theorem therefore implies

  inf spectrum(H_N) = -infinity,
  sup spectrum(H_N) = +infinity.                           (15.2)

The model is not a positive-energy ground-state theory.

15.4 Hamiltonian expectation does not bound the H^3 observable.

Let eta be real, normalized, smooth, and compactly supported. For
translations eta_R(q)=eta(q-Rv), with v!=0,

  ||eta_R||_2=1,
  <eta_R,H_N eta_R>=0,

while

  <eta_R,mathcal E_{3,N}eta_R>
    = R^2 e_{3,N}(v) + O(R) -> infinity.

Hence no finite universal function F can satisfy

  <psi,mathcal E_{3,N}psi>
    <= F(||psi||_2,<psi,H_N psi>)

for all such normalized states. This excludes this particular
coercivity inference; it does not exclude estimates involving other
observables or stronger spectral information.

15.5 Continuum boundary.

The theorem constructs the sequence

  {mathcal H_N, H_N, U_N, mathfrak A_N}_{N>=1}.

It does not construct a single continuum selfadjoint quantum generator
on a prescribed field-configuration Hilbert space. No infinite-dimensional
Lebesgue measure or unproved measure-equivalence assumption is used.

The full continuum NSE endpoint is accessed by (14.3), (L2), and (P20):
  FB(nu)<=>QREG(nu,hbar)<=>QLIP(nu,hbar)
        <=>QREG_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar)<=>QLIP_pkt^{rho,eta}(nu,hbar)
for every prescribed admissible family with bounded spectral radius.
The universal cutoff-uniform regularity upper bound remains unresolved.
Conditional continuum scalar-observable limits are proved in P22.

15.6 ROUND 10: FINITE-WIDTH LOCALIZATION AND CONJUGATE MOMENTUM

LEAN_SOURCE_INDEX [LI36]
  CHECKPOINTS: CP36; exact contract in Section 21.
  REFERENCES: ML14, ML47, ML50, ML51; MT02, MT21.
  FORMAL_ADAPTERS: AD06, AD07, AD16.
  APPLICATION: Compact-support integration by parts, L2 Cauchy--Schwarz,
    exact Fourier dimension, and the polynomial-width packet of Section14.B.
  DETAILS: Section18.5; adapter contracts: Section19.
  STATUS: SOURCE_VERIFIED; new bridge theorem bodies remain pending.

Fix d>=1, epsilon>0, a in R^d, hbar>0, and
  psi in C_c^infinity(R^d;C),
  ||psi||_2=1,
  supp psi subset closedBall(a,epsilon).
For P_j=-i*hbar*partial_j on the test domain, define
  K_P(psi)=sum_{j=1}^d ||P_j psi||_2^2
           =hbar^2 integral |nabla psi|^2 dq.
K_P is the conjugate-momentum quadratic norm.

The compactly supported vector field (q-a)|psi(q)|^2 satisfies
  integral div((q-a)|psi|^2)dq=0.
Expanding the divergence and using normalization gives
  0=d+2 Re integral sum_j (q_j-a_j) conjugate(psi) partial_j psi dq.
Consequently, by Cauchy--Schwarz on L2(R^d;C^d),
  d <=2 ||(q-a)psi||_2 ||nabla psi||_2
     <=2 epsilon ||nabla psi||_2.
Therefore
  K_P(psi)>=hbar^2*d^2/(4*epsilon^2).                    (R10.1)
Every integral is finite by smoothness and compact support.
The argument applies to complex profiles without a phase restriction.

For the normalized scaled packet
  Psi(q)=epsilon^(-d/2) eta((q-a)/epsilon),
the change of variables q=a+epsilon*z gives the exact identity
  K_P(Psi)=hbar^2*epsilon^(-2)*||nabla eta||_2^2.          (R10.2)

For the full real solenoidal ball cutoff, define
  K_N={k in Z^3 : 0<|k|<=N}.
Each pair {k,-k} has two real transverse polarizations and two real
sine/cosine coordinates per polarization; the constants contribute three.
Thus
  d_N=3+2*card(K_N).                                      (R10.3)
For N>=2 let m=floor(N/sqrt(3)). The integer cube |k_i|<=m lies in
the Euclidean ball |k|<=N. Since N/sqrt(3)>=1 and floor(x)>=x/2
for x>=1,
  d_N>=1+2*(2*m+1)^3
      >=1+16*m^3
      >=1+2*N^3/(3*sqrt(3))
      >=2*N^3/(3*sqrt(3)).                                (R10.4)

For the explicit Section14.B radius
  epsilon_N=1/[(N+1)*(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^(3/2)],
one has
  epsilon_N^(-2)=(N+1)^2*(1+4*pi^2*N^2)^3
               >=64*pi^6*N^8.
Combining (R10.1) and (R10.4), for N>=2,
  K_P(Psi_{N,a}^{pkt})
    >=(64*pi^6/27)*hbar^2*N^14.                          (R10.5)
The bound holds for every normalized smooth packet with the stated support,
including the explicit real radial profile of Section14.B. A smaller
actual support can only strengthen (R10.1).

For real-valued psi in the test domain,
  <psi,P_j psi>=-i*hbar/2 * integral partial_j(psi^2)dq=0,
and, using div b_N=-kappa_N,
  <psi,H_N psi>
    =-i*hbar/2 * integral div(b_N*psi^2)dq=0.              (R10.6)
On this invariant test domain define
  Var_psi(P_j)=||P_j psi-<psi,P_j psi>psi||_2^2.
For real packets (R10.6) gives K_P=sum_j Var_psi(P_j). This equality
requires no extra selfadjoint-domain identification for each P_j.

Conclusions (R10.1)--(R10.6) concern conjugate momentum, the explicitly
derived first-order Hamiltonian, and normalized compactly supported states.
They provide no computational complexity estimate or positive physical
Hamiltonian-energy interpretation. They do not obstruct the criterion
equivalences: neither QREG_pkt nor QLIP_pkt assumes a cutoff-uniform
conjugate-momentum bound. The root theorem retains fixed hbar>0.

DECLARATION: SingularClosure.GlobalSmoothNSE
SOURCE_LINE: 96
PINNED_URL: https://github.com/randogelist/Methlib/blob/09dfe94a1ef150e21d09df3013fbe09002ef139c/regularity-B-assembly/Singular-Axiomatic-closure/SingularClosure/Contracts.lean#L96
VERBATIM_SIGNATURE_OR_DEFINITION:
  structure GlobalSmoothNSE (ν : ℝ) (a : Field)
      (u : Velocity) (p : Pressure) : Prop where
    velocity_smooth :
      ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun z : ℝ × Vec => u z.1 z.2) forwardSpacetime
    pressure_smooth :
      ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun z : ℝ × Vec => p z.1 z.2) forwardSpacetime
    velocity_periodic : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → SpatialPeriodic (u t)
    pressure_periodic : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → SpatialPeriodic (p t)
    divergence_free : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ x : Vec, divergence (u t) x = 0
    equation : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ x : Vec,
      timeDerivative u t x + convection (u t) x + gradient (p t) x =
        ν • laplacian (u t) x
    initial : u 0 = a
    velocity_mean_zero : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → MeanZero (u t)
    pressure_mean_zero : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → PressureMeanZero (p t)

DECLARATION: SingularClosure.cutoffModes
SOURCE_LINE: 32
PINNED_URL: https://github.com/randogelist/Methlib/blob/09dfe94a1ef150e21d09df3013fbe09002ef139c/regularity-B-assembly/Singular-Axiomatic-closure/SingularClosure/Galerkin.lean#L32
VERBATIM_SIGNATURE_OR_DEFINITION:
  def cutoffModes (N : ℕ) : Finset Frequency :=
    let s : Finset ℤ := Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) (N : ℤ)
    (((s.product s).product s).image
      (fun q : (ℤ × ℤ) × ℤ => ![q.1.1, q.1.2, q.2])).filter
        (fun k => k ≠ 0 ∧ galerkinFreqSq k ≤ (N : ℤ) ^ 2)

      (((2 * Real.pi * (∑ i : Fin 3, (k i : ℝ) * x i) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)

DECLARATION: SingularClosure.coefficientLeray
SOURCE_LINE: 58
PINNED_URL: https://github.com/randogelist/Methlib/blob/09dfe94a1ef150e21d09df3013fbe09002ef139c/regularity-B-assembly/Singular-Axiomatic-closure/SingularClosure/Galerkin.lean#L58
VERBATIM_SIGNATURE_OR_DEFINITION:
  def coefficientLeray (k : Frequency) (v : Fin 3 → ℂ) : Fin 3 → ℂ :=
    if k = 0 then v else
      fun i => v i - (k i : ℂ) * (∑ j : Fin 3, (k j : ℂ) * v j) /
        (∑ j : Fin 3, (k j : ℂ) ^ 2)

DECLARATION: SingularClosure.coefficientTransport
SOURCE_LINE: 64
PINNED_URL: https://github.com/randogelist/Methlib/blob/09dfe94a1ef150e21d09df3013fbe09002ef139c/regularity-B-assembly/Singular-Axiomatic-closure/SingularClosure/Galerkin.lean#L64
VERBATIM_SIGNATURE_OR_DEFINITION:
  def coefficientTransport (N : ℕ) (c : FourierCoeff) (k : Frequency)
      (i : Fin 3) : ℂ :=
    ∑ p ∈ cutoffModes N,
      (∑ j : Fin 3,
        c p j * (((2 * Real.pi * ((k j - p j : ℤ) : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) *
        c (k - p) i

DECLARATION: SingularClosure.galerkinRhs
SOURCE_LINE: 72
PINNED_URL: https://github.com/randogelist/Methlib/blob/09dfe94a1ef150e21d09df3013fbe09002ef139c/regularity-B-assembly/Singular-Axiomatic-closure/SingularClosure/Galerkin.lean#L72
VERBATIM_SIGNATURE_OR_DEFINITION:
  def galerkinRhs (ν : ℝ) (N : ℕ) (c : FourierCoeff)
      (k : Frequency) (i : Fin 3) : ℂ :=
    -((ν * (2 * Real.pi) ^ 2 * (galerkinFreqSq k : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * c k i -
      coefficientLeray k (coefficientTransport N c k) i

DECLARATION: SingularClosure.GalerkinSolution
SOURCE_LINE: 83
PINNED_URL: https://github.com/randogelist/Methlib/blob/09dfe94a1ef150e21d09df3013fbe09002ef139c/regularity-B-assembly/Singular-Axiomatic-closure/SingularClosure/Galerkin.lean#L83
VERBATIM_SIGNATURE_OR_DEFINITION:
  structure GalerkinSolution (ν : ℝ) (a : Field) (N : ℕ) where
    coeff : ℝ → FourierCoeff
    coefficient_continuous : ∀ k : Frequency, ∀ i : Fin 3,
      ContinuousOn (fun t : ℝ => coeff t k i) (Ici 0)
    mode_support : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ k : Frequency,
      k ∉ cutoffModes N → ∀ i : Fin 3, coeff t k i = 0
    real_symmetry : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ k : Frequency, ∀ i : Fin 3,
      coeff t (-k) i = star (coeff t k i)
    solenoidal : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ k : Frequency,
      (∑ i : Fin 3, (k i : ℂ) * coeff t k i) = 0
    initial_integrable : ∀ k : Frequency, ∀ i : Fin 3,
      IntegrableOn (datumFourierIntegrand a k i) unitCube volume
    initial : ∀ k : Frequency, ∀ i : Fin 3,
      coeff 0 k i = if k ∈ cutoffModes N then datumFourierCoeff a k i else 0
    equation : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ k ∈ cutoffModes N, ∀ i : Fin 3,
      HasDerivWithinAt (fun s : ℝ => coeff s k i)
        (galerkinRhs ν N (coeff t) k i) (Ici 0) t

19. FORMAL ADAPTER CONTRACTS AND PROOF DEPENDENCIES

Common status:
  ROOT_MATHEMATICAL_DERIVATION = recorded in Sections 1--16.
  EXACT_SOURCE_API_ADAPTATION = prospective; source indexing alone does
    not prove type equivalence or discharge the listed interface contracts.
  LEAN_IMPLEMENTATION_FOR_THIS_BRIDGE = not supplied.
  MATCHING_EXTERNAL_THEOREM_AUDIT = absent.
  Each contract below requires a new exact theorem or an exact source
  endpoint plus proved type/hypothesis transport. No adapter is an axiom.

[AD01] Periodic quotient / periodic lift.
  Input: functions on UnitAddTorus (Fin 3) and unit-periodic lifts Vec->Vec.
  Required conclusions: equivalence of integration, differentiation,
    divergence, pressure gauge, smoothness on the closed time half-line,
    and Fourier coefficient conventions.
  Sources: ML01--ML05; MT01, MT02, MT07.
  Sections: 1, 2, 12.
  Scope: normalized volume on the unit torus; no change of spatial period.

[AD02] Real finite coordinates / constrained Fourier coefficients.
  Input: chosen real orthonormal solenoidal Fourier basis including means.
  Required conclusions:
    injective/surjective synthesis onto the real solenoidal finite space;
    for q=(m,z) and zero-mean Fourier coefficients c:
      |z|^2 = SingularClosure.coefficientEnergy N c,
      |q|^2 = |m|^2 + SingularClosure.coefficientEnergy N c
            = ||m + I_{N,0}(z)||_2^2;
    exact real-linear isometry and exact RHS conjugacy;
    preservation of all (1+lambda)^s quadratic forms.
  Sources: ML01--ML05; MT02--MT07, MT20.
  Sections: 2, 7.A, 8, 9.
  Scope: the default norm of the plain finite Pi type is not silently l2.
    Realification of the full complex ambient space must first restrict to
    spectral reality and solenoidality. Invariant-subspace structure is
    part of the theorem.

[AD03] Conserved mean and Galilean transformation.
  Required conclusions: Section 2.A chain rules, inverse, norm identity,
    fixed-nu mean-zero/arbitrary-mean predicate equivalences.
  Sources: MT01, MT02, MT09--MT11.
  Sections: 2.A, 12, 14.
  Mathematical status: proved in Round 1.
  Formal status: new adapter; a zero-mode-excluded trajectory cannot be
    used as an arbitrary-mean trajectory without this construction.

[AD04] Cutoff, Leray, and Sobolev normalization.
  Required conclusions: full ball = {0} union source nonzero ball;
    exact Laplacian eigenvalues; Fourier multiplier commutation;
    orthogonality, contraction, spectral tails and weighted norm identities.
  Sources: ML01--ML05; MT02, MT10, MT11.
  Sections: 1--2, 3.A, 8.3, 10.1, 13.1.
  Distinction: source adjacent-order tail N^-1 is not literally the
    arbitrary-gap sharp-weight formula (10.2).

[AD05] Complete smooth flow and determinant.
  Required conclusions: polynomial smoothness, finite-time bounds in both
    time directions, continuation, smooth initial-state dependence, group
    law, inverse diffeomorphism, variational equation, Liouville formula,
    constant diagonal Fourier kernel and div b=-nu Tr(A_N).
  Sources: ML06--ML10; MT03--MT06, MT08, MT09, MT20.
  Sections: 2--3.A.
  Mathematical status: Sections 3 and 3.A.
  Formal distinction: MT09 leaves negative-time values unconstrained.
    ML07 gives local joint continuity, not smooth global dependence.

[AD06] Half-density L2 representation.
  Required conclusions: representative-independent Jacobian-weighted
    pullback on L2, complex linearity, isometry, inverse, group law,
    strong continuity, invariance of the smooth compact-support subspace.
  Sources: ML11--ML18.
  Sections: 4--5.
  Scope: actual Lebesgue measure and actual J_N; no false
    measure-preservation premise for the dissipative flow.

[AD07] Explicit resolvents, graph closure and maximal generator domain.
  Required conclusions: dense minimal domain and integration-by-parts
    symmetry; closable graph; both vectorwise nonreal Laplace resolvents;
    finite-time graph identity; full-space right and left inverse laws;
    A*=A from the two conjugate ranges; equality of graph, adjoint and
    strong-derivative domains; unique strong evolution and actual core;
    resolvent adjoint/identity/holomorphy and quantitative core bounds.
  Sources: ML14, ML15, ML19--ML25, ML37--ML45.
  Sections: 4--6.
  Formal distinction: the range and graph arguments are explicit new
    theorem bodies. Generic Stone and deficiency criteria are not required
    inputs of the selected route. Integrate U(t)f vectorwise, not U(t) in
    operator norm. Only bounded graph projections commute with integrals.
  Exponential convention: encode the root by the explicit U(t) and the
    exact strong generator/domain relation. If a separate spectral exp
    is used, prove its strong-evolution characterization as in Section6.7.
  Section15 spectral diagnostics additionally use selfadjoint spectral
    calculus; no bounded operator is substituted for H_N.

[AD08] Unbounded observables and deterministic characters.
  Required conclusions: real measurable multiplication operator with
    maximal domain; selfadjointness; equality of conjugated domains;
    commutator identities on the invariant common domain; C0-character
    identification and point-evaluation transport.
  Sources: ML11--ML14; ML19--ML26 as operator foundations.
    ML31--ML36 supply the compactification/C0 inputs for CP12.
  Sections: 7--9, 14--15.
  Scope: point characters are not normalized L2 vectors; general state
    means do not satisfy the nonlinear classical closure equation.

[AD09] Coordinate and parameter covariance.
  Required conclusions: W_O and D_nu unitary, transformed drift identities,
    equality of closed generators and groups, transformed observable
    domains and packet profiles, viscosity scaling, hbar cancellation.
  Sources: ML11--ML16, ML24--ML26; MT02, MT03.
  Sections: 7.A, 15.1.
  Scope: fixed unit torus; time/amplitude scaling; no spatial rescaling.

[AD10] Quantitative localization and integrated observables.
  Required conclusions: beta_N bilinear bound, forward trajectory
    Lipschitz estimate, packet normalization and compact support, (P3)
    through (P5), fixed-N uniform-in-time limit, integrated limit.
  Sources: ML09--ML15; MT05, MT06.
  Sections: 8, 8.4, 14, 14.A.
  Scope: original Section8.4 constants depend on N; its epsilon limit
    precedes the cutoff supremum. Section8.5 supplies the additional
    reference-gradient estimate; prescribed-width criteria are AD15.

[AD11] Periodic Sobolev calculus.
  Required conclusions: scalar/vector product estimates, H3->W1,infinity,
    precise periodic Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation, integer tame
    commutator estimate, N-independent constants and projected energy law.
  Sources: ML29, ML30 as Euclidean inputs; MT10, MT11 for discrete norms.
  Sections: 10--13.
  Distinction: no unsupported import-level identification of Euclidean
    continuous-frequency Sobolev space with discrete periodic H^s.

[AD12] Continuum criterion in both directions.
  Required conclusions:
    G3 -> all spatial and time derivative bounds -> diagonal compactness
      through t=0 -> nonlinear PDE limit -> normalized pressure -> gluing;
    FB -> spectral residual estimate -> nonlinear stability bootstrap
      -> H3 convergence of every sufficiently large cutoff -> G3.
  Sources: ML04, ML05, ML08--ML10, ML27, ML28; MT10, MT11.
  Optional conditional source chain: MT13--MT18, with its hypotheses.
  Sections: 11--13.
  Scope: all smooth divergence-free data, arbitrary mean, every finite T;
    fixed-nu predicate and smoothness at t=0 are preserved.

[AD13] Exact quantum criterion equivalences.
  Required conclusions: FB<->G3<->LIP, G3<->QREG, LIP<->QLIP, with exact
    quantifiers, maximal observable domains, fixed-N localization order,
    and parameter/mean covariance.
  Sources: preceding adapters; ML09 for scalar differential inequalities.
  Sections: 14, 14.A, 14.B, 14.C.
  Additional conclusion: compose AD15 with the five-criterion theorem
    to obtain the seven-criterion theorem, preserving each definition.
  Scope: implication/biconditional theorem; no proof of the universal bound.

[AD14] Conditional Methlib interface.
  Required conclusions if this optional route is used:
    retain or derive AX6Statement with its literal all-data/all-time
    quantifiers; construct the exact strong-limit/positive-flow witnesses;
    transport Fefferman_B_0_adjust to the document's fixed-nu FB;
    preserve initial trace and mean adapter.
  Sources: MT01, MT12--MT19.
  Sections: 11--16.
  Scope: the present B-tier proof uses its direct G3 argument and does not
    assume AX6. Merely invoking MT19 does not formalize the converse,
    the quantum representation, QREG, QLIP, or arbitrary-mean transport.

[AD15] Prescribed normalized packet families and exact finite-width access.
  Required conclusions: reference-trajectory L2 estimate, H3 spectral
    upgrade, normalized explicit profiles, Born probability measure,
    fixed-N/T product integrability and Fubini, subaverage reference
    witness, the G3/QREG_pkt/QLIP_pkt cycle, full-ball bound, P21 packet
    error formulas and P22 conditional continuum-observable convergence.
  Sources: ML05, ML09, ML13, ML14, ML46--ML49, ML51; MT10, MT11.
  Sections: 8.5, 14.B, 14.C.
  Scope: prescribed rho_N>0 and normalized eta_N fixed while a,T vary;
    bounded theta_N=w_N*rho_N suffices for criterion equivalence;
    theta_N->0 is required for the packet error limit. G3 is an explicit
    premise of P21/P22, and not a premise of QLIP_pkt=>G3.
  Selection is derived from the probability average, never supplied as
    an unresolved witness or inferred from an exponential-moment bound.

[AD16] Compact localization and conjugate-momentum quadratic norm.
  Required conclusions: integration-by-parts identity, L2 Cauchy--Schwarz,
    K_P>=hbar^2*d^2/(4*epsilon^2), exact scaled norm, real cutoff dimension,
    cube inclusion/cardinality, N^14 lower bound and real-profile means.
  Sources: ML14, ML47, ML50, ML51; MT02, MT21.
  Section: 15.6; supporting theorem CP36, not a CP29 prerequisite.
  Scope: compactly supported smooth states; d_N retains constant modes;
    hbar>0 is fixed. K_P is a conjugate-momentum norm, not H_N energy.

[AD17] Finite-moment state families and exact regularity equivalence.
  Required conclusions: measurable normalized translated L2 states;
    actual fourth-moment integrability; maximal E3/L domains; fixed-N/T
    noncompact product integrability; first-moment selection of

  Sources: ML13,ML14,ML46--ML49; MT10,MT11.
  Sections: 14.D; CP37,CP38.
  Scope: profiles prescribed before a,T, D_2<infinity, fourth moments
    finite separately for every N. No H_N-domain hypothesis is imposed
    on a general measurable profile. G3 occurs only in its displayed
    implication or conditional error theorem.

[AD18] Gaussian/Weyl access and finite Fourier trace identities.
  Required conclusions: actual Gaussian normalization/moments in Euclidean
    volume; Schwartz polynomial differential calculus; exact H_N powers;

    via the explicit translation-resolvent construction; bounded Weyl

  Sources: ML02,ML05,ML13,ML14,ML20--ML24,ML37--ML45,ML49,ML50,

  Scope: exact finite-dimensional canonical states and coefficient drift;

[AD19] Weighted resolvent products and exact criterion transport.

[AD20] Finite Gaussian polynomial powers and graph data.

21. STRUCTURED INTERMEDIATE GOALS

21.0 Contract and source-selection conventions.

Checkpoint schema:
  ID; role; exact predecessor IDs; prospective declaration names;
  quantified input/output contracts; selected Mathlib and Methlib
  declarations; named subgoals; proof steps; formal gaps; acceptance.

Status separation:
  Sections 0--16: complete strengthened B-tier derivation; P21/P22 retain G3.
  CPxx contracts: exact targets for future formalization.
  MLxx/MTxx members: source-verified existing declarations.
  NSEQuantumBridge.* names: proposed new declarations, not existing
    source endpoints and not proved Lean theorems.
  A pending edge signature is not a proof of its body.
  No Lean or lake execution was performed for this revision.

Roles of source selections:
  DIRECT: an existing declaration supplies the stated subgoal after its
    explicit hypotheses are established; it need not prove the whole CP.
  TRANSPORT: the useful theorem has a different concrete type/convention;
    the recorded adapter must be proved.
  FOUNDATION: a relevant construction or general lemma used in a new proof.
  COMPARISON: source scope differs; the result is recorded for comparison
    and is not an input to the selected direct proof.
  NONE_NEW: a composition checkpoint uses already proved CP edges.
  NONE_DIRECT: no complete exact checkpoint theorem is asserted available.
  EXCLUDED: a tempting source declaration has an inapplicable hypothesis.

Global mathematical conventions:
  Hilbert_N=L2(R^{d_N},dq;C); H_N is the Hamiltonian operator.
  D_N is initially the dense C-infinity compact-support test subspace.
  Graph-core status is a conclusion of CP10, not an initial premise.
  Realify_N is the real-coordinate/Fourier isometry of CP03.
  R_N(y) retains its Section2.A meaning as a translation matrix.
  Source coefficientEnergy excludes k=0; the full energy adds |m|^2.
  Input derivative conventions at t=0 are fixed at CP01.
  All CP outputs retain their displayed hypotheses; an implication from
    G3 or FB does not prove either proposition independently.
  Comparison endpoints with AX6 or supplied witnesses are isolated.

Root relation:
  CP29 assembles the exact R1--R24 theorem and its original-root projection.
  CP15 and CP36 supply the Section9/15 diagnostics and are not root prerequisites.
  CP30 is a separate conditional AX6 application and is not a root premise.
  CP31 is the external evidence gate, not a mathematical lemma.

Prescribed-family conventions:
  theta_N=w_N*rho_N is the spectral support radius; d_N is dimension.
  The profile/radius family is fixed before datum a and finite time T.
  D<infinity is a design condition in the universal family implication;
    the canonical explicit family satisfies it with D=1/2.
  No state-localization limit occurs in QREG_pkt or QLIP_pkt.

Additional frozen conventions:
  General moment profiles require actual fourth-moment Integrable.
  omega_N is a scalar second-moment radius; D_N remains the actual test domain.
  weight_m(q)=(1+|q|^2)^m defines a state-space weight, not fluid H^m.
  Lap_q b_N=0 is coefficient-space harmonicity; Lap_x is distinct.
  CP39 core excludes supporting Gaussian consequence G13 (assigned CP36).
  The finite-product schedule retains the full horizon T index.

Further frozen conventions:
  R15.* labels refer to finite Gaussian graph data; R16.* to partitions;
  R17.* to nodal residuals; R18.* to normalized continuous core paths.
  Polynomial degree2r uses the actual radial NSE energy identity.
  Graph norms D_{H,2},D_{H,3} are distinct from the moment-radius D_2.
  The1/24 mesh-integrated coefficient belongs to the fixed-partition path.
  A finite tuple of smooth functions is not a finite-bit certificate.
  Admissible core-family existence is derived before quantified criteria.

Further finite-certificate conventions:
  R19.* labels denote Hermite completeness and graph tails;
  R20.* denotes finite least residuals and rational trial density;
  R21.* denotes exact interval residual checking;
  R22.* denotes finite accuracy certificates and admitted criteria.
  The real trial subspace is used for Q coefficients; complex extension
    uses Q+iQ. POLY and compact-support CORE are distinct witness classes.
  Actual fine-box containment is not inferred from coarse containment.
  Coarse n and epsilon stay fixed during fine-box refinement.
  Total EffectiveEnclosure is a premise of search, not of finite
    certificate existence and not of checker totality.

Further effective-access conventions:
  R23.* labels denote total certified arithmetic and actual-pi names;
  R24.* denotes explicit Fourier circuits and actual input enclosures;
  R25.* denotes rational matrix certificates and adaptive residual trials;
  R26.* denotes refined accuracy, exact energy names and refined criteria.
  A certified name is a total finite program with actual containment
    and width guarantees, not merely a mathematical interval sequence.
  theta^eff uses the explicit CP61 frame. Another frame requires
    effective transition-matrix names for an effectiveness theorem.
  Matrix kappa is the row-sup/L1 norm, with its exact source instance.
  Final residual checking uses the identical interval syntax and
    coefficient/support ordering used when each trial was accepted.
  RefinedAccuracyCheck_(N,0)=AccuracyCheck_N; r>0 generally changes n.
  Finite polynomial moment evaluation is asserted for E3_N;
    the integrated gradient statement retains its semantic scope.
  R27.* denotes actual spatial grids and total elementary names;
  R28.* denotes finite Gaussian tail/quadrature and exact gradient names;
  R29.* denotes exact temporal moduli, extrema and integral names;
  R30.* denotes represented-data strict thresholds and rational boundedness.
  The CP65/CP66 polynomial-only restriction is unchanged locally.
  CP67--CP70 supply a separate nonpolynomial gradient quadrature extension.
  A uniform total input provider is distinct from arbitrary smoothness.
  Strict-excess semidecision leaves equality and boundedness undecided.

CHECKPOINT [CP01]
TITLE: Periodic quotient / physical-lift dictionary
ROLE: CORE_INTERFACE
STATE: TARGET_SPECIFIED; FORMAL_PROOF_PENDING; no A-tier claim.

  NSEQuantumBridge.periodic_lift_integral_dictionary

INPUT_CONTRACT:
  01. T := UnitAddTorus (Fin 3), Vec := EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), pi:Vec->T the unit-period quotient
      map; volume on T has mass one.
  02. Physical lift of f:T->R^3 is f o pi. Unit-periodicity means invariance under every Z^3
      translation. Scalar pressure uses the same quotient.
  03. No mean-zero hypothesis is imposed on the dictionary itself; the mean-zero source predicates
      are specialized only after taking the mean.
OUTPUT_CONTRACT:
  01. For every quotient-integrable scalar/vector function f: integral_T f = integral_unitCube (f o
      pi). In particular, L2 norms and means agree.
  02. For every smooth periodic lift F there exists a unique quotient function f with F=f o pi;
      spatial derivatives, divergence, Laplacian, and periodic gradients commute with this
      identification.
  03. For every integrable f and k in Z^3, the quotient Fourier coefficient equals integral_unitCube
      exp(-2*pi*i*k.x)*(f o pi)(x) dx, matching star(fourierCharacter k).
  04. For smooth trajectories restricted to t>=0, construct compatible smooth extensions at t=0
      whenever an actual full time derivative is used by the source contract; restrictions preserve
      the PDE, initial trace, periodicity and pressure mean.
  05. Under zero velocity mean, the dictionary transports the literal fields of
      SingularClosure.SmoothSigmaZero and SingularClosure.GlobalSmoothNSE to their quotient-torus
      predicates. Arbitrary mean remains unrestricted in the general dictionary.

PROOF_STEPS:
  01. Prove r is complex linear and bounded: ||r(F)||<=2||F||; consequently chiTilde is continuous
      and complex linear.
  02. Compute r(FG)=r(F)r(G)+F(infty)r(G)+G(infty)r(F); multiplicativity of chi gives
      multiplicativity of chiTilde.
  03. Compute chiTilde(1)=1, hence chiTilde is a nonzero character of C(Xplus,Complex).
  04. Apply ML31 on compact Hausdorff Xplus to obtain unique p with chiTilde(F)=F(p).
  05. If p=infty then for every f, chi(f)=chiTilde(E(f))=E(f)(infty)=0, contradicting chi!=0.
      Therefore p is the image of x in X.
  06. For every f, chi(f)=chiTilde(E(f))=f(x). If two points define the same C0 character, extend to
      C(Xplus) using the same formula and apply the injective part of ML31.
  07. Construct evaluation on C0 as a continuous linear multiplicative functional using
      |f(x)|<=||f||. To prove it is nonzero, assume every f(x)=0. For every F in C(Xplus), apply
      this to r(F), obtaining F(x)=F(infty). Then the injectivity of ML31 gives coe(x)=infty, a
      contradiction. Thus no additional bump-function theorem is required for nonzeroness.
  08. Define alpha_t by ML34 applied to ML35(Phi_t). Establish star preservation, inverse alpha_-t
      and sup-norm isometry; compute chi_x(alpha_t f)=chi_{Phi_t(x)}(f) pointwise.

22.4 Formalization boundaries requiring explicit new proofs.

  B01 / CP01:
    quotient/lift integration and derivative transport, especially the
    source full derivative at t=0 versus a closed-half-line restriction.

  B02 / CP03:
    constrained realification with l2 energy; arbitrary-mean RHS contains
    -2*pi*i*(k dot m)*c(k). Bare mean-zero source dynamics is insufficient.

  B03 / CP05--CP07:
    two-sided continuation, smooth initial-state dependence, variational
    equations, determinant differentiation, exact Fourier divergence.

  B04 / CP09--CP11:
    Jacobian-weighted L2 composition, unbounded generator/domain,
    explicit vectorwise resolvents, graph limits, the direct two-range
    selfadjointness proof and maximal multiplier conjugacy.

  B05 / CP12:
    compact-character theorem transported through the explicit OnePoint
    extension/restriction. The exact source endpoints are ML31--ML36.

  B06 / CP18--CP21:
    periodic interpolation, N-independent tame estimates, one common
    smooth subsequence, compatibility of every limit derivative at t=0.

  B07 / CP23--CP25:
    cross-transport energy estimates, first-exit bootstrap, finite
    exceptional-cutoff maximum, variable-coefficient integrating factor.

  B08 / CP27--CP29:
    exact quantifier and domain composition; localization before sup_N;
    exact earlier-root projections and the explicit strengthened R5--R24.

  B09 / CP32--CP35:
    reference-only stability, normalized support probability, fixed-N/T
    Fubini, derived subaverage witness, finite-width quantifiers and
    conditional continuum-observable rates.

  B10 / CP36:
    compact-support derivative products, exact dimension/cardinality
    transport and the explicit conjugate-momentum lower bound.

  B11 / CP37--CP39:
    actual moment Integrable rather than totalized finiteness; full noncompact
    multiplier domains; score selection; exact Gaussian Euclidean volume;
    Schwartz-to-actual-H_N powers; weighted cutoff graph approximation.

  B12 / CP40:
    full constant Fourier kernel, distinct nonlinear trace contraction,
    coefficient-space Laplacian and initial-only centroid consistency.

  B13 / CP41--CP43:
    actual affine inverse domains, weighted complete state-space realization,

    identity and weighted telescoping. No bounded-H_N shortcut is permitted.
